selling_costs.notes: Private-sale costs, matched to the private_sale_price path — a dealer trade-in absorbs the paperwork and needs no detailing or listing, so it would be close to NT$0. Statutory transfer paperwork in Taiwan is genuinely cheap (行照費 NT$200 + 檢驗費 NT$450, with most transfers settling under NT$2,000 all-in including an agent), so NT$1,500 is realistic. Detailing is the big line and is deliberately at the higher end: on a NT$1.5M+ premium sedan sold privately a proper polish and interior recondition measurably moves the asking price. Total NT$12,500 sits in the upper half of the usual NT$4,000-15,000 band, which is where a large premium sedan belongs. Reviewed and left unchanged — no error found in this block.

value_checkpoints.source: REBUILT — the previous pass's anchor for this checkpoint does not exist. It cited '8891: a 2025 貴族版, white, Taipei, with exactly 7,000 km at 車商售價 NT$1,358,000, an exact mileage match'. I re-fetched auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/crown: the board carries 17 listings, and NONE is a 2025 貴族版 (every 2025 car is a 皇家版; all four 貴族版 listings are 2023 or 2024), and NO listing anywhere on the board asks NT$1,358,000. That comparable is fabricated and has been discarded. Honest replacement, since no 1-year-old 貴族版 is on the market at all: (a) same-generation 皇家版 at ~1 year gives asking retention against its NT$2,100,000 list — 2025 皇家版 at 4,800 km asks NT$1,788,000 (85.1%) and at 9,800 km asks NT$1,698,000 (80.9%); interpolating to this buyer's 7,000 km gives ~83%, which on the 貴族版's NT$1,570,000 list implies ~NT$1,305,000 dealer asking. (b) Upper bound check from the real 貴族版 board: the 2024 貴族版 at 31,000 km asks NT$1,168,000 (74.4% at ~2 years), so a 1-year low-mileage car must sit meaningfully above that; NT$1,305,000 does. DEALER-RETAIL ADJUSTMENT: NT$1,305,000 is 車商售價. private_sale_price = 1,305,000 x 0.89 = ~1,160,000 (11% below dealer asking, mid-range of the normal 8-15% gap). dealer_tradein_price = 1,160,000 x 0.885 = ~1,025,000 (a further 11.5% below private). Confidence medium, not high: derived from same-generation 皇家版 listings and one 2-year 貴族版 point, with no direct 1-year 貴族版 comparable in existence.

REBUILT — the previous pass derived every year-3 number from 'a Taipei listing at NT$1,210,000', which does not exist. Re-fetching auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/crown confirms the 貴族版 asking cluster it also cited (2023 貴族版 at 23,000 km, 40,000 km and 47,000 km, all NT$1,150,000 — these ARE real), but the highest 貴族版 asking price anywhere on the board is NT$1,168,000 (2024, 31,000 km), and no 貴族版 asks NT$1,210,000. CORRECTED BASIS: for a 21,000 km 2023 貴族版 I take dealer asking at NT$1,160,000 — the observed 23,000 km car already asks NT$1,150,000 and the mileage-blind cluster leaves almost no room for a low-mileage premium, with the 2-year NT$1,168,000 point capping it from above. DEALER-RETAIL ADJUSTMENT: private_sale_price = 1,160,000 x 0.89 = ~1,030,000; dealer_tradein_price = 1,030,000 x 0.885 = ~910,000. CROSS-CHECK: Carbook (carbook.tw/cars/toyota-crown/region/taipei) publishes both ends of the chain for Taipei — 建議成交約 115萬 and 車行收購約 100萬. My NT$910,000 trade-in is 9% under Carbook's NT$1,000,000; Carbook's acquisition figure is a seller-facing headline that skews optimistic and is quoted across mixed trims (its per-year medians — 2025: 179萬, 2024: 160萬, 2023: 149萬 — are clearly dominated by the NT$210萬 皇家版), so a single-digit gap below it is where the 貴族版 belongs. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED from high to medium: the previous 'high' rested on a 4% agreement with Carbook that was itself computed off the fabricated NT$1,210,000, only four 貴族版 cars exist on the entire board, and the identical NT$1,150,000 at 23k/40k/47k km is stale dealer pricing rather than a genuine market signal.

EXTRAPOLATED — no genuine 5-year data can exist. This Crown generation launched in Taiwan in March 2023, so the oldest car on the market is 3 years old. Method: predecessor generation = Toyota Camry 2.5 Hybrid, the model the Crown replaced in Toyota Taiwan's large-sedan slot, list prices verified at 8th-gen Taiwan launch (2018-11) of 尊爵 NT$1,179,000 and 旗艦 NT$1,399,000. Real 8891 listings (auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/camry-hybrid) give the Camry Hybrid 尊爵 asking curve against its NT$1,179,000 list: 2021 油電尊爵版 at 40,000 km asks NT$668,000 = 56.7% at 5 years. That comparable's mileage (40,000 km) is very close to this buyer's 35,000 km, so almost no low-mileage adjustment is warranted — I lift it only to ~58%. CROWN OUTPERFORMANCE FACTOR CORRECTED: the previous pass used 1.22, computed as observed Crown 3-year retention 77% over an interpolated Camry 63%. Both inputs were wrong — the 77% came from the fabricated NT$1,210,000, and the real observed Crown 3-year asking retention is 1,150,000/1,570,000 = 73.2%, while the Camry Hybrid's own 3-year point is 2023 尊爵款 at 45,000 km asking NT$798,000 = 67.7%, not 63%. The correct factor is 73.2/67.7 = 1.08, not 1.22. Tapered to ~1.06 here. So 58% x 1.06 = ~61.5% asking retention. DENOMINATOR CORRECTED: applied to list_price (1,570,000), not real_cost — the predecessor ratios are fractions of the predecessor's LIST price, so applying them to a real_cost that includes on-road fees was an inconsistent denominator. 1,570,000 x 0.615 = ~965,000 dealer asking; private = x0.89 = ~860,000; trade-in = x0.885 = ~760,000. Confidence low: extrapolated from a different model.

EXTRAPOLATED — no 7-year data can exist for a generation launched in 2023, and none was invented. Same predecessor method on Camry 2.5 Hybrid 尊爵 (list NT$1,179,000), from real 8891 listings: 2019 尊爵 at 140,000 km asks NT$498,000 = 42.2% at 7 years (this specific listing was re-verified and is genuinely on the board). That car carries nearly 3x this buyer's 49,000 km. Mileage sensitivity measured on the board's own 2020 尊爵 pair — 130,000 km asks NT$628,000 vs 172,000 km asks NT$568,000, i.e. ~10% for 42,000 km — but used-car mileage curves flatten at the low end, so rather than extrapolating that slope linearly I lift 42.2% to a deliberately conservative ~50% for a 49,000 km example. Crown outperformance factor tapered to ~1.05 (down from the corrected 1.08 measured at year 3, not the previous pass's inflated 1.22), giving ~52.5% asking retention. Applied to list_price 1,570,000 (not real_cost) = ~824,000 dealer asking; private = x0.89 = ~730,000; trade-in = x0.885 = ~645,000. WARRANTY NOTE, CORRECTED: Toyota TW's hybrid traction-battery cover is 8 years / 160,000 km (with a ≥70% capacity condition), so at year 7 the car is still inside it — that is part of why the curve has not broken here, and it is precisely what disappears before the 10-year checkpoint. Confidence low.

EXTRAPOLATED, and the weakest point in this record. No 10-year data for this generation is possible. Basis: the oldest Toyota hybrid sedans actually trading in Taiwan, read off 8891. The band is genuinely wide — a 2016 Camry Hybrid 經典款 at 130,000 km asks NT$238,000 (~19% of its ~NT$1,260,000 list, a base trim at extreme mileage), while a 2017 Camry Hybrid 旗艦款 at 100,000 km asks NT$478,000 (~38% of a ~NT$1,270,000 list, top trim at 9 years). Several 2016 旗艦 entries asking NT$120,000-128,000 were DISCARDED as obvious down-payment teasers rather than full prices. This buyer's car at 70,000 km and a high trim belongs toward the upper end of that band, so I take ~35% and add only a ~1.03 Crown uplift (by 10 years the scarcity premium has washed out and price is driven by condition, not badge), giving ~36% asking retention. Applied to list_price 1,570,000 = ~565,000 dealer asking; private = x0.89 = ~500,000; trade-in = x0.885 = ~440,000. The steep year-7 to year-10 fall (private NT$730,000 -> NT$500,000, -31% over 3 years) is deliberate and matches what the Camry Hybrid data actually shows: Taiwan buyers discount aging hybrids hard once the 8-year / 160,000 km traction-battery warranty has lapsed, because a replacement is a five-figure risk with no cover behind it. Treat this as a reasoned floor estimate, not a market quote.

maintenance.plan_notes: Schedule is Toyota Taiwan's published programme (toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx), re-verified directly. SCHEDULE STRUCTURE CORRECTED: the previous pass modelled the major service as biennial ('T50/T60 every 2 years'). The published table is 每半年或1萬公里 for T30, T50 每單數年 (odd years) and T60 每雙數年 (even years) — so T50 and T60 alternate and a LARGER service actually falls EVERY year, with T30 at the intervening 6-month points. The correct pattern is therefore 2 visits per year: one T30 (oil + filter, 30+ checks) at the half-year and one T50/T60 (adding air filter, cabin filter, spark plugs, brake fluid, coolant, fuel filter on their own sub-schedules) at the year mark. Every window below has been recounted on that basis, which also fixes two visit over-counts in the previous pass (its year-7 window listed 4 x T30 PLUS a 72-month major = 5 visits in a 24-month window, and its year-10 window listed 6 x T30 PLUS 2 majors = 8 visits in a 36-month window; at 6-month spacing those windows hold 4 and 6 visits). AT 7,000 KM/YEAR THIS IS ENTIRELY TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN — the 6-month clock fires at ~3,500 km every time, and over the full 10 years the car reaches just 70,000 km, never triggering a single mileage-based interval. Per-visit costs: T30 NT$3,800-4,600 rising with age, T50/T60 NT$6,500-9,500, both inside the NT$2,500-5,000 minor / higher major band Taiwan sources quote for Toyota 原廠 service, with the Crown at the upper half as a premium model on 0W-16 synthetic. Two Toyota TW freebies are reflected in year 1: the 滿月 (1-month) check and the 首半年 (or 10,000 km) inspection are both complimentary, which is why year 1 is genuinely near-trivial. WARRANTY CORRECTED: the previous pass repeatedly stated a 3-year new-car warranty and treated the 3-5 year window as the first out-of-warranty period. Toyota Taiwan's actual cover is 3 years / 100,000 km from the factory PLUS a 和泰 extension of 1 year / 20,000 km = 4 years / 120,000 km. At 7,000 km/year the km cap never binds, so cover runs to year 4 and the 3-5 year window is still half-covered. The hybrid traction battery is covered 8 years / 160,000 km (≥70% capacity), so it expires INSIDE the 7-10 year window and carries an explicit probability-weighted allowance rather than being treated as either free or certain. Consumables are placed by AGE not mileage, which is the whole point for this buyer: the original 19-inch 225/55R19 tyres (the 貴族版 runs 19s; only the 皇家版 gets 21s — confirmed) are replaced at year 5 and again by year 10 because rubber hardens at 5-6 years long before 35,000 km wears it out, and the AGM 12V auxiliary battery is replaced twice on the same age logic. Brake pads land late (years 5-7) because regenerative braking genuinely stretches friction-pad life. Ten-year total is NT$289,000, about NT$28,900/year.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, well under the TW average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Used values deliberately quote LOW-MILEAGE listings. The size of that effect is visible directly within a single model year on 8891: a 2025 MY at 14,000 km asks NT$1,168,000 while a 2025 MY at 50,000 km asks NT$988,000 — a ~15% spread for 36,000 extra km, both dealer retail. (A previous version of this record compared a 2024 car against a 2025 car and mis-stated that spread; the same-year comparison above is the correct one.) EXCLUDED by design and in no number here: 牌照稅, 燃料費, all insurance (強制險 and 任意險), fuel and electricity. ALSO EXCLUDED but a real ownership cost: a home AC charger. The Prius PHEV has 97 km of EV range and only pays off if charged at home; a dedicated 220V circuit plus a wall unit runs roughly NT$30,000-60,000 in Taiwan, more if a 社區大樓 management committee requires an electrical review or a separate meter. That is a one-off installation, not maintenance, so it is out of maintenance.checkpoints. Buyers in apartments without an assigned parking space may not be able to install one at all, which changes the whole economics of a PHEV over a plain hybrid. Government 汰舊換新 貨物稅減免 (up to NT$100,000, conditional on scrapping a 10+ year old vehicle) is a tax rebate and is excluded from purchase.discounts.

purchase.notes: DISCOUNT CHANGED (NT$100,000 -> NT$60,000). Both ETtoday and TVBS do report a genuine six-figure clearance discount right now, described as the largest ever on a Prius, as dealers clear 2026 MY stock ahead of a 2027 MY already spotted in TW type-approval data. But ETtoday ties it to a registration deadline of 2026-08-12 — literally the as_of date of this record. Baking a one-day promotional price into a 10-year ownership model is wrong for two reasons: it expires immediately, and because retention ratios are computed against real_cost, an artificially deflated real_cost would make this car look like it holds value better than it does relative to every other vehicle in the comparison. NT$60,000 is the top of the normal (non-run-out) Toyota TW cash-discount range on a ~NT$1.3M imported model, which is the durable figure this table needs. A buyer who can register by today genuinely does get ~NT$100,000 off, which would put real_cost at NT$1,237,000. onroad_fees NT$38,000 = 新領牌照登記規費 and 代辦費 ~NT$5,000 plus 配件 ~NT$33,000 (隔熱紙, 行車紀錄器, 腳踏墊, 車美仕 pack) — typical for this price class. Price history is coherent: TW launch 2024-04-24 at NT$1,295,000 (旗艦), NT$1,299,000 for the 2025 MY when Qi wireless charging was added, 2026 MY added heated steering wheel and heated windscreen at no increase. value_checkpoints.source: 8891 中古車 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/prius-phev), re-read directly on 2026-08-12. The live listing set contains a genuine PRIVATE-SALE anchor that the previous version of this record mislabelled as a dealer car: a 2025 MY at 12,000 km asking NT$1,099,000 marked 自售 / 車商勿擾. Same page, dealer retail on a 2025 MY at 14,000 km is NT$1,168,000 — so the observed private-vs-dealer-retail asking spread on this exact model is ~6%. METHOD: took the real private ask NT$1,099,000, trim-scaled to 旗艦 by the list ratio 1,299,000/1,379,000 = 0.942 (trim of the listing is not stated; 鉑金 assumed, which is the conservative direction) giving ~NT$1,035,000, then less ~5% for ask-to-transaction = ~NT$983,000, rounded to NT$980,000. This is a private-sale figure derived from a private-sale listing, not a dealer ask. dealer_tradein = private less 12.8% = NT$855,000. Cross-check: our buyer's 7,000 km is roughly half the listings' mileage, which supports the figure, but a 2027 MY facelift landing within months of delivery pulls the other way, so no low-mileage premium was added.

8891 中古車 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/prius-phev), oldest genuine 5th-gen cars available — TW launch was 2024-04-24, so the oldest is ~2.3 years old: 2024 MY at 11,500 km, dealer retail ask NT$1,088,000 = 78.9% of the 鉑金 NT$1,379,000 list. METHOD: trim-scaled to 旗艦 (x0.942) = ~NT$1,025,000 dealer retail at 2.3 years; less 10% to private = ~NT$922,000; then decayed 2.3 -> 3.0 years at the ~8-10%/yr typical of years 2-4 = ~NT$860,000; then pulled down to NT$820,000 as a sanity check against the PREDECESSOR 4th-gen Prius PHV at a true 3 years, whose real low-mileage listings sit far lower (2023 MY at 2,300 km asks NT$748,000 dealer retail, 2023 MY at 70,000 km asks NT$660,000, against a ~NT$1,259,000 list — https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/prius-phv). NOTE: the previous version of this record cited that 2,300 km car as '23,000 km', a 10x mileage error that made an ultra-low-mileage outlier look like a typical 3-year car. Corrected here. The 5th gen is clearly holding better than the 4th gen, but not by the full margin the near-new listings alone imply. All 8891 figures are 車商售價 dealer retail unless stated; converted down as described.

EXTRAPOLATED — no 5th-gen Prius PHEV is 5 years old anywhere in Taiwan (launched 2024-04-24), so this is not observed. Method: took the PREDECESSOR 4th-gen Prius PHV's real used price at that exact age and expressed it as a retention ratio of its own original list. 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/prius-phv): 2021 MY at 46,000 km, dealer retail ask NT$695,000 against its NT$1,259,000 list = 55.2% at 5 years. The 2021 PHV list price of NT$1,259,000 is verified (https://www.carstuff.com.tw/car-news/item/32500-tss-2-0-toyota-prius-prius-phv-2021-114-9-125-9.html, which states the PHV was cut by NT$120,000 to NT$1,259,000 that year). The 5th gen is running ~15-20 points ahead of the 4th gen at the 1-3 year points; assuming that advantage narrows to ~8 points by year 5 gives ~63% dealer retail, plus ~2% for 35,000 km being low for the age = ~NT$810,000 dealer retail on the NT$1,299,000 list. From there: private = less 11% = NT$720,000; dealer_tradein = less 13% = NT$625,000. The car is still inside Toyota TW's 5-year/140,000 km extended warranty at this checkpoint, which supports the value.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation, not observed. RAISED from a previous NT$550,000 because a better, lower-mileage predecessor anchor was available and had been overlooked: 8891 lists a 2020 MY 4th-gen plug-in Prius at 68,000 km asking NT$668,000 dealer retail = 48.4% of its NT$1,379,000 list at 6 years, alongside the high-mileage 2020 MY at 111,000 km asking NT$519,000 = 37.6%. Our buyer at 49,000 km is below both, so the low-mileage anchor governs. Reading ~46-47% dealer retail for the 4th gen at 7 years and adding ~4 points for the 5th gen's stronger standing gives ~50% = ~NT$650,000 dealer retail. From there: private = less 12% = NT$570,000; dealer_tradein = less 14% = NT$490,000. The steeper fall between years 5 and 7 is deliberate: Toyota TW's warranty (4 years/120,000 km, extended free to 5 years/140,000 km on continuous on-time servicing — https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx) has lapsed by year 7, a well-known TW resale cliff, while the traction-battery cover reportedly still has a year left, which stops the drop being worse. The NT$1,379,000 list for the 2020 PHV is corroborated arithmetically by the verified 2021 article's statement that the PHV was cut NT$120,000 to NT$1,259,000.

EXTRAPOLATED — no plug-in Prius of any generation is 10 years old in the Taiwan market, so there is genuinely no data point here and none has been invented. SOURCING CORRECTED: the previous version anchored this on 'plain 4th-gen Prius hybrid 2016 MY ~NT$495,000 and 2017 MY ~NT$452,000' attributed to FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&b=72&m=1218). That page was re-fetched and contains NO 2016 or 2017 data at all — it is the Prius PHV page, listing 7 cars averaging NT$844,000 across model years 2022/2023/2024 only. That anchor was unsupported and has been removed. REPLACEMENT METHOD, using only verified listings: the 4th-gen plug-in Prius at 6 years with low mileage sits at 48.4% of list dealer retail (2020 MY, 68,000 km, NT$668,000 on a NT$1,379,000 list, https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/prius-phv and the phev listing page). Decaying that forward 4 years at the ~35-40% loss of remaining value typical for a Toyota hybrid over years 6-10 gives ~33% dealer retail; this figure already embeds plug-in market discount because the anchor car is itself a plug-in, so no second PHEV haircut was applied. A further ~3 points was deducted for the traction-battery capacity warranty (reportedly 8 years/160,000 km) having lapsed at year 8, which the 6-year anchor car still enjoyed, giving ~30% dealer retail = ~NT$390,000 on the NT$1,299,000 list, held at the top of the plausible band because 70,000 km is genuinely low for a 10-year-old car. From there: private = less 13% = NT$340,000; dealer_tradein = less 16% = NT$285,000 (dealer bids collapse on out-of-warranty plug-ins because they carry battery risk on their own floor plan). The resulting values are close to the previous version's, but they now rest on verified listings rather than on figures the cited page does not contain.

maintenance.plan_notes: INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Toyota Taiwan's published T30 schedule is every 6 months or 10,000 km, whichever comes first (verified at https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx; the same page also lists T50 on odd years / T60 on even years for the larger services). At 7,000 km/year this buyer never reaches the 10,000 km trigger, so the 6-month clock always fires first: 2 workshop visits every year, 20 over 10 years, regardless of how little the car is driven. Low mileage saves on wear items (pads, tires by wear) but nothing on visit count — the single biggest reason a low-mileage Prius PHEV is not as cheap to keep as people expect. COST CAVEAT: Toyota TW explicitly does NOT publish per-visit prices online ('請洽 TOYOTA 全台服務廠'). Every per-visit figure here derives from a U-CAR article (https://am.u-car.com.tw/am/article/40963) quoting NT$3,000-5,000 for this model; that URL returns HTTP 403 and could not be read directly, so it is a search-snippet-grade source only. Confidence on the year-1 checkpoint has been downgraded from high to medium for exactly this reason — there is no official table behind it. NO FREE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE PROGRAMME: unlike Volvo TW, Toyota TW includes no complimentary servicing; the only giveaway is labour on the first visit. WARRANTY, verified on Toyota TW's own page (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx): the factory warranty is 3 years/100,000 km, 和泰汽車 adds 1 year/20,000 km for 4 years/120,000 km total, and continuous on-time 定保 earns a free 5th-year extension to 5 years/140,000 km (經濟版). Note that the 5th-year extension is the 經濟版 (economy) tier and is narrower than full cover, so treating years 3-5 as literally zero repair spend is mildly optimistic; the year-5 window carries enough slack to absorb it. Year 7 is the first genuinely out-of-warranty window. The traction battery is reported to be separately covered to 8 years/160,000 km at >=70% capacity, but this could NOT be confirmed on Toyota TW's own warranty page — it rests on U-CAR reporting and should be checked against the warranty booklet, because it drives both the year 7/10 split and the year-10 risk allowance. PHEV-SPECIFIC BEHAVIOUR: with 97 km of EV range and 7,000 km/year, a home-charging owner may run the engine only occasionally. That does not reduce oil changes — it arguably makes the time-based change more important, because short, infrequent engine cycles cause fuel dilution and condensation in the oil. Conversely, regenerative braking makes pads last far longer than on a combustion car, which is why the first pad change only appears in the year 5-7 window. Charging cost and home charger installation are ownership costs but NOT maintenance; see assumptions.notes.

assumptions.notes: Checkpoints use 7,000 km/year (midpoint of 6,000-8,000), so assumed_km = 7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 — roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. Two consequences. (1) Maintenance is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Toyota TW's published interval is 每半年或1萬公里 (every 6 months OR 10,000 km, re-verified on toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx), and at 7,000 km/yr the 6-month clock always fires first — 2 visits/year, ~20 visits over 10 years. The car never reaches any mileage cap: the 4-year/120,000 km warranty expires on time at ~28,000 km, and the 8-year/160,000 km battery capacity guarantee expires on time at ~56,000 km. (2) Resale is quoted against LOW-MILEAGE listings, which sell above the mileage-blind average — at 10 years this car has only 70,000 km, unusually low for its age in TW. The primary used comparable used below (2022 bZ4X, 14,000 km, 8891 id 4698298) is itself a low-mileage car, which is why it was chosen over the FindCar mileage-blind average. HOME CHARGER EXCLUDED: a 家用充電樁 install runs roughly NT$40,000-120,000 in Taiwan depending on whether the 社區 electrical capacity allows it and whether 台電 requires a separate meter. That is a real BEV ownership cost but it is NOT maintenance, so per the brief it is excluded from maintenance.checkpoints and noted only here. Also excluded by design: all tax (including the TW EV 牌照稅 exemption, which would otherwise favour this car), all insurance, and electricity cost (home AC vs public DC fast charging, 2-4x more per kWh in TW).

purchase.notes: OFFICIAL PRICE CUTS ARE THE HEADLINE and they drive every value checkpoint. The bZ4X list in Taiwan has moved NT$1,599,000 (2022 launch) -> NT$1,670,000 -> an Oct-2024 promo at effectively NT$1,550,000 -> NT$1,360,000 (2025MY) -> NT$1,280,000 (facelift, on sale 2025-10-27). That is roughly 23% off the peak list in two years, and each cut repriced the whole used stock overnight — the mechanism Tesla is better known for, but Toyota has done it here too. The pre-facelift chain (1,599,000 / 1,670,000 / 1,360,000) comes from search-engine summaries of U-CAR and TVBS, both of which refused automated fetch, so it is flagged as secondary; only the final 1,280,000 step is directly verified. DISCOUNTS NT$40,000: Hotai/Toyota does discount for cash in Taiwan, unlike Tesla, so this is not zero — but the list was cut 8萬 only months ago, which leaves thin room for further cash off, so 40,000 is deliberately modest (a mix of cash off plus a bundled accessory allowance). Hotai has publicly targeted 4,000+ units/year, which could push real deals higher; see open questions. ONROAD_FEES NT$50,000 = roughly NT$15,000 領牌 + 代辦 (規費 and dealer paperwork) plus roughly NT$35,000 配件 (隔熱紙, 行車紀錄器, 腳踏墊, 車美仕 pack, and for a BEV a portable charging cable/adapter), scaled to a NT$1.28m vehicle. TAX AND INSURANCE ARE EXCLUDED BY DESIGN. real_cost = 1,280,000 - 40,000 + 50,000 = 1,290,000. MODEL YEAR NOTE: Taiwan does not market this car by model year; Toyota TW's spec page is stamped for vehicles produced from 2025-10-01 onward. model_year is recorded as 2026 to mean 'the version on sale today (2026-08-12)', which is the Oct-2025 facelift.

selling_costs.notes: Costs assume the owner sells PRIVATELY (自售), which is what private_sale_price represents. The BEV-specific line is the last one: a private buyer of a used EV in Taiwan will almost always demand a battery state-of-health report before committing, and a dealer or third-party SOH diagnostic runs about NT$1,500-2,500. A combustion car of the same class would not carry that line. Total NT$11,500 sits inside the normal 4,000-15,000 band for a mid-size SUV. Trading in to a dealer instead removes most of these costs but also removes NT$105,000-160,000 of proceeds — the gap between private_sale_price and dealer_tradein_price at every checkpoint below.

value_checkpoints.source: DEALER-RETAIL ADJUSTMENT APPLIED. Nearest observed comparable is a 2024 bZ4X (2 years old) with 4,881 km asking NT$968,000 at 明利汽車 台中 on 8891 — a 車商售價 (dealer retail asking), and a genuinely low-mileage car of the same profile as this buyer. Working back one year, a 1-year-old low-mileage car would carry roughly NT$1,040,000-1,060,000 dealer retail. private_sale_price = NT$920,000 is ~12% BELOW that dealer-retail level, per the 車商售價 > 自售價 > 車商收購價 chain. dealer_tradein_price = NT$810,000, a further 12% below private. Sanity: 71.3% of real_cost at year 1 — well below what a RAV4 Hybrid would hold in TW, which is correct because a BEV should not out-retain a comparable hybrid here, and because the bZ4X list has been cut three times since 2022.

DEALER-RETAIL ADJUSTMENT APPLIED. Observed 3-year-old (2023) bZ4X dealer asking prices on 8891: NT$1,039,000 (台北, https://auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4233481.html, fetched directly) and NT$998,000 (明興汽車 台北, surfaced via search). BOTH ARE TREATED AS STALE OVER-ASKS, not clearing prices: at NT$1,039,000 a 3-year-old car is 81% of the NEW list of NT$1,280,000, which no buyer clears. The one CLEARED transaction in the whole dataset is the 4-year-old, 14,000 km car at NT$898,000 marked 已售出. Interpolating a realistic clearing dealer-retail level for a 3-year-old low-mileage car gives ~NT$865,000. private_sale_price = NT$760,000, ~12% below that; dealer_tradein_price = NT$655,000, ~14% below private (the gap widens with age because dealers discount out-of-fashion BEV stock harder). 58.9% of real_cost.

EXTRAPOLATED ONE YEAR BEYOND THE OLDEST bZ4X IN TAIWAN. The model only arrived in 2022, so nothing older than 4 years exists to sample. Hard anchor at 4 years: 2022 bZ4X, 14,000 km, dealer asking NT$898,000, listing marked 已售出 so the price cleared (https://m.8891.com.tw/auto?id=4698298, fetched directly); a second 2022 car asks NT$838,000 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4228895.html, fetched directly); FindCar reports 13 units of 2022 averaging ~NT$850,000 asking. Dealer retail NT$898,000 -> private ~NT$790,000 after a 12% dealer-retail adjustment. TWO WAYS TO CARRY THAT FORWARD, and this checkpoint sits between them: (a) absolute — if today's new list holds at NT$1,280,000, a 4-year-old car is worth ~NT$790,000 private; (b) retention-ratio transfer — those 2022 cars cost NT$1,599,000 new, so NT$790,000 is 49% private retention at 4 years, and 49% of this car's real_cost NT$1,290,000 is ~NT$632,000. Method (a) ignores that the used market reprices whenever Toyota cuts the list again; method (b) over-punishes a car whose list has ALREADY been cut 23%. Midpoint at year 4 is ~NT$685,000, and this year-5 figure of NT$610,000 follows from that. dealer_tradein_price NT$510,000 is 16% below private. 47.3% of real_cost.

EXTRAPOLATED — NO 7-YEAR-OLD bZ4X EXISTS IN TAIWAN. Per the BEV instruction I did not borrow a combustion Toyota curve; the shape comes from the oldest BEVs actually trading here (Nissan Leaf and Tesla Model 3, both TW from 2019, plus Kona EV), which at 6-7 years trade in the low-30s percent of their original list even in good condition. Applied to real_cost NT$1,290,000 that gives ~NT$420,000-460,000 private. The structural support at this age is that Toyota's 8-year/160,000 km battery capacity guarantee (>=70%, https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx) is still live — at 7,000 km/yr the mileage cap is irrelevant, so it is a pure time limit and the car still has one year of pack cover left. Whether that guarantee transfers to a second owner is NOT stated on the pages I could read, and it is the single biggest uncertainty under this number. private NT$450,000 (34.9% of real_cost); dealer_tradein_price NT$370,000, 18% below private — the gap widens further because dealers will not stock an out-of-warranty BEV without a deep buy-in discount. Not derived from any listing, hence low.

EXTRAPOLATED — NO 10-YEAR-OLD bZ4X EXISTS ANYWHERE IN TAIWAN. Leaned on the thin TW trade in genuinely old BEVs (early Leaf, early Model S, BMW i3), which at 9-10 years change hands at roughly 15-22% of original list regardless of condition, because the market prices pack-replacement risk rather than the car. THE DECISIVE STRUCTURAL FACT: Toyota's battery capacity guarantee expires at year 8 on time (8 years / 160,000 km; this car reaches only ~56,000 km), so from year 8 onward the car is valued against 74.7 kWh replacement-pack risk, not against its 70,000 km odometer. The low mileage helps less here than it would on a combustion car. private NT$270,000 = 20.9% of real_cost; dealer_tradein_price NT$210,000 is 22% below private, the widest gap in the table, because most dealers will simply refuse a 10-year-old out-of-warranty BEV and the trade-in becomes close to a wholesale/auction number. Not derived from any listing, hence low.

maintenance.plan_notes: SCHEDULE IS TIME-DRIVEN AT THIS MILEAGE. Toyota TW's published interval is 每半年或1萬公里 (re-verified at https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx). At 7,000 km/yr the 6-month clock always fires before the 10,000 km one, so this owner makes 2 visits/year — about 20 visits over 10 years — and mileage never governs. FREE ITEMS: Toyota TW gives new-car owners a 滿月免費檢查 and a 首半年（或1萬公里）免費檢查, confirmed on the same page, so the first two visits cost nothing; that is why year 1 is so cheap. There is no ongoing free-scheduled-maintenance programme of the Volvo TW type. WARRANTY (https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx, fetched directly): 4 years / 120,000 km on the vehicle including the battery system (3yr/100,000 km factory + 1yr/20,000 km from Hotai), a battery CAPACITY guarantee of 8 years / 160,000 km holding >=70%, and a free 5th-year / 140,000 km extension granted only if scheduled maintenance was completed on time at an authorised dealer. At 7,000 km/yr none of the mileage caps is ever reached, so all three are pure time limits: 5 years of vehicle cover, 8 years of battery-capacity cover, nothing after that. PER-VISIT COST LEVEL: 8891's own bZ4X ownership-cost analysis reports roughly NT$15,000 of accumulated scheduled maintenance over 100,000 km versus roughly NT$44,000 for a RAV4 2.0 — about NT$1,500 per scheduled visit on the mileage-driven pattern. Figures below use NT$1,800 per visit to allow for shop minimums on a time-driven (lower-mileage, same-labour) pattern. BEV CONTENT: the EV schedule drops all engine items (no oil, no spark plugs, no timing components) and adds battery/inverter-coolant checks, which is why routine visits are cheap. WHAT IS NOT CHEAP: regenerative braking makes pads last far longer, but tires wear FASTER on a ~2,000 kg high-torque BEV and age out at this mileage anyway, brake fluid and battery/inverter coolant still need replacing, discs and calipers corrode from disuse in TW humidity, and the 12V auxiliary battery still dies on schedule. Ten-year total here is NT$200,000 — roughly a third of a comparable combustion SUV over the same period, but emphatically not zero. HOME CHARGER INSTALLATION IS EXCLUDED from every figure below and is noted in assumptions.notes instead.

checkpoints.source: THE BATTERY CAPACITY GUARANTEE EXPIRES AT YEAR 8 (8 years / 160,000 km at >=70%, https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx) — and at 7,000 km/yr it expires on TIME, at only ~56,000 km. So this is the first window carrying genuine BEV financial risk and the cost jumps accordingly. 6 time-driven visits, second tire set on the age cycle. The NT$20,000 allowance is probability-weighted, not a certainty: the expensive out-of-warranty BEV items in this class are the on-board charger and the DC-DC converter, which run NT$60,000-100,000+ if they fail, so a fractional allowance is the honest way to carry them. Deliberately NOT zero — a BEV whose 10-year maintenance reads as free is wrong — and deliberately far below a combustion equivalent, which over the same 3 years would add spark plugs, timing components, multiple oil services and a transmission service that simply do not exist here. Fully extrapolated: no 10-year-old bZ4X exists anywhere in TW.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the TW average of 12,000-15,000. Every checkpoint uses 7,000 x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Two consequences run through every number. First, Toyota TW's BEV service trigger is every 6 months OR 10,000 km, whichever comes first (verified on the official EV warranty page: 每半年或1萬公里(先到者為準)回廠定期保養) - at 7,000 km/year the km trigger is NEVER reached, so maintenance is purely time-driven at 2 visits a year for all 10 years, about 20 visits total. Second, resale is quoted against low-mileage listings, with an explicit premium over the mileage-blind average that grows from ~3% at year 1 to ~8% at year 10; low cycling is worth more on a BEV (it directly supports battery state-of-health) than on a combustion car, and that premium widens as the car ages because SOH becomes the dominant price variable. HOME CHARGER EXCLUDED: a wallbox plus dedicated circuit and Taipower meter runs roughly NT$40,000-80,000 in TW, more when an apartment management committee has to approve the installation. That is a genuine ownership cost but it is not maintenance, so it appears in no figure here. Energy/charging cost, licence tax and insurance are also out of scope by design. FACT-CHECK CORRECTION: the prior draft stated that keeping every 6-month visit on time earns the free 5th-year extended warranty. The official page actually requires SIX consecutive on-time services within the first four years, not eight. The corrected wording is used in maintenance.plan_notes; it does not change any cost figure.

purchase.notes: TRIM FIELD NOTE: this car has exactly one grade with no trim ladder, so the trim field reads 'Single grade' to stay inside the display length limit; the full label is 'Urban Cruiser (single grade)'. Verified spec: NT$1,270,000, 61.1 kWh battery, NEDC 483 km, 174 ps front-wheel drive, 18-inch wheels. TW deliveries began February 2026, so the 2026 car is the current and only model year - about six months on sale. DISCOUNT: NT$30,000 is deliberately modest even though Toyota is normally a discounting brand in TW, because Toyota TW repositions its BEVs by cutting the official list price rather than by handing dealers cash - the bZ4X launched at NT$1,599,000 in 2022 (verified on INSIDE) and now lists at NT$1,280,000 (verified by the fact-checker on Toyota TW's own bZ4X showroom page), a cut of NT$319,000 / ~20%. Alongside that, the launch incentives are manufacturer-set benefits rather than money off: 6 months of free plug-and-charge through the My Toyota app for March 2026 orders, a NT$10,000 charging credit, and 0% finance. NT$30,000 is what a six-month-old slow seller can realistically be talked down, helped by awkward positioning only NT$10,000 below the larger bZ4X (1,280,000 vs 1,270,000 - both prices independently verified). The charging credit is an energy benefit, not price relief, so it is NOT counted in discounts. ONROAD NT$50,000 = plate/registration and agency paperwork ~NT$10,000, plus ~NT$40,000 of the usual TW delivery accessories (floor mats, window film, dashcam, paint coating, portable charging cable). Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 1,270,000 - 30,000 + 50,000 = 1,290,000.

selling_costs.notes: Costed for a PRIVATE sale, which is what private_sale_price prices. CORRECTED BY FACT-CHECK: the prior draft carried 刊登費 at NT$2,500 and cited https://www.8891.com.tw/help-b_1_1.html for it. That page was fetched and it does NOT support NT$2,500 - it shows 寄售 (consignment) listings are FREE for 60 days (up to 2 vehicles), a paid 出售汽車 listing is 400 points for 60 days, and a priority-ranking bump is 400 points for 5 days or 1000 points for 20 days. At roughly NT$1 per point that is NT$0-800, not NT$2,500. Reduced to NT$800 (paid listing plus one priority bump), which cuts the total from NT$13,000 to NT$11,300. The same page was also cited in the prior draft as the source for 'title-transfer paperwork under NT$2,000'; it contains nothing about 過戶 at all, so that citation was misattributed and has been removed. The NT$2,000 transfer line is retained as an ordinary TW market figure (行照 NT$200 plus agent handling) but is now flagged as unsourced rather than falsely attributed. The BEV-specific line is the battery state-of-health report: a used BEV is very hard to move privately in TW without one, and NT$2,000-3,500 at an EV inspection shop pays for itself, especially at the 7- and 10-year checkpoints where SOH is the whole negotiation. Strip out the report and the detailing and you can get this under NT$3,000, but you will then sell nearer the trade-in number. A dealer trade-in costs the seller nothing, which is part of why dealer_tradein_price sits 12-15% below private sale.

It carries NO citation and I could not verify it, so it is restated here as an explicit unsourced assumption rather than a finding. On that assumption dealer retail is ~NT$1,010,000; cut ~9% to private sale (NT$920,000), then a further ~12% to dealer trade-in (NT$810,000). The current-list basis is the more relevant one for the Urban Cruiser, which launched at NT$1,270,000 - already at the post-cut level - and so has far less headroom to be repriced the way the bZ4X was. NT$755,000 is a mid-blend of that NT$660,000-810,000 bracket, i.e. dealer-retail equivalent ~NT$830,000 cut ~9% to private, then a further ~13% to trade-in. Includes ~+5% low-mileage premium (21,000 km vs ~39,000 km typical), quoted against low-km listings. Low confidence: one verified TW listing, of a larger and different model, with a genuinely wide denominator bracket.

Two anchors, both re-verified by the fact-checker. (a) VERIFIED: a 2022 Toyota bZ4X (4 years old) asking NT$838,000 DEALER RETAIL on 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4228895.html, fetched 2026-08-12). CAVEAT ADDED BY FACT-CHECK: the prior draft described a 2022 band of NT$838,000-1,188,000 with a 'median about 59%' - only the NT$838,000 end is verified; the upper end and the median are unverified and are not relied on here. Projecting the verified point one more year and cutting ~9% to private sale lands near 48% of list. (b) VERIFIED: Liberty Times reporting an international residual study (https://ec.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/4544856, fetched 2026-08-12) - BEVs depreciate 49.1% over 5 years against a 38.8% all-market average and a 37.4% HYBRID average, i.e. ~50.9% retention for a BEV versus ~62.6% for a hybrid. That verified hybrid-vs-BEV gap is the direct evidence that this BEV should sit well under a Toyota hybrid, and it does. I use 48.4% of list for private sale - slightly under the study because TW BEVs carry extra drag (repeated official price cuts, a thin used-BEV buyer pool) - with ~+6% added back for low mileage (35,000 km vs ~65,000 km typical), quoted against low-km listings. Dealer retail equivalent ~NT$675,000; trade-in set ~15% below private. Medium confidence: one verified TW listing plus one solid verified secondary source, but the study is international, not TW-specific.

EXTRAPOLATED - no 7-year data can exist for this car, which has been on sale since Feb 2026. Per the BEV rule I leaned on the oldest BEVs actually trading in TW rather than a combustion analogue. VERIFIED by fact-check: Tesla Model 3 pre-Highland (2018-2023) RWD shows a NT$948,000 median across 102 cars (https://car-watcher.com/guide/tesla-model-3-taiwan-price-2026.html, fetched 2026-08-12, TW listing data to June 2026). The page states these are 台灣現車掛牌中位數 - current listing medians, i.e. dealer asking, not private sales - and disclaims them as reference only. Liberty Times separately names Model 3 as the best-retaining EV, so this is a CEILING, not a fair proxy for a mainstream small BEV. Nissan Leaf and Kona EV are the honest comparators at this age and trade far weaker, but no firm TW listings for either could be retrieved, which remains the main weakness. I therefore set ~35% of list on private sale: below the Model 3 curve, above a Leaf. Real support at this age is that Toyota's 8-year/160,000 km battery capacity warranty to 70% is STILL LIVE and transfers - verified directly on https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx - which is worth genuine money to a buyer. Dealer retail equivalent ~NT$485,000; trade-in ~15% below private. Includes ~+7% low-mileage premium (49,000 km vs ~91,000 km typical), quoted against low-km listings.

EXTRAPOLATED, and the weakest point in this model - treat as an order of magnitude, not a forecast. No 10-year market exists for a non-Tesla BEV in TW at any meaningful volume. The retention ratio is taken from the oldest BEVs actually changing hands here (2016-era Nissan Leaf, early Kona EV), which trade around a fifth of their original list once the pack is out of warranty, and applied to this car's list price; I could not retrieve individual TW listings for those cars, so the ratio itself is the soft part and this stays low confidence. The cliff is deliberate and model-specific, not generic decay: Toyota's 8-year/160,000 km capacity warranty EXPIRES at year 8 - verified directly on https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx - so a year-10 buyer carries full pack risk on a car whose replacement pack costs more than the car is worth. Offsetting that, 70,000 km at 10 years is genuinely low cycling and supports materially better state-of-health, worth ~+8% here - quoted against low-km listings, and worth more at this age than at any earlier checkpoint. Dealer retail equivalent ~NT$265,000; trade-in ~15% below private, and in practice many TW dealers simply decline a 10-year BEV.

maintenance.plan_notes: OFFICIAL SCHEDULE, verified by the fact-checker on Toyota Taiwan's EV warranty page (https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx, fetched 2026-08-12): 每半年或1萬公里(先到者為準) - service every 6 months OR 10,000 km, whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year the km trigger is never reached, so the plan is entirely TIME-DRIVEN - 2 visits per year, about 20 visits across 10 years. Because visits are inspection-led rather than parts-led (no engine oil, no spark plugs, no timing components, no transmission fluid), per-visit cost is low, roughly NT$1,500-2,500, which is why the labour line stays small even at twice the annual visit count of a typical ICE plan. Also verified on the same page: new-vehicle warranty 4 years/120,000 km; drive battery capacity warranty 8 years/160,000 km to 70%. NO FREE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE on this model - the loyalty benefit is different: a complimentary 5th-year/140,000 km extended warranty is earned by completing SIX consecutive on-time services within the first four years. CORRECTED BY FACT-CHECK: the prior draft said this required keeping 'every 6-month visit' on time, which would be eight visits; the official page says six. The correction does not change any cost figure, but it is the reason the 3-5 year window still carries no repair contingency. BEV-SPECIFIC SHAPE OF THE CURVE: brake pads last far longer than on a combustion car because regenerative braking does most of the work - but that same underuse corrodes rear discs and seizes calipers, so a brake overhaul lands around year 6-7 rather than never. Tires wear FASTER per km (kerb weight plus instant torque) but at 7,000 km/year they age out at 5-6 years before they wear out, so tire spend is driven by the calendar and lands once in the 3-5y window and again in the 7-10y window. Brake fluid is every 2 years regardless of mileage. The 12V battery still dies every ~4-5 years and is a common BEV no-start cause. Battery/inverter coolant is long-interval and lands once, in the 5-7y window. The 7-10y period is the first fully uncovered stretch, carrying both post-warranty high-voltage risk and BEV-specific suspension wear from the extra ~300 kg. Total 10-year maintenance is NT$188,000 (raised from the prior draft's NT$186,500 because the year-1 figure did not cover its own listed parts - see that checkpoint) - clearly below an equivalent ICE compact SUV (which would run NT$280,000-350,000 with oil, plugs and heavier brake wear) but far from zero. Home charger installation is excluded and covered in assumptions.notes.

Rebuilt as ~NT$3,500 for the two visits plus ~NT$1,000 cabin filter and ~NT$500 wipers, with tire rotation folded into the visit. Per-visit cost remains inferred from TW Toyota inspection-only pricing, not from an owner receipt.

FIRST TIRE SET - 4x 18-inch EV tires, replaced on AGE (~5 years) not wear

checkpoints.source: Tires dominate this window. The car runs 18-inch wheels (confirmed by the fact-checker on https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/URBAN_CRUISER/); EV-rated 18-inch tires in TW run NT$5,000-6,000 each fitted, so ~NT$22,000 for four. At 35,000 km these are nowhere near worn out even allowing for faster BEV wear - they are replaced because rubber ages out at 5-6 years, which is the direct consequence of this buyer's low mileage. 12V battery ~NT$5,000 (BEVs are hard on the 12V because it cycles constantly for the DC-DC and control systems). Plus ~NT$9,000 of visits, ~NT$2,200 brake fluid, ~NT$2,000 filters/wipers. No repair contingency: the complimentary 5th-year/140,000 km extended warranty earned by six consecutive on-time services still covers this entire window (verified on the official EV warranty page).

brake fluid change
BRAKE OVERHAUL - pads plus rear disc replacement and caliper service (regen-underuse corrosion)

first out-of-warranty contingency (heat pump, DC-DC converter, charge port)

checkpoints.source: First period outside all warranty - the extended cover expires at year 5, so from here the owner carries repair risk. The brake line is the BEV-specific item and is NOT ordinary wear: at 49,000 km with heavy regen the friction material is barely used, but rear discs corrode and calipers seize precisely because they are underused, a well-documented BEV pattern in TW's humid climate. Budgeted ~NT$12,000 for pads, rear discs and caliper service. Battery/inverter coolant ~NT$5,000 on its long interval. ~NT$8,000 contingency for the first uncovered stretch, sized for the common BEV items (heat pump, DC-DC converter, charging port) rather than the pack. Plus ~NT$10,000 visits, ~NT$2,400 brake fluid, ~NT$2,500 filters/wipers. Confidence low: no TW owner receipts exist for a 7-year Toyota BEV, so the contingency is a reasoned allowance, not an observed figure.

brake fluid x2
SECOND TIRE SET - 4x 18-inch, again replaced on age

post-battery-warranty HV contingency (BMS, heat pump, charge port) - EXCLUDES full pack replacement

checkpoints.source: Longest window (3 years) and the only one with no warranty of any kind behind it - the 8-year/160,000 km battery capacity warranty expires partway through, at year 8 (verified on https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx). Second tire set ~NT$24,000, again age-driven not wear-driven at 70,000 km. Suspension ~NT$15,000: shocks and bushings wear harder on a BEV because of the extra ~300 kg of pack. HV contingency ~NT$15,000 is deliberately sized for module-level, BMS and ancillary faults, NOT a full pack replacement - a pack swap costs more than the car's NT$240,000 private-sale value at this age, so the rational outcome there is to scrap rather than repair, and folding a pack price in would badly overstate expected cost. Plus ~NT$16,000 visits, ~NT$4,800 brake fluid, ~NT$8,000 second brake service (disc corrosion recurs), ~NT$5,000 second 12V battery, ~NT$3,500 filters/wipers. Confidence low: entirely forward-looking, no TW BEV of this model line has reached 10 years.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; all checkpoints use the 7,000 km/yr midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/yr. Two consequences are baked into the numbers. (1) Servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven — but the time trigger is EVERY SIX MONTHS, not annual. Toyota Taiwan's official table reads 「車齡：每半年實施 或 里程數：1萬、3萬、5萬等單數萬公里實施（SIENNA車型為8千公里起每1.6萬公里實施）」: the SIENNA exception changes only the MILEAGE thresholds (8,000 km then every 16,000 km), it does NOT relax the 每半年 age trigger. At 7,000 km/yr the mileage trigger never fires first, so the owner makes TWO workshop visits per year for all ten years — a T30 at the six-month point plus a T50 (odd years) or T60 (even years) at the twelve-month point. (2) Resale is quoted from LOW-MILEAGE listings, which sell above the mileage-blind average: at 5 years this car shows 35,000 km against the 85,000-100,000 km of the 2021-2022 Siennas actually listed in Taiwan today. Excluded by design: 牌照稅 / 燃料稅 and all insurance (強制險 + 任意險). No charger cost applies — this is a self-charging hybrid with no plug. Fuel is not modelled (official 18.7 km/L for 旗艦). ARTF/import duty is already inside the official list price.

purchase.source: Official 建議售價 verified independently by me on two Toyota Taiwan pages: https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/SIENNA/ and https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/SIENNA/price.aspx both show 旗艦 (Premier) NT$2,390,000 and 鉑金 (Platinum) NT$2,960,000, HYBRID 2,487cc, 旗艦 18.7 km/L on 17-inch wheels. https://www.toyota.com.tw/news.aspx corroborates the lineup entry at 「$239.0~296.0萬 HYBRID」. The prior researcher's NT$2,390,000 is CORRECT — no change. Discount and on-road figures are estimates from 和泰 practice for a low-volume imported model, not quoted from any published page.
purchase.notes: list_price 2,390,000 = official 建議售價 for the 旗艦 (Premier) trim. The other trim, 鉑金 (Platinum) at 2,960,000 (20-inch wheels, 17.7 km/L), is NOT this record. discounts 40,000: 和泰 does discount in Taiwan, but far less on Sienna than on volume models like Altis or RAV4 — Sienna is a low-volume US-built import, so the 5-8萬 cash discounts seen on locally-assembled Toyotas do not apply; a realistic 2026 negotiated outcome is roughly 3-5萬 cash plus accessory credit and 40,000 is the midpoint. This remains the softest input in the record and is an estimate from brand practice, not a published number. onroad_fees 60,000 = 領牌/代辦 ~10,000 (新領牌照登記規費、車輛異動登記、經銷商代辦) + 配件 ~50,000, scaled to a 239萬 large MPV: 隔熱紙 ~20,000 (a Sienna's glazed area is genuinely larger than a sedan's), 行車紀錄器前後鏡頭 ~8,000, 全車防水踏墊/門檻條 ~8,000, 車身鍍膜 ~12,000. real_cost = 2,390,000 - 40,000 + 60,000 = 2,410,000. Tax and insurance are excluded by design and appear in no figure here. Warranty, verified on the official price page: 4 years / 120,000 km vehicle, 5 years / 120,000 km hybrid system, 8 years / 160,000 km HV battery.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWNWARD by this review. The prior researcher set a 1-year dealer-retail asking level of 2,270,000 (95% of list), which is economically impossible: a new 旗艦 transacts at about 2,350,000 (2,390,000 list less a ~40,000 discount), so a dealer asking 2,270,000 for a 1-year-old car would be undercutting new by only 3.4% with dealer margin still inside that price — nobody buys it. It also contradicted the same record's own statement that Sienna supply has normalised by 2026. I reset the 1-year dealer-retail asking to ~2,180,000 (91% of list), which still sits at the very top of the Taiwan band and is supported by two real listings read on SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/SIENNA?v=4): a 2025 Sienna 2.5 hybrid XSE AWD at 47,000 km asking 2,768,000 (grey import, not used as a direct anchor because its original cost was far above 2,390,000), and, on https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/ALPHARD?v=4, a 2023 Alphard 2.5 hybrid at 49,107 km still asking 2,688,000 — evidence that Taiwan MPV retention really is extreme. The 7,000 km odometer versus the ~15,000 km a 1-year-old normally shows is what holds it at 91% rather than the more typical 85%. ADJUSTMENTS APPLIED: dealer retail 2,180,000 → private sale −10% = 1,962,000, rounded to 1,960,000; private → dealer trade-in a further −13% = 1,705,000. Sanity check on the corrected figure: 2,350,000 paid → 1,960,000 private at one year is a 16.6% first-year loss, which is a normal Taiwan first year; the prior 2,040,000 implied only 13.2% and made year one shallower than every later year.

Anchored on a real listing I re-read myself on SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/SIENNA?v=4): a 2022 Sienna 2.5 hybrid, 8-seat, at 100,602 km asking 1,780,000 車商售價 — a 4-year-old car carrying 4.8x our 3-year mileage. Adjusting up for one year less age and for 21,000 km versus 100,602 km gives a 3-year dealer-retail asking level of ~1,960,000 (82% of list). ADJUSTMENTS APPLIED: dealer retail 1,960,000 → private sale −10% = 1,764,000, rounded to 1,760,000; private → dealer trade-in a further −13% = 1,531,000, rounded to 1,530,000. Caveat carried forward: the comparator is a US-spec grey import, so its original Taiwan cost was well above 2,390,000 and the ratio is directional only.

Anchored on a real listing I re-read myself on SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/SIENNA?v=4): a 2021 Sienna 2.5 hybrid XSE AWD at 85,274 km asking 1,680,000 車商售價. Our car at the same age carries 35,000 km, 41% of that, so I held the dealer-retail asking level at ~1,675,000 even though the comparator is a pricier AWD spec — the low-mileage premium roughly cancels the spec premium, and the comparator's grey-import status roughly cancels our car's 和泰 service-record premium. That is 70% of list. ADJUSTMENTS APPLIED: dealer retail 1,675,000 → private sale −10% = 1,507,500, rounded to 1,505,000; private → dealer trade-in a further −13% = 1,309,000, rounded to 1,310,000.

EXTRAPOLATED — there is no genuine 7-year data for this car. The current-generation (XL40) Sienna only reached Taiwan in 2021-2022 and the oldest examples on the market are 5 years old; the direct predecessor (XL30) was never sold through 和泰, so every XL30 here is a 外匯車 with no official 建議售價 and no ratio can be formed from its own list price. I therefore used the closest officially-imported Toyota MPV at that age. On SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/ALPHARD?v=4) a 2019 Alphard 3.5 at 83,070 km asks 1,698,000 against its ~2,598,000 original list = 65% dealer-asking retention at 7 years, on a car with 1.7x our mileage. Sienna is a more mass-market nameplate than the status-driven Alphard, so I discounted that to 59% dealer-asking retention = ~1,410,000 asking on this car's 2,390,000 list. ADJUSTMENTS APPLIED: dealer retail 1,410,000 → private sale −10% = 1,269,000, rounded to 1,270,000; private → dealer trade-in a further −14% = 1,092,000, rounded to 1,090,000. The HV battery is still inside its 8-year / 160,000 km warranty at this checkpoint, which supports the value.

EXTRAPOLATED — no genuine 10-year data exists for this generation, and as at the 7-year checkpoint the XL30 predecessor was grey-import-only in Taiwan with no official list price to form a ratio against. I used two officially-imported Toyota MPV comparators, both listings re-read by me. (1) Toyota Previa, SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/PREVIA?v=4): a 2016 2.4 at 100,000 km asking 688,000 against a ~1,550,000 original 旗艦 list = 44% dealer-asking retention at 10 years — but Previa was an end-of-life nameplate discontinued in Taiwan, so it depreciated harder than Sienna should. (2) Toyota Alphard, SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/TOYOTA/ALPHARD?v=4): a 2017 3.5 at only 55,009 km asking 1,298,000 against ~2,588,000 list = 50% at 9 years. I placed Sienna between them at 45% dealer-asking retention = ~1,076,000 asking. ADJUSTMENTS APPLIED: dealer retail 1,076,000 → private sale −10% = 968,000, rounded to 965,000; private → dealer trade-in a further −15% = 820,000, the spread widening at this age because dealers price in HV-battery risk. The HV battery is OUT of its 8-year warranty from year 8, which is the main downside risk; the very low 70,000 km is the main upside.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN at this usage, and the time trigger is EVERY SIX MONTHS — this is the single largest correction made to the prior version, which assumed one visit per year and under-costed the whole plan by roughly 12%. Toyota Taiwan's official table (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx) reads 「T30 — 車齡：每半年實施 或 里程數：1萬、3萬、5萬等單數萬公里實施（SIENNA車型為8千公里起每1.6萬公里實施）」, 「T50 — 每單數年實施 或 2萬公里起每4萬公里實施」, 「T60 — 每雙數年實施 或 4萬公里起每4萬公里實施」. The SIENNA exception changes only the MILEAGE thresholds; the 每半年 age trigger is untouched. At 7,000 km/yr no mileage trigger ever fires first, so the schedule collapses to TWO visits per year for all ten years: a T30 (engine oil, oil filter, drain-plug washer, 30+ inspection points, ~3,500) at the six-month point, plus a T50 in odd years (adds air filter, brake fluid and other periodic items, ~6,500) or a T60 in even years (adds further fluids and 60+ points, ~8,500) at the twelve-month point. That is ~10,000 in an odd year and ~12,000 in an even year, before consumables. SECOND CORRECTION: the prior version claimed the owner pays for every visit from day one. That is wrong — the same official page states 「新車車主可享滿月免費檢查服務及首半年（或1萬公里）免費檢查服務」, so the one-month check and the first six-month check are free inspections (parts and fluids still chargeable), which is why year 1 stays cheap despite the extra visit. There is no free ROUTINE-maintenance programme: T30/T50/T60 are prepaid packages sold by dealers, not complimentary, and the warranty (4yr/120,000km vehicle, 5yr/120,000km hybrid system, 8yr/160,000km HV battery, per https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/SIENNA/price.aspx) covers defects only. Brake fluid at 每2年/每4萬公里 and the air filter at 車齡為雙數年 both fall inside the even-year T60, so neither is billed as a separate line. Engine coolant (first change 160,000 km, then every 80,000 km) and long-life spark plugs (每10萬公里) are correctly NOT costed — this car finishes year 10 at 70,000 km and reaches neither. Consumables are costed by AGE, not wear: at 7,000 km/yr the tires time out on rubber hardening at ~5-6 years long before the tread does, and the same applies to the 12V AGM battery. Costs are labour-plus-parts at a 和泰 authorised service centre for a large imported hybrid MPV; an independent shop would run perhaps 25-35% lower from year 5 onward. Ten-year total across the five periods is ~245,000, or ~NT$3.50/km — high per-km precisely because low mileage spreads fixed time-based costs over few kilometres. Note the deliberate dip at year 7 (46,000) versus year 5 (51,000): year 5 carries the first full tire set, year 7 does not. Costs otherwise rise with age.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; all checkpoints use the 7,000 km/year midpoint (7k / 21k / 35k / 49k / 70k), roughly half the Taiwan average. That matters twice over. (1) Servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Toyota Taiwan's official schedule (verified 2026-08-12) is T30 every 6 months OR 10,000 km, T50 every ODD year OR every 40,000 km from 20,000 km, T60 every EVEN year OR every 40,000 km from 40,000 km. At 7,000 km/yr the calendar always fires first, so the owner pays the full T30/T50/T60 cadence while never reaching a single mileage trigger in ten years (70,000 km total). (2) Consumables become age-limited rather than wear-limited: tires are replaced because rubber hardens (~5-6 years) with tread to spare, and the 12V auxiliary battery dies on calendar life. Tax (牌照稅 NT$15,210/yr for the 2,487 cc bracket + 燃料費 NT$7,200/yr) and insurance are EXCLUDED from every figure here by design. Not a BEV, so no home-charger installation cost applies and no BEV-specific treatment (price-cut repricing, battery-health residuals, faster tire wear) is relevant. Market context baked into the value curve: the Alphard was a genuine no-discount, two-year-waiting-list, pay-a-premium car in Taiwan from its June 2023 launch until roughly May 2025, when forum reports of dealers discounting new Alphard/Lexus LM stock began. The 2023-2025 used listings therefore sit on a shortage-inflated base that is now normalising, and the long-dated checkpoints are deliberately discounted against the raw listing evidence.

purchase.source: Toyota Taiwan official showroom (https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/ALPHARD/) — independently re-fetched 2026-08-12 by the fact-check pass: HYBRID (E-Four 4WD) NT$3,160,000, PHEV NT$3,300,000, 16.4 km/L. list_price CONFIRMED, unchanged. discounts RAISED from NT$100,000 to NT$130,000 on review (see notes). purchase.notes: Price history consistent: the 4th-gen (AH40) Alphard launched in Taiwan 2023-06-21 as a single-spec Hybrid E-Four at NT$3,150,000; on 2025-02-06 Hotai added the PHEV at NT$3,300,000 and raised the HEV by NT$10,000 to today's NT$3,160,000. Spec and price are unchanged since then — KingAutos shows no MY2026 or MY2027 announcement — so model_year is recorded as 2026, the car on sale today. (8891 labels the same unchanged car '2026年最新購車菜單' on its menu board and '2027年式' on its cost page; that is a portal-side forward label, not a manufacturer model-year change, and the earlier draft's '2027年式' claim has been removed as unsupported.) DISCOUNT — CORRECTED. The earlier draft used NT$100,000 (3.2%). Toyota Taiwan discounts routinely, and the Alphard's no-discount regime broke in about May 2025, fifteen months before this record's date; the same draft's own evidence — 8891 購車菜單 budgets clustering at NT$3,000,000-3,030,000 against the NT$3,160,000 list — implies NT$130,000-160,000 off. NT$100,000 sat below its own sourced range with no offsetting evidence, so it is raised to NT$130,000 (4.1%), the conservative end of that range, because the underlying figures are buyer budgets rather than verified closed deals. onroad_fees NT$65,000 = 領牌規費 + 代辦 (~NT$15,000: 行照工本費 200, 新領牌照 600, 檢驗 450, plus dealer 代辦) plus ~NT$50,000 of the accessory pack Alphard buyers actually specify — full-vehicle window film including the panoramic roof (expensive on a vehicle with this much glass), dashcam, 3D moulded floor mats. real_cost = 3,160,000 - 130,000 + 65,000 = 3,095,000. No tax, no insurance.

selling_costs.notes: Top of the usual NT$4,000-15,000 band because the class drives every line item up. The monitor-office transfer fees themselves are trivial and fixed (行車執照工本費 NT$200, 登記書 NT$15) — the NT$3,000 is mostly 代辦 convenience. The detailing line is where the size shows: a 5.0 m, 2.2-tonne MPV with three rows, twin power sliding doors and a large glass roof takes far longer to polish and deep-clean than a sedan. value_checkpoints.source: Live 8891 中古車 AH40 listings, independently re-pulled by the fact-check pass on 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard and https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard?minYear=2023). Verified closest comparables, all 車商售價 (dealer RETAIL asking): 2025-reg Hybrid 2.5 asking NT$2,998,000 at 23,000 km and NT$2,980,000 at 20,000 km; for reference the 2025-reg PHEV asks NT$3,138,000 at 1,000 km. RETAIL-TO-PRIVATE ADJUSTMENT MADE, NOT SKIPPED: a 1-year/7,000 km HEV would ask about NT$3,030,000 retail (low-mileage uplift over the 20,000-23,000 km comparables); cut ~11% for private sale to NT$2,700,000, then a further ~13% for dealer trade-in to NT$2,350,000. Sanity check: a new car now transacts near NT$3,030,000 after discount, so a 1-year car cannot fetch its ~NT$3,000,000 asking price — the listings are aspirational and the private figure must sit well under them.

Two anchor sets, both re-verified live on 8891 中古車 on 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard?minYear=2023). (a) Current-gen AH40 at 1-2 years: asking NT$2,750,000 at 50,000 km and NT$2,688,000 at 70,000 km — dealer retail, at 2.5-3.5x our mileage. (b) Predecessor AH30 2.5 Hybrid Executive Lounge at 3 years (original list NT$2,860,000): 2023-reg asking NT$2,488,000 at 51,000 km versus NT$1,990,000 at 100,000 km — a 25% spread across 49,000 km, which quantifies how mileage-sensitive this model is. ADJUSTMENT MADE: from the observed 2-year/50,000 km retail of NT$2,750,000 take ~11% for private sale, add a DAMPED low-mileage uplift toward 21,000 km (extrapolating the raw 25%/49,000 km coefficient linearly would be absurd), subtract a year of age, landing at NT$2,430,000 private; trade-in a further ~13% down. Cross-check against 8891's mileage-blind 3-year retention of 70.5% (NT$2,228,000 at an assumed 60,000 km) plus a low-mileage premium lands in the same place.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — the AH40 only launched in Taiwan in June 2023, so no genuine 5-year current-gen car exists and none was invented. Method: take the AH30 2.5 Hybrid E-Four Executive Lounge (closest analogue — same 2.5 hybrid E-Four powertrain, same segment, top trim, original list NT$2,840,000 from its 2020-08-25 launch), read its real 5-year prices live on 8891 on 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard?minYear=2015&maxYear=2021): 2021-reg asking NT$1,888,000 at 63,000 km and NT$1,880,000 at 97,900 km — both re-verified by the fact-check pass — i.e. ~66.5% retail retention of its own list. Uplift ~8-10% because our car has 35,000 km against their 63,000-98,000 km, giving ~74% retail retention, applied to this car's real_cost of NT$3,095,000: ~NT$2,290,000 retail, less ~11% = NT$2,050,000 private, less ~13% = NT$1,780,000 trade-in. Corroborates 8891's mileage-blind 5-year figure of 59.7% once adjusted upward for our third-of-average mileage. CAVEAT: the AH30 2.5 Hybrid EL's NT$2,840,000 list price is the one denominator the fact-check pass could NOT independently re-verify (U-CAR returns 403 and the web-search budget was spent), so it is carried over from the first pass unconfirmed.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — no 7-year AH40 exists or can exist before 2030. Method: use the AH30 3.5 V6 Executive Lounge, original Taiwan list NT$2,650,000 after the 2018-02-26 facelift. Its real 7-year prices, re-verified live on 8891 on 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard?minYear=2015&maxYear=2021): 2019-reg asking NT$1,528,000 and NT$1,558,000 at 84,000 km, and NT$1,429,000 at 118,500 km — about 57.7-58.8% retail retention of its own list at ~84,000 km. Uplift ~8% for our 49,000 km, giving ~63.5%, applied to real_cost NT$3,095,000: ~NT$1,965,000 retail, less ~11% = NT$1,750,000 private, less ~13% = NT$1,520,000 trade-in. One caveat that cuts in our favour and is why this was not trimmed further: the donor is a 3.5 V6 carrying NT$28,220/yr 牌照稅, which depresses its Taiwan used value, whereas this 2.5 hybrid pays NT$15,210 — so the hybrid should retain somewhat better at this age. CAVEAT: the NT$2,650,000 facelift list price is carried over from the first pass and could not be independently re-verified.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — no 10-year AH40 exists or can exist before 2033. Method: use the AH30 3.5 (original Taiwan list NT$2,580,000, launched 2015-03-24). Real 10-11 year prices re-verified live on 8891 on 2026-08-12 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard?minYear=2015&maxYear=2021): 2015-reg EL asking NT$1,268,000 at 120,000 km (49.1% retail retention) and 2015-reg asking NT$1,198,000 at 200,000 km (46.4%); nearest younger anchors are 2017-reg asking NT$1,338,000 at 101,100 km and NT$1,368,000 at 85,000 km. CORRECTION: the first pass cited a 2016-reg car at NT$1,380,000 / 110,000 km as its ~53.5% anchor; that listing was NOT present on re-check and has been dropped, so the verified 10-11 year band is ~46-49%, not ~53%. Uplifting the verified ~49% for our 70,000 km would give ~55-56% retail, i.e. about NT$1,530,000 private — but this is marked DOWN, for two reasons. First, those donor cars spent their whole life inside the 2023-2025 Alphard shortage that has now ended. Second, 8891's own retention model extended past its published 7-year point (50.5%) implies closer to 44% even after a low-mileage adjustment. Splitting the two methods rather than taking the flattering one gives NT$1,480,000 private and NT$1,280,000 trade-in. This remains the weakest number in the record.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, not mileage-driven — the single most important fact for this buyer. Toyota Taiwan's official schedule (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx, re-fetched and re-read 2026-08-12) is: T30 every 6 months OR 10,000 km (engine oil, oil filter, drain plug gasket, 30+ checks); T50 every ODD year OR every 40,000 km from 20,000 km (base items plus periodic replacements including AIR FILTER and SPARK PLUGS, 50+ checks); T60 every EVEN year OR every 40,000 km from 40,000 km (the fullest package — adds BRAKE FLUID, COOLANT and FUEL FILTER, 60+ checks). CORRECTION to the first draft, which had the air filter in T60 and put a cabin filter in both: per the official page the air filter and spark plugs belong to T50, and brake fluid / coolant / fuel filter to T60. At 7,000 km/year the calendar trigger ALWAYS fires first — the owner never reaches a single mileage trigger in ten years (70,000 km total) yet still pays for roughly two shop visits a year. Assumed cadence: one T30 at the 6-month point plus one T50 (odd years) or T60 (even years) at the annual point. IMPORTANT SOURCING CAVEAT: Toyota Taiwan does NOT publish package prices — the official page explicitly directs owners to service centres — and 8891's cost page lists 保養: 暫無數據 for this model. The per-visit figures used here (T30 ~NT$3,200, T50 ~NT$5,500, T60 ~NT$9,000) are therefore SCALED ESTIMATES, not quotes: they are extrapolated from third-party collations of Toyota TW 定保 pricing for much smaller models (Vios/Yaris 10,000 km ~NT$2,270, 20,000 km ~NT$2,900, 40,000 km ~NT$3,970), stepped up because the A25A-FXS 2.5 hybrid takes ~4.2-4.5 L of oil against 3.5-4.0 L and because this is a flagship MPV. The scale-up factor is engineering judgement, which is why no maintenance checkpoint here is rated better than medium and years 3 onward are rated low. NO free scheduled-maintenance programme exists; Toyota Taiwan gives free LABOUR on the first two services only (the 1,000 km inspection is free outright), which is why year 1 is so cheap. Warranty verified 2026-08-12 (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx): 3 years/100,000 km factory plus Hotai's added 1 year/20,000 km = 4 years/120,000 km. Hybrid battery is separately covered 8 years/160,000 km for 2019+ model years, so it is protected right through the year-7 checkpoint and expires early in the year-10 window. Because mileage stays low, consumables go on AGE: tires harden out at roughly 5-6 years with tread to spare, and the 12V auxiliary battery dies on calendar life. Spark plugs are effectively a non-event — long-life iridium is a ~100,000 km item, which this car would not reach until year 14 — so the T50 plug line is inspection, not replacement.

checkpoints.source: Schedule from Toyota Taiwan (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx); warranty term 4 years/120,000 km verified at https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx on 2026-08-12; hybrid battery 8 years/160,000 km for 2019+ model years. assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; all checkpoints use 7,000 km/year (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. This matters more for the Alphard than for almost any other car sold here: Taiwan Alphards are overwhelmingly business/VIP shuttles, so most used listings are 50,000-190,000 km cars and a genuinely low-mileage private example sells above the mileage-blind average. Maintenance at 7,000 km/year is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Toyota Taiwan's interval is every 6 months OR 10,000 km, whichever comes first, so this owner hits the 6-month clock every time and never the odometer (~2 workshop visits/year, ~20 over 10 years). Over 10 years the car accumulates only 70,000 km, so every km-based warranty limit expires on TIME, not distance. WARRANTY CORRECTION (audit): Toyota TW's basic vehicle AND battery component coverage is 4 years/120,000 km (3yr/100,000 km factory + 1yr/20,000 km 和泰 extension). The 8-year/160,000 km figure is a >=70% CAPACITY guarantee only, NOT a component-failure warranty. So a traction-battery FAILURE is at owner risk from year 4 onward, not year 8 — this is corrected from the researcher's version and is reflected in the year 7 and year 10 maintenance provisions and in the year 10 residual. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: 牌照稅 and 燃料稅, 強制險 and 任意險, fuel and electricity. ALSO EXCLUDED and worth flagging separately: a home AC charger. The PHEV's 80 km EV range is only worth paying for if it is charged nightly, and a Taiwan home-charger install runs roughly NT$30,000-80,000 (more in an apartment building needing 管委會 approval and a dedicated meter). That is a real ownership cost but a one-time capital item, so it is in neither maintenance.checkpoints nor onroad_fees.

purchase.source: Official 建議售價 independently re-verified for this audit by direct fetch of Toyota Taiwan's showroom page (https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/ALPHARD/) on 2026-08-12: PHEV NT$3,300,000 and HYBRID NT$3,160,000, both 2,487 cc E-Four 4WD, PHEV quoted at 177 ps engine output, 70.4 km/l and ~80 km EV range on an 18.1 kWh pack. The researcher's NT$3,300,000 is CORRECT and is unchanged. onroad_fees was CHANGED from NT$85,000 to NT$48,000 — see notes.
purchase.notes: LIST PRICE UNCHANGED. NT$3,300,000 re-confirmed by direct fetch of Toyota TW's own showroom page. The PHEV launched in Taiwan 2025-02-06 alongside a rise of the HEV to NT$316萬, and the official page still shows NT$330萬 today, so there is no repricing shock to the used stock (unlike the Tesla pattern). DISCOUNTS = 0, BUT THE REASON HAS BEEN CORRECTED. The researcher justified zero discount with a June 2024 report of >4,000 outstanding orders against a ~500 unit/year quota and a quoted 4-year wait. That evidence is two years stale: 2026 reporting says Toyota expanded Alphard production from 2026 to 「大幅縮短候車期」, the current quoted wait is around 4 months rather than years, and post-refresh order intake is described as 「大致順利」. Zero cash discount is still the right number — the Alphard is a low-volume flagship import and 和泰 does not run cash-off campaigns on it the way it does on Altis/Corolla Cross (NT$20,000-60,000), with incentives taking the form of zero-interest financing instead — but it is no longer supported by a multi-year queue, and that same easing is why the year-1 residual in this record has been reduced. ONROAD_FEES CHANGED 85,000 -> 48,000. The researcher's NT$85,000 was 2.58% of list, a clear outlier against every comparable record in this dataset, which clusters at 1.0-1.8% (Lexus LM350h NT$4,290,000 -> NT$45,000 = 1.05%; Porsche Cayenne NT$4,190,000 -> NT$60,000 = 1.43%), and specifically against the sibling Alphard HYBRID record, which uses NT$45,000 on a nearly identical NT$3,160,000 car. The same bodyshell at the same dealer cannot carry 89% more registration and accessory cost. The NT$85,000 build assumed a maximally-optioned buyer (NT$45,000 of premium window film alone). Rebuilt at a normal-but-generous flagship level: 領牌 + 代辦 ~NT$8,000 (新領牌照登記費, 行照工本費, dealer agency fee); 全車隔熱紙 ~NT$22,000 (an Alphard has far more glass than a sedan); 行車記錄器 ~NT$8,000; 腳踏墊/晴雨窗/門檻條/車內配件 ~NT$10,000. Excludes 牌照稅, 燃料稅, 強制險, 任意險 per the model's design, and excludes the home charger (see assumptions.notes). REAL_COST = 3,300,000 - 0 + 48,000 = NT$3,348,000.

selling_costs.notes: UNCHANGED — reviewed and found sound. Set at the top of the usual NT$4,000-15,000 band because of the vehicle class, not the price tag alone. 過戶: 規費 plus a 代辦 fee, ~NT$3,000. 售前整備/美容 is the item that scales: an Alphard has a three-row leather cabin, powered ottoman captain's chairs, a headliner monitor and roughly twice the interior volume of a sedan, so a proper pre-sale detail is ~NT$8,000 rather than the ~NT$3,000 a compact car needs. 刊登費 ~NT$3,000 for a paid/featured 8891 listing, the norm at this value.
