Matches the sibling Alphard HYBRID record at NT$14,000, which is correct — selling costs depend on the body, not the powertrain.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWN from NT$2,840,000. The researcher stated no PHEV used listings could be found and therefore synthesised a dealer retail asking price of NT$3,150,000. Real Alphard PHEV listings DO exist and were pulled directly on 2026-08-12 from https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard?year=2025 — four identifiable 2025 MY PHEVs: NT$3,138,000 @ 1,000 km (Keelung), NT$3,028,000 @ 4,900 km (Kaohsiung), NT$2,988,000 @ 21,000 km (Taipei), NT$3,190,000 @ 23,000 km (Tainan). The synthesised NT$3,150,000 exceeded the asking price of the 1,000 km car, which is not possible for a 7,000 km car. OBSERVED DEALER RETAIL for a 7,000 km PHEV, interpolated between the 1,000 km and 4,900 km cars, is ~NT$3,080,000 (~93% of list — high, but that is the Alphard). ADJUSTMENT MADE, NOT COPIED: private sale = 3,080,000 x 0.89 = NT$2,740,000, an 11% step down inside the 8-15% dealer-retail-to-private band; I used the middle rather than the tight end because the new-car wait has fallen to roughly 4 months, so a private seller no longer has queue-jumping buyers competing in days. Dealer trade-in = 2,740,000 x 0.885 = NT$2,420,000. SEPARATE FINDING that shapes every later checkpoint: at matched mileage the PHEV asks the SAME as the HEV (PHEV NT$2,988,000 @ 21,000 km vs HEV NT$2,980,000 @ 20,000 km and NT$2,998,000 @ 23,000 km), so the NT$140,000 new-car PHEV premium has already evaporated by year 1.

CORRECTED DOWN from NT$2,420,000. No 3-year-old PHEV exists (launched 2025-02), so this uses same-generation AH40 HEV cars at age 3 and applies the observed year-1 PHEV-equals-HEV parity in ABSOLUTE NT$ rather than scaling by the PHEV's higher list price — the researcher scaled the ratio up to the NT$330萬 list and then took only a 2% haircut, which re-inflates a premium the market has already discarded. Dealer RETAIL anchors, FindCar 2026-08-12 (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&b=72&m=577&op=4): 2023 2.5HV 4WD NT$2,598,000 @ 30,885 km, NT$2,488,000 and NT$2,480,000 @ 51,807 km. 8891's 2023 band (NT$1,770,000-2,488,000) is contaminated by leftover AH30 stock and was not used. Uplifting the 30,885 km car to our 21,000 km gives dealer retail ~NT$2,660,000, and the PHEV sits at parity per the year-1 finding. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private = 2,660,000 x 0.89 = NT$2,370,000; trade-in = 2,370,000 x 0.88 = NT$2,090,000. Now correctly sits BELOW the sibling Alphard HYBRID record's year-3 figure of NT$2,470,000, as it must once the PHEV premium is gone.

CORRECTED DOWN from NT$2,210,000 — this was the single worst number in the researcher's record. At NT$2,210,000 the PHEV sat ABOVE the sibling Alphard HYBRID record's year-5 value of NT$2,110,000, i.e. the plug-in with a large battery approaching the end of its coverage was modelled as out-retaining the plain hybrid, which is backwards for Taiwan. It also produced a broken curve shape: only -8.7% across years 3-5 followed by -19.0% across years 5-7, when depreciation should not re-accelerate that way. EXTRAPOLATED — no 5-year-old AH40 exists (generation launched 2023) and no 5-year-old PHEV. Method: continued the observed AH40 curve from the year-3 dealer retail anchor of NT$2,660,000 at roughly 6.5%/year to ~NT$2,320,000 dealer retail at age 5 / 35,000 km, cross-checked against the predecessor AH30 2.5 Hybrid (TW list NT$2,840,000, cars.tvbs.com.tw/car-news/10828) whose 5-year-old cars ask NT$1,698,000-1,888,000 at 63,000-100,000 km and which supports a materially higher figure at our 35,000 km. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private = 2,320,000 x 0.885 = NT$2,060,000; trade-in = 2,060,000 x 0.875 = NT$1,800,000. Placed just below the HYBRID sibling, reflecting the first real battery-health questions and a thinner buyer pool. Confidence low: cross-generation and cross-powertrain inference, not observation.

CORRECTED DOWN from NT$1,790,000 (small change, curve continuity). EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION — there is no 7-year-old AH40 and no 7-year-old Alphard PHEV anywhere in Taiwan, and none was invented. Method: 2019 MY AH30 3.5 Executive Lounge, TW list NT$2,650,000 after the 2018 facelift (news.u-car.com.tw/article/40886, read via search index), is 7 years old now and asks NT$1,429,000-1,558,000 on 8891 — but every one of those cars carries 84,000-185,000 km (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard). That is ~56% retention on dealer ASKING at shuttle-grade mileage; our car has 49,000 km, a large premium on this model, supporting ~68% asking retention for the combustion predecessor. Cross-checked against continuing the AH40 curve from the year-5 anchor, which lands in the same place. Dealer retail asking ~NT$2,030,000 after a PHEV haircut that is now LARGER than the researcher applied, because the audit found battery COMPONENT coverage ends at 4 years/120,000 km — only the >=70% capacity guarantee runs to 8 years — so a year-7 buyer is already pricing uncovered pack risk. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private = 2,030,000 x 0.87 = NT$1,770,000; trade-in = 1,770,000 x 0.865 = NT$1,530,000, wider spreads than year 1 because an out-of-warranty 7-year-old moves slowly and dealers bid defensively.

CORRECTED DOWN from NT$1,400,000. The researcher's figure was IDENTICAL to the sibling Alphard HYBRID record's year-10 value, which cannot be right: at 10 years the dominant price driver is battery risk, and the PHEV's 18.1 kWh pack is a NT$300,000+ replacement against roughly NT$100,000-150,000 for the HEV's much smaller pack. The PHEV must sit below the HEV here, not level with it. EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION, stated rather than invented. Method: 2016 MY AH30 3.5 Executive Lounge, TW list NT$2,580,000 at the 2015 launch (news.u-car.com.tw/news/article/25820, read via search index), is exactly 10 years old and asks NT$1,380,000 @ 110,000 km; 2017 MY asks NT$1,338,000-1,368,000; 2015 MY (11 years) asks NT$1,198,000-1,268,000 (all https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/alphard). That is ~52-54% retention on dealer ASKING at 85,000-110,000 km; our car's 70,000 km lifts that to ~58% for a combustion predecessor. Applied to NT$3,300,000 and then discounted ~21% for PHEV-specific risk (larger than the researcher's 15%): the capacity guarantee lapsed on TIME at year 8, component coverage lapsed back at year 4, a pack replacement is a NT$300,000+ event, and there is no 10-year-old PHEV MPV market in Taiwan to price against. Dealer retail asking ~NT$1,510,000. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private = 1,510,000 x 0.86 = NT$1,300,000; trade-in = 1,300,000 x 0.855 = NT$1,110,000. Confidence low; read as a band, not a point.

maintenance.plan_notes: INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Toyota Taiwan's schedule is every 6 months OR 10,000 km, whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year this owner ALWAYS hits the 6-month clock first and never the odometer, so the cost driver is 2 workshop visits per year (~20 over 10 years) regardless of how little the car is driven, alternating a 小保養 (oil + filter, roughly NT$4,000-5,000 on an Alphard) with a larger service (roughly NT$7,000-10,000). Mobile01 owner reports put Toyota 小保養 at ~NT$4,000 and 大保養 near NT$10,000; the Alphard sits at the top of that band as the flagship. FREE-SERVICE CLAIM CORRECTED (audit): Toyota Taiwan gives the 1個月/1,000 km delivery check free, but the first 6-month/10,000 km scheduled service is NOT free — it is a normal paid 定期保養. The researcher treated it as free and set year 1 at only NT$8,000; year 1 has been raised to NT$13,000 to carry two paid visits (6-month and 12-month), which also brings it into line with the sibling Alphard HYBRID record's NT$14,000. Toyota Taiwan runs no Volvo-style included-servicing programme. WARRANTY, CORRECTED: basic vehicle and battery-component coverage is 4 years/120,000 km (3yr/100,000 km factory + 1yr/20,000 km 和泰 extension) per https://www.toyota.com.tw/electric_guarantee.aspx. The 8-year/160,000 km term on that page is a >=70% CAPACITY guarantee only, not a component-failure warranty — the researcher read it as a full 8-year battery warranty. Practical effect: traction-battery FAILURE risk is uncovered from year 4, so a provision now appears in the 5-7y window as well as 7-10y, and the 7-10y provision was raised. The page states coverage generically for 所有車型; it does NOT explicitly name the Alphard PHEV, so the researcher's 'ALPHARD is named on the covered list' claim has been removed. PHEV-SPECIFIC SHAPE: regenerative braking makes pads and discs last far longer than on a 2.3-tonne combustion MPV (first pad change only in the 5-7y window), and the engine runs relatively few hours; but the mass and torque are hard on TIRES, and at this mileage tires AGE OUT rather than wear out — sets are replaced on a ~5-6 year clock (periods 5 and 10), not on tread depth. The 12V auxiliary battery is an AGM/EFB unit that still dies on schedule and is budgeted three times over 10 years. Excludes tax, insurance, fuel, electricity and the home charger.

First brake job lands here rather than earlier precisely because regen braking does most of the retardation; a combustion MPV would have needed pads by ~40,000 km. assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000/21000/35000/49000/70000), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. Three consequences dominate. (1) VALUES: every predecessor comp on 8891/FindCar sits at 90,000-130,000 km, i.e. 2-3x our car's age-matched mileage, so each was adjusted UP for low mileage before use — but moderately (+5% to +20% relative depending on the mileage gap), not the +20-25% a prior draft applied. (2) The year-1 value is propped up by a SUPPLY SHORTAGE, not by intrinsic retention: Taiwan launched the LC250 as a 100-unit online lottery (registration 2025/07/11-20, ~2,500 applicants, deliveries from 2025/11), so near-new cars trade at or above list today. That premium unwinds as 和泰 delivers more allocation, which is why depreciation stays elevated through years 1-5 and only flattens after year 7 onto the Land Cruiser enthusiast floor visible in the predecessor data. (3) MAINTENANCE: Toyota TW's interval is 每半年或1萬公里, whichever first, so at 7,000 km/year this car is entirely TIME-driven — 2 visits/year, never mileage-triggered, 20 visits against only 70,000 km over 10 years. Consumables age out rather than wear out: tires are replaced on rubber age (~5-6 years) with tread remaining. THE BIG CAVEAT: 2.8L diesel + 7,000 km/year is the worst-case DPF (diesel particulate filter — traps soot and must burn it off at 600-650°C) combination. Short low-mileage trips rarely get the exhaust hot enough to complete regeneration, so soot accumulates; an OEM DPF replacement quotes NT$150,000-200,000. This is priced as an explicit probability-weighted provision in the 5-7y and 7-10y windows and is the single most decision-relevant fact here — a gasoline SUV would not carry it. Excluded by design: tax (牌照稅/燃料費), insurance, fuel, parking, and the NT$20,000 dual-tone roof option. Not a BEV, so no home-charger consideration applies.

purchase.source: Official 建議售價 NT$2,880,000 verified directly on Toyota Taiwan's showroom page (https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/LANDCRUISER/), which lists 越野探索版 at NT$2,880,000 and the sister 越野極境版 at NT$2,900,000, both 2.8L turbo diesel + 48V mild hybrid, 2,755 c.c., 204 ps @ 3,000-3,400 rpm. purchase.notes: Trim full name 越野探索版 (Wilderness Explorer), the NT$2,880,000 entry grade of a two-grade line-up. DISCOUNTS = 0, which breaks the normal Toyota TW rule. 和泰 does routinely discount its mainstream lineup, but the LC250 is supply-allocated: Taiwan launched it via an online lottery for just 100 units (registration 2025/07/11-20, NT$20,000 deposit, ~2,500 applicants), with deliveries from 2025/11. Live 8891 listings confirm no discount exists — a 2027 LC250 with 8 km asks NT$2,960,000 and a 2026 with 5,100 km asks NT$2,890,000, i.e. dealers transact near-new cars ABOVE official list. The realistic 'discount' is negative; floored at 0 rather than modelling a premium. ONROAD_FEES NT$85,000 (~3.0% of list): 領牌規費+代辦 ~NT$13,000 plus ~NT$72,000 of 車美仕/原廠配件 typical on a NT$2.9M imported SUV delivery (隔熱紙, 行車記錄器, 側踏板, 行李廂墊, 避光墊). Land Cruiser buyers often add off-road hardware (winch, bars, AT tires) worth another NT$100,000-300,000; excluded as buyer-specific. Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 2,880,000 - 0 + 85,000 = 2,965,000.

value_checkpoints.source: Best-evidenced checkpoint: a near-exact comp exists. 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/land-cruiser) lists a 2025 LC250 2.8 柴油48V at 7,000 km asking NT$2,660,000 marked 個人自售 (PRIVATE SALE) — same model, same powertrain, and the exact mileage this buyer reaches at year 1. Because that is already a private ASKING price, no dealer-retail haircut was applied; I deducted ~3% for negotiation and a further small amount because deliveries only began 2025/11, so that car is ~9 months old rather than a full 12 — giving NT$2,560,000. Dealer-route cross-check agrees: the same page shows a 2026 LC250 at 5,100 km asking NT$2,890,000 (車商售價); the ~10% 車商售價→自售價 adjustment gives NT$2,601,000. Two routes converge on NT$2.56-2.60M. Retention is extraordinary (86% of real_cost) but it is MEASURED, not assumed — near-new cars transact at or above list because the 100-unit lottery capped supply. Confidence MEDIUM, not high: this rests on a single private listing plus one dealer listing, and both are asking prices rather than confirmed transactions. dealer_tradein NT$2,300,000 = private -10.2%, at the narrow end of the usual 10-15% because allocation-limited LC250 stock is actively hunted by 車商 and re-lists fast.

EXTRAPOLATED — no LC250 in Taiwan is older than ~1 year (deliveries began 2025/11), so no current-generation 3-year data can exist. Method: anchor on the predecessor Land Cruiser Prado and step back. carbook.tw (https://carbook.tw/cars/toyota-land-cruiser-prado/2022) prices a 2022 Prado (4 years old, median 50,000 km) at 在線開價 NT$1,790,000 / 建議成交 NT$1,640,000-1,690,000 / 車行收購 NT$1,560,000; private sale sits between 建議成交 and 收購 at ~NT$1,600,000. FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/land%20cruiser%20prado) gives that car's ORIGINAL list as NT$2,790,000 (2022 探索旗艦版) — the 探索玩家版 at NT$2,400,000 is ruled out because it would imply an implausible 74.6% dealer-asking retention at 4 years. So real 4-year private retention is 57.3% of list. Stepping back one year (+~8 points) gives ~66%; +10% relative for 21,000 km vs a ~42,000 km median gives ~72.6%; +4% for the LC250 being the more desirable, supply-tighter model gives ~73% of list = NT$2,100,000 (70.8% of real_cost). Confidence LOW: the anchor is real, but the cross-generation transfer and, critically, the rate at which the lottery-driven supply premium unwinds between years 1 and 3 are both my judgement. dealer_tradein = private -11.0%.

EXTRAPOLATED from two real predecessor data points, both on the SAME 2.8 diesel engine family, and deliberately lower than a naive read of the 4-year table. Route A: FindCar/8891 list a 2021 Prado 2.8 柴油 7-seater at 125,459 km asking NT$1,299,000 (車商售價) against an original list of NT$2,780,000 (2021 探索旗艦版, https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/land%20cruiser%20prado) — 46.7% on dealer asking, ~42.1% as private sale after the -10% adjustment, at exactly 5 years. Adjusting UP ~20% relative for our 35,000 km versus its 125,459 km, plus ~5% for LC250 desirability, gives ~53% of list = NT$1,527,000. Route B: the carbook 2022 Prado table (https://carbook.tw/cars/toyota-land-cruiser-prado/2022) gives 57.3% private retention at 4 years / 50,000 km against its NT$2,790,000 list; ageing one year (x0.90), +5% for 35,000 vs 50,000 km, +5% for LC250 gives ~56.9% = NT$1,639,000. I take NT$1,600,000 between the two routes — 55.6% of list, 54.0% of real_cost. NOTE this is materially below a prior draft's NT$1,920,000, which had applied an oversized low-mileage uplift and used an unsourced NT$2,690,000 denominator for the Prado; the verified NT$2,780,000-2,790,000 list makes real predecessor retention lower than assumed. Confidence LOW. dealer_tradein = private -11.9%.

EXTRAPOLATED — the LC250 generation is under 1 year old in Taiwan, so no genuine 7-year data can exist and none is claimed. Because I could not verify an original list price for the 4.0 Prado, I used the older comps for SHAPE (age-to-age ratio) rather than for absolute level, which avoids resting on an unsourced denominator. Real comps: 2019 Prado 4.0 at 130,000 km asking NT$958,000 versus the 2021 Prado 2.8 at 125,459 km asking NT$1,299,000 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/land-cruiser-prado, https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/land%20cruiser) — at essentially identical mileage, two extra years costs 26.3% (958/1299 = 0.737). Applying that ratio to my year-5 figure, with the low-mileage uplift carried through roughly unchanged (49,000 km at year 7 is the same proportional discount to median as 35,000 km at year 5), gives NT$1,180,000-1,250,000; I use NT$1,250,000, the upper end, for the LC250's stronger standing. That is 43.4% of list, 42.2% of real_cost. Cross-check: the 2018 Prado 4.0 VX at 90,000 km asks NT$1,080,000, and our car at year 7 is one year younger with 46% less mileage, which is consistent with ~NT$1.25M private. Confidence LOW by construction. dealer_tradein = private -12.8%.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation, same method as year 7, and explicitly not a current-generation observation. Real Prado LC150 comps at 10-12 years (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/land-cruiser-prado, https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/land%20cruiser): 2016 Prado 4.0 at 110,000 km asking NT$958,000 and 2014 Prado 4.0 VX at 115,084 km asking NT$898,000. The striking feature of the Prado data is how FLAT it is at the long end — the 2016 at 110,000 km asks exactly the same NT$958,000 as the 2019 at 130,000 km, so once mileage is accounted for, years 7 to 10 are almost level. Land Cruisers in Taiwan hit a hard enthusiast floor rather than sliding. Taking that flatness plus a ~+12-15% low-mileage uplift (70,000 km against the comps' 110,000-115,000 km) and a small LC250 premium gives ~38% of list = NT$1,100,000 (37.1% of real_cost). A real risk NOT in this number: a DPF-troubled short-trip diesel with a service history full of carbon-cleaning invoices sells below a clean one, and buyers of 10-year diesels scrutinise exactly that. Confidence LOW by construction. dealer_tradein = private -14.1%, the widest spread in the table, since a decade-old diesel carries the most reconditioning and emissions risk for a 車商.

maintenance.plan_notes: NO free scheduled maintenance, but MORE warranty than a flat 4-year reading suggests. Toyota TW (和泰) runs no complimentary-servicing programme of the Volvo kind — 定保 is billed per visit and the T30 定保套餐 is a paid package. Two free items only: the 滿月 check and the 首半年（或1萬公里）free inspection (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx). Base warranty is 4 years / 120,000 km (3yr/100,000km Toyota + 1yr/20,000km 和泰 top-up, https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx), which at 7,000 km/year expires on TIME at year 4 with only ~28,000 km showing — the mileage half is worthless to this buyer. CRITICALLY, that same page also documents two loyalty extensions a prior draft missed: owners who keep servicing on schedule at 和泰 receive a complimentary 5th year / 140,000 km economy warranty, and continued compliance extends engine 8-major-systems coverage to 10 years / 150,000 km. This buyer makes 20 on-schedule visits over 10 years, so they qualify: the 3-5y window is effectively fully covered, not half-covered, and major engine-internal failure risk in years 7-10 is substantially underwritten. The DPF is an emissions component and is NOT expected to fall under engine-systems coverage, so the DPF provision stands undiminished. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: Toyota TW specifies 每半年或1萬公里，以先到者為準 (verified on the owner_maintenance page). At 7,000 km/year the 6-month clock always fires first — 2 visits/year for all 10 years, 20 visits against only 70,000 km, never once mileage-triggered. Consumables age out rather than wear out: tires replaced on rubber age (~5-6 years) with tread left, budgeted at years ~5 and ~10 at ~NT$44,000-46,000 per set of four fitted for a 2.4-tonne vehicle; brake pads last far longer than mileage-average. Diesel-specific items replace the gasoline ones: no spark plugs at all, but fuel filters, low-ash diesel oil (~7.5L per change, dearer than gasoline oil), and full-time-4WD front/rear diff plus transfer-case oils a monocoque SUV does not have. THE DOMINANT RISK IS THE DPF: it needs 600-650°C exhaust to burn off trapped soot, and a 7,000 km/year short-trip car rarely gets there (https://www.mys-spirit.com.tw/exhaustview-328.html, which quotes OEM DPF replacement at NT$150,000-200,000). Owner reports indicate Toyota TW dealers do not offer EGR/DPF carbon cleaning as a menu item, pushing owners to independent specialists. The 5-7y and 7-10y period costs therefore carry explicit probability-weighted DPF provisions. Costs assumed at 和泰 authorised service; independent shops would run 25-35% cheaper on routine visits but riskier on the 48V and emissions hardware — and using them would forfeit the loyalty warranty extensions above.

checkpoints.source: Tire replacement is the step change and it is AGE-driven, not wear-driven: at 7,000 km/year the OE 18-inch tires still have tread at year 5 but the rubber is 5-6 years old, and a set of four fitted for a 2.4-tonne 4WD runs ~NT$11,000 each. Routine servicing continues at 4 visits per the 每半年 interval (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx), now including full-time-4WD front/rear diff and transfer-case oils a monocoque SUV never pays for. Base warranty lapses at year 4 on the clock with ~28,000 km showing, BUT https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx documents a complimentary 5th-year / 140,000 km economy warranty for owners who service on schedule at 和泰, which this buyer does — so this window is effectively covered end to end and carries no repair provision. Confidence medium: the tire and battery lines are well-grounded, the exact 定保 pricing is benchmarked rather than quoted.

checkpoints.source: First window outside the extended warranty for non-engine items. The DPF cleaning line is buyer-profile-specific, not boilerplate: 7,000 km/year of short trips keeps exhaust below the 600-650°C regeneration threshold, so soot accumulates and periodic forced cleaning becomes necessary (https://www.mys-spirit.com.tw/exhaustview-328.html; owner threads report Toyota TW dealers do not offer EGR/DPF cleaning on the menu, so this goes to an independent specialist at ~NT$8,000-20,000). Note the DPF is an emissions component and is not expected to be covered by the engine 8-major-systems loyalty extension. Front brakes finally come due at year 6-7 — late by mileage-average standards precisely because there are only 49,000 km on them. 8AT fluid and driveline oils fall in this window on the time-based schedule. Confidence medium: routine items are well-grounded, the DPF provision is a judgement call on frequency.

major_items: 第二套輪胎 ≈ NT$46,000（再次因老化更換）
DPF風險準備 ≈ NT$50,000（清洗約NT$15,000＋20%機率的原廠更換NT$15-20萬期望值NT$35,000）
後煞車 ≈ NT$10,000、12V/AGM電瓶 ≈ NT$7,500、水箱精（SLLC約10年）≈ NT$4,500
差速器／分動箱齒輪油 ≈ NT$9,000

checkpoints.source: Largest window by design — 3 years wide and carrying the deferred DPF exposure. The NT$50,000 DPF line is explicitly PROBABILITY-WEIGHTED, not a quoted repair: OEM DPF replacement is NT$150,000-200,000 (https://www.mys-spirit.com.tw/exhaustview-328.html, midpoint NT$175,000) and a decade of sub-7,000 km/year short-trip running is the exact duty cycle that causes blockage, so ~NT$15,000 of cleaning plus a 20% chance of the big-ticket replacement gives 15,000 + 0.20 x 175,000 = NT$50,000. A prior draft stated 20% but carried NT$68,000, which implies ~30%; this version makes the arithmetic match the stated probability. Second tire set is again age-driven at ~year 10. No separate provision for 噴油嘴/渦輪/發電機 engine-internal failures because https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_guarantee.aspx documents engine 8-major-systems coverage extendable to 10 years / 150,000 km for owners maintaining on schedule at 和泰, which this buyer does. Ten-year total across all five windows is NT$414,000 — high for only 70,000 km, and that is the point: a body-on-frame 2.8 diesel 4WD driven this little is expensive per kilometre, and a gasoline SUV on the same schedule would avoid the DPF, fuel-filter and driveline-oil lines entirely. Confidence LOW: the routine portion is sound but the failure provision is an actuarial estimate, not observed invoices.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; all checkpoints use 7,000 km/yr (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km) — roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. This matters twice. (1) Maintenance is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Toyota TW's published schedule (toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx, verified) is T30 every 6 months OR 10,000 km, T50 in odd years OR every 40,000 km from 20,000 km, T60 in even years OR every 40,000 km from 40,000 km — 'whichever comes first'. At 7,000 km/yr the calendar always triggers first, so the owner pays for ~2 visits a year and never reaches a mileage-based interval within 10 years. The 3-year/100,000 km factory warranty is likewise time-limited: it expires at year 3 with only ~21,000 km used, so years 3-10 are fully out of warranty. (2) Resale is helped: 7,000 km/yr puts the car under the mileage-blind average at every age, and the value_checkpoints are quoted from low-mileage listings on that basis. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ADDED IN REVIEW: the visible 8891 GR86 pool is even lower-mileage than this buyer — 2022-2024 cars showing 4,000-10,000 km, i.e. roughly 2,000-3,500 km/yr — so those asking prices are NOT a like-for-like read on a 7,000 km/yr car and have been adjusted down for mileage at each checkpoint. Two GR86-specific cost drivers: the Brembo package makes brake consumables roughly double a standard 86's (86-club TW lists standard 86 front pads at NT$7,000 / rear at NT$5,350; Brembo equivalents run ~2x), and the FA24 flat-four takes ~5.6 L of 0W-20, so even a routine T30 is expensive for a Toyota. Vehicle licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (燃料稅) and insurance are EXCLUDED from every figure by design. Fuel is also excluded. Note the 2.4 L boxer sits in the 2001-3000cc tax bracket and demands 98-octane, so real-world running cost is higher than this record shows.

purchase.source: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY IN REVIEW on the official Toyota Taiwan showroom page (https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/GR86/), spec sheet revision 'GR86 202508A版' (applicable to vehicles built from January 2026): 6MT Brembo NT$1,730,000 and 6AT Brembo NT$1,740,000, 2,387cc flat-four, 234 ps. NT$1,740,000 for the 6AT Brembo is CONFIRMED CORRECT — no change to list_price or real_cost. Discount and on-road figures are estimates from Taiwan market practice, not quoted prices.
purchase.notes: The 2026 TW lineup is Brembo-only, two variants separated purely by transmission; the official spec sheet confirms the 6AT adds paddle shifters, SPORT/SNOW drive modes, 4 (vs 2) rear sensors, ACC adaptive cruise, PCTM and PKSB, none of which the 6MT gets. That is why the AT carries a NT$10,000 premium — it is the better-equipped car here, unusually for a sports model. PRICE HISTORY CORRECTED IN REVIEW: the original record described a '~11% new-price ramp over four years' and used NT$1,598,000 as the 2023-MY original list. Both are wrong. The real sequence is: Aug 2022 TW launch at NT$1,528,000 (6MT) / NT$1,568,000 (6AT) with NO Brembo trim in the range; November 2023 the range went to four cars — 6MT NT$1,670,000, 6MT Brembo NT$1,720,000, 6AT NT$1,680,000, 6AT Brembo NT$1,730,000 (kingautos.net/353324); by the 202508A spec sheet the non-Brembo cars are gone and the 6AT Brembo lists at NT$1,740,000. So like-for-like the 6AT Brembo has risen only +0.6% since Nov 2023 — the list price is essentially FLAT, not ramping. There was one step change (the 2023 repricing, +7.1% on the base 6AT plus a NT$50,000 Brembo step), and it is already fully absorbed into today's used prices. This correction matters because the original record used the phantom ongoing ramp as its justification for steepening years 5-10; the steepening is retained but re-justified on sounder grounds (see the year-5 source string). Discount NT$30,000: deliberately modest. Toyota TW (和泰) discounts volume models like Altis and Corolla Cross by NT$50,000-80,000, but the GR86 is allocation-limited and has been quota-constrained since launch. Under quota, cash off list is small and the deal is sweetened with accessories instead; scattered owner-group reports of six-figure discounts refer to leftover pre-facelift stock and are not the normal transaction. On-road NT$45,000 = 領牌規費 and 代辦 (~NT$12,000, including 行照/牌照 fees and agent handling) plus a typical accessory pack (~NT$33,000: 隔熱紙 for a coupe's large glass area, 行車紀錄器, mats, 車美仕 protection). Proportionally lighter than a luxury saloon because Toyota's accessory catalogue is cheaper. Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 1,740,000 - 30,000 + 45,000 = 1,755,000.

selling_costs.notes: 過戶 statutory fees are genuinely small — 行照費 NT$200 plus 驗車費 NT$450 — but a private seller almost always pays an agent NT$2,000-2,500 to handle the monitor-office paperwork, so NT$3,000 all-in. 售前整備 NT$6,500 is set above the sedan norm on purpose: on a two-door sports car, paint condition, wheel-lip rash and kerbed 18-inch rims visibly move the private-sale price, so polish plus interior plus wheel refurbishment is money that pays for itself. 刊登費 NT$1,500: CORRECTED NOTE IN REVIEW — I re-read 8891's fee schedule (8891.com.tw/help-b_1_1.html, verified) and for an individual seller 寄售 is FREE for 60 days with up to 12 photos, capped at 2 concurrent listings; only the 出售汽車 product costs 400 points for 60 days. So the true floor for a private seller is NT$0, not a few hundred as the original record implied. The NT$1,500 is retained purely as a budget for cross-posting to a second platform and relisting, since niche sports coupes take longer to sell than a Corolla — it is a discretionary spend, not a required fee. Total NT$11,000 sits at the upper-middle of the usual NT$4,000-15,000 band, which is where a sports coupe belongs.

value_checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN IN REVIEW (was NT$1,350,000 / NT$1,170,000). The original record set year-1 DEALER RETAIL at ~NT$1,500,000, which is above every listing actually visible on 8891 — the dealer-retail trap re-entering through an inflated anchor. Live 8891 data I re-pulled myself (auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/gr86): the best like-for-like comparable is a 2024-MY 6AT Brembo, 7,500 km, Yilan, asking NT$1,460,000 車商售價, alongside a 2024-MY 6AT non-Brembo at 10,000 km asking NT$1,428,000 and two 2024-MY 6MT Brembo cars at NT$1,428,000. Separately, the only genuine ~1-year-old car found is a 2025-MY at NT$1,380,000 (Taoyuan dealer 六順國際車業, auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4446903.html) — spec and mileage not stated, and it sits BELOW the 2024 cars, so the pool is noisy and asking prices are not cleanly ordered by age. I set DEALER RETAIL at NT$1,480,000, just above the top real comparable rather than NT$40,000 above it. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = retail x 0.888 (NT$1,315,000, i.e. 11% below dealer asking, inside the 8-15% band); dealer_tradein = private x 0.863 (NT$1,135,000, a further 13.7%), the gap set slightly wide because dealers hold niche two-door stock longer and price that carrying risk into the buy. Low-mileage basis: 7,000 km at one year, and all listings quoted are themselves low-mileage cars.

SOURCE CORRECTED AND CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED IN REVIEW (values unchanged). The original record claimed 'five real 2023-MY GR86 listings' and rated this the best-evidenced row at high confidence. I re-pulled auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/gr86 and there are only SEVEN GR86 listings in total, of which exactly TWO are 2023-MY: NT$1,398,000 at 10,000 km (6MT Brembo, Yunlin) and NT$1,240,000 at 37,000 km (6MT, Taoyuan, dealer 冠豪汽車). The other four cars the original record counted as 2023-MY (NT$1,428,000 at 10,000 km, NT$1,428,000 at 8,479 km, NT$1,460,000 at 7,500 km, NT$1,428,000 at 8,000 km) are all 2024-MY — two years old, not three. Interpolating the two genuine 3-year anchors to our 21,000 km gives DEALER RETAIL of ~NT$1,335,000, which happens to land where the original record put it, so the numbers stand. Note both 3-year anchors are 6MT while this record prices the 6AT. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = retail x 0.903 (NT$1,205,000, 9.7% below dealer asking); dealer_tradein = private x 0.867 (NT$1,045,000). Confidence high -> medium: two real listings straddling the target mileage, not five, and neither is the right transmission.

EXTRAPOLATED ONE YEAR beyond real data; values unchanged in review, reasoning corrected and one dead source removed. The GR86 launched in Taiwan in Aug 2022, so the oldest cars trading today are 2022-MY at four years old — a genuine five-year GR86 does not yet exist here. Real four-year anchors that I re-verified: auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-3798120.html NT$1,398,000 (2022-MY, Taipei dealer 任昱汽車) and auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4057885.html NT$1,330,000 (2022-MY, Taipei); carmaxtw.com/used-toyota-gr86-price/ independently puts 2022-2023 AT cars at NT$1,300,000-1,450,000 and MT at NT$1,350,000-1,500,000. REMOVED IN REVIEW: the original record's fourth anchor, sum.com.tw/carinfo-767532.php at NT$1,380,000, returns HTTP 404 — it cannot be verified and is no longer cited. Credible four-year retail band NT$1,300,000-1,400,000, centre ~NT$1,350,000. I extended one year to a DEALER RETAIL of ~NT$1,180,000, a steeper step than the flat 2022-2024 asking curve implies. REASON RESTATED (the original justification, an ongoing ~11% new-price ramp, is factually wrong — see purchase.notes): the steepening is instead justified by three things — (a) the 2023 repricing that lifted the range is a one-off already absorbed, so no further tailwind is coming; (b) every visible listing is an ultra-low-mileage garage queen at roughly 2,000-3,500 km/yr, a selection bias that inflates the observable band relative to our 7,000 km/yr car; (c) asking prices are not transactions, and scarce-segment stock sits on lots for months. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = retail x 0.898 (NT$1,060,000); dealer_tradein = private x 0.863 (NT$915,000).

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION — the current GR86 (ZN8) is only four years old in Taiwan, so no genuine seven-year data exists and none has been invented. Method, stated explicitly: I took the previous-generation Toyota 86 (ZN6) at seven years old from real 8891 listings (auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/86, 49 cars, re-verified in review), where a 2019-MY 86 at 70,000 km asks NT$860,000 dealer retail (Yunlin, 6MT). That car's original TW list was ~NT$1,270,000 (2017 facelift opened at NT$1,230,000 起; the 2012 range was NT$1,229,000 / 1,269,000 / 1,299,000). Retention = 860,000 / 1,270,000 = 67.7% of original list. I adjusted that UP to ~71% for mileage, since our car has 49,000 km versus that listing's 70,000 km, then DOWN by a factor of 0.90 to ~61%, because a NT$1.75M car depreciates faster in percentage terms in Taiwan than a NT$1.27M one. Applied to real_cost NT$1,755,000 that gives a DEALER RETAIL of ~NT$1,070,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = retail x 0.893 (NT$955,000); dealer_tradein = private x 0.859 (NT$820,000). Confidence low: the anchor is a single predecessor listing from the same Yunlin dealer that also posts the segment's other outlier asking price, plus two judgement-based corrections and a nameplate change in between.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION, same method as the 7-year row and equally not real GR86 data. Values unchanged in review; the supporting characterisation corrected. Ten-year-ish anchors from the ZN6 86 on 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/86): a 2016-MY at 58,000 km asks NT$683,000 (= 53.8% of its ~NT$1,269,000 list) and a 2017-MY at 50,000 km asks NT$880,000 (= 71.5% of ~NT$1,230,000). CORRECTION MADE IN REVIEW: the original record described the ZN6 curve as 'unusually FLAT' with ten-year-old 86s fetching NT$650,000-880,000, and implied its own numbers were therefore biased low. That was cherry-picked. The same 49-listing page also shows a 2015-MY at 67,000 km asking NT$486,000, a 2013-MY at 33,000 km asking NT$490,000, a 2013-MY at 30,000 km asking NT$318,000 and a 2012-MY at 75,000 km asking NT$698,000 — a true spread of roughly 26-72% of original list at this age, not 54-72%, and a central tendency nearer 45-55% than the 57% the original record used. The NT$650,000-880,000 pair are the top of a very noisy distribution, largely from one optimistic Yunlin dealer. I have kept the original figures because the record already shaded its 57% down to ~48.5%, which lands inside the corrected central band; that gives a DEALER RETAIL of ~NT$851,000 on real_cost NT$1,755,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = retail x 0.893 (NT$760,000); dealer_tradein = private x 0.855 (NT$650,000). The steeper 7-to-10-year step versus the 5-to-7-year step is intentional: it is the out-of-warranty cliff, where mainstream buyers discount for repair risk on an ageing boxer.

maintenance.plan_notes: Toyota Taiwan runs three service packages (toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx, verified in review): T30 every 6 months or 10,000 km (oil, oil filter, drain plug gasket, 30-point check); T50 in odd years or every 40,000 km from 20,000 km (adds air filter and spark plugs, 50-point); T60 in even years or every 40,000 km from 40,000 km (adds brake fluid, coolant and fuel filter, 60-point). At 7,000 km/yr this schedule is entirely TIME-DRIVEN — the calendar trigger always fires first and the car never reaches a single mileage-based interval in ten years. The owner therefore pays for roughly two visits a year, alternating a plain T30 with whichever of T50/T60 the year parity calls for. There is NO free scheduled-maintenance programme comparable to Volvo TW's: the official page confirms only a free one-month check and a free six-month (or 10,000 km) check for new buyers, which is why year 1 is so cheap. Factory warranty is 3 years / 100,000 km — time-limited here, so it lapses at year 3 with only ~21,000 km covered and years 3-10 carry full repair exposure. Three GR86-specific cost drivers run through every period: the FA24 flat-four holds ~5.6 L of 0W-20, so a routine oil service is dear by Toyota standards; the Brembo package roughly doubles brake consumable cost against the standard car; and boxer engines are awkward to work on, with plugs and gaskets carrying heavy labour. UNIT-COST SOURCE CORRECTED IN REVIEW: the 86-club TW price list (86-club.tw/forum.php?mod=viewthread&tid=3336) quotes a T30 package at NT$4,425, not NT$4,590, and although the thread was opened in 2013 its title records a 2024-01-11 update — so it is far more current than the original record's 'dated, 2013 origin' description and needs much less uprating than was claimed. Other figures confirmed: oil filter NT$460, brake fluid NT$452, front pads NT$7,000, rear pads NT$5,350 (all standard non-Brembo 86). MONOTONICITY FIXED IN REVIEW: the original record had year 7 (NT$68,000) costing LESS than year 5 (NT$73,000). The automatic-transmission fluid service has been moved from the 7-10 year window into the 5-7 year window, where it actually falls due on both time and the ~49,000 km reading, and the out-of-warranty allowance raised; a second ATF service is not due by 70,000 km, so year 10 drops it. Period costs below are PER-WINDOW, not cumulative, and now rise monotonically: 5,500 / 30,000 / 73,000 / 78,000 / 142,000, totalling ~NT$328,500 over ten years (~NT$33,000/yr). Tyres are included as consumables (a set roughly every 5-6 years at this mileage, since they age out before they wear out); tax, insurance and fuel are excluded throughout.

Cost from 86-club.tw/forum.php?mod=viewthread&tid=3336, verified in review: T30 package NT$4,425, oil filter NT$460, drain gasket NT$60, with the price list carrying a 2024-01-11 update. Uprated modestly to ~NT$5,000 for the FA24's larger ~5.6 L fill, plus wipers and fluids. Time-driven, not mileage-driven: the car reaches only 7,000 km, well short of the 10,000 km trigger. Cheapest window by far because Toyota TW covers the 1-month and 6-month visits.

checkpoints.source: Schedule verified on toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx (T50 odd years, T60 even years at this mileage). checkpoints.source: REVISED UP IN REVIEW from NT$68,000, which sat below the year-5 figure and broke the requirement that maintenance cost generally rise with age. The AT fluid service has been moved here from the 7-10 year window — it falls due around 7 years / 49,000 km, and a second one is not needed by 70,000 km — and the out-of-warranty allowance lifted from NT$15,000 to NT$16,000. Tyres are NOT repeated here; the year-5 set is still in date.

front Brembo discs and pads ~NT$30,000 — Brembo rotors are the single most expensive routine part on this car
water pump, thermostat, hoses and belt at 8-10 years ~NT$18,000

checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN IN REVIEW from NT$148,000: the automatic transmission fluid service has been moved into the 5-7 year window where it actually falls due, so it is no longer double-counted here. Service cadence from the verified toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx; tyre pricing as per the year-5 row; brake costs scaled ~2x from the 86-club.tw standard-86 list for the Brembo package, which is inference rather than a quoted Brembo price. HONEST CAVEAT — this is the least evidenced row in the record: the GR86 has existed in Taiwan for four years, so every figure here is a forward projection of what a 10-year-old, out-of-warranty, Brembo-equipped boxer coupe costs, not observed data. Roughly NT$47,000/yr across this window is high for a Toyota but appropriate for a sports model where brakes, tyres and dampers are all premium parts and all age out rather than wear out at 7,000 km/yr. A meaningful share (discs, dampers) could be deferred by an owner willing to accept degraded performance, so treat this as an upper-middle estimate.

assumptions.notes: 買家年行駛 6,000-8,000 km，遠低於台灣平均 12,000-15,000 km。各檢查點一律以 7,000 km/年計（7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km）。此低里程假設對兩邊都有影響：(1) 殘值端，低里程車賣得比「不看里程的平均行情」高，所以本表所有殘值都刻意引用低里程實例，並在 source 說明；(2) 保養端，Toyota 台灣官方定保是「每半年或 1 萬公里，以先到者為準」（官網原文「建議您愛車每半年或 1 萬公里回廠進行定期保養」），在 7,000 km/年之下 10 年全期都由『時間』觸發、不是里程 —— 一年固定兩次進廠、10 年約 20 次，跟開多少完全無關。原廠保固 3 年／10 萬公里，同樣是時間先到，第 3 年就出保（屆時里程僅 21,000 km，離 10 萬公里還很遠），所以第 5、7、10 年都必須編列出保後的自費風險。此車為純汽油（1.6L 三缸渦輪 G16E-GTS + GR-FOUR 四驅），無充電樁等 BEV 相關成本。依規定，牌照稅、燃料稅與任何保險（強制險、車體險）全部排除在本記錄之外。

purchase.source: https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/GR_YARIS/ — 由 fact-check 端獨立重新讀取（2026-08-12），官網現列 GR YARIS AT NT$1,990,000、GR YARIS MT NT$1,950,000，規格頁註記「2026年5月起生產」。與原研究者的 1,990,000 一致，差異 0%，故不修改。另以 DuckDuckGo 檢索交叉確認 AT 版 2025-09-23 上市價 199 萬、同日手排由 205 萬調降為 195 萬（Mobile01／U-CAR／SiCAR 標題與摘要一致）。

selling_costs.notes: 以自售（私下賣給個人）情境估算，對應 value_checkpoints 的 private_sale_price。美容整備抓 8,000 偏高，原因是這是性能車、買家會細看漆面與輪圈，整備到位與否直接影響成交價；一般家庭房車抓 4,000-5,000 即可。若改走車商收購（dealer_tradein_price），過戶與刊登由車商處理，賣方這 12,500 幾乎可省下 —— 這是收購價雖低但仍有人選的原因之一。

value_checkpoints.source: 8891 中古車 GR Yaris 車系頁（https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/gr-yaris）由 fact-check 端於 2026-08-12 獨立重新讀取，全頁 16 筆。同款 AT、同年式（2026）低里程實例三筆【車商售價】：NT$1,798,000（2,000 km，桃園）、NT$1,750,000（800 km，基隆）、NT$1,698,000（2,000 km，台中），中位數 1,750,000；另有 2026 AT 2,300 km（台北）與 2025 AT 6,000 km（苗栗）標「電洽」無價可用。本檔設定 1 年 7,000 km，比這些近全新車再多用一些，但仍遠低於台灣同齡平均（12,000-15,000 km），故車商售價僅小幅下修至 1,700,000。價格鏈調整（本表核心）：車商售價 1,700,000 → 自售 -11% = 1,510,000 → 車商收購 -12% = 1,330,000。已確認引用值不是直接抄車商開價（1,510,000 較觀察到的車商開價中位數低 13.7%，落在合理的 8-15% 區間內）。同變速箱、同年式、多筆實掛牌照價且經二次獨立讀取，故 high。

同 8891 車系頁（2026-08-12 重新讀取）的第一代實例【車商售價】：2023年式（3 年）28,000 km NT$1,398,000（彰化）、2022年式（4 年）18,700 km NT$1,380,000（新竹）、2022年式 24,000 km NT$1,320,000（台中）、2022年式 31,000 km NT$1,298,000（台北）。該世代原始定價 NT$1,790,000（2021-08 上市，首批配額 80 台；已用 DuckDuckGo 檢索交叉確認「正式售價179萬元」「首批配額增至80輛」），故 3 年車商售價保值率約 78.1%、4 年約 72.5-77.1%。本車里程更低（21,000 km，低於該 3 年實例的 28,000 km）本應加分，但 AT 版的在台配額數量未知、可能比第一代首批 80 台寬鬆，未來在市車源會較多，兩者抵銷後保守取 77%：1,990,000 × 77% ≈ 車商售價 1,530,000。再 -11% 得自售 1,360,000，-12.5% 得車商收購 1,190,000。資料點為同車系但跨變速箱、跨世代代用，故 medium。

8891 車系頁上唯一一筆 5 年期實例（2026-08-12 重新讀取確認）：2021年式 6MT、19,000 km，【車商售價】NT$1,298,000（台北），對原始定價 1,790,000 為 72.5%（另一筆 2021年式 13,000 km 標「電洽」，無價可用）。本車設定 35,000 km，里程高於該實例，且 AT 版在市量預期較大，下修至 69%：1,990,000 × 69% ≈ 車商售價 1,370,000。再 -11.5% 得自售 1,210,000，-13% 得車商收購 1,050,000。註：本車 35,000 km 相對台灣同齡平均（約 60,000-75,000 km）仍屬低里程，69% 已是保守取值。同齡實例僅一筆、且為手排版，故 medium 而非 high。

外推，非實測。GR Yaris 2021-08 才在台上市，2026-08 全市場最老僅 5 年，7 年車不存在，AT 版更是不到 1 年 —— 沒有任何真實成交可引用。【本次 fact-check 修正】原研究者直接把 Toyota 86 的『絕對保值率』（7-8 年 53-57%）套到 GR Yaris 並取上緣 57%，但這忽略了兩車保值水準的落差：GR Yaris 自己在第 5 年的實測車商售價保值率是 72.5%，而 86 在第 7 年才約 57%，GR Yaris 整條曲線明顯高於 86。若照原做法，本車要在第 5→7 年這兩年內從 72.5% 崩到 57%（掉 15.5 個百分點），之後三年只再掉 12 個百分點，曲線形狀自相矛盾。改採：以本車自己實測的第 5 年 72.5% 為錨，套用性能車第 5 年後跌幅趨緩的形狀，第 7 年取 60% 車商售價保值率（仍高於 86 同齡的約 57%，反映 WRC 同源配額限量車的稀有度溢價）。1,990,000 × 60% ≈ 車商售價 1,195,000，再 -13% 得自售 1,040,000，-14% 得車商收購 895,000。代用車佐證：8891 Toyota 86 車系頁（https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/86，2026-08-12 讀取，共 49 筆）2016-2019 年式【車商售價】NT$683,000-880,000，其中 2019 年式 NT$860,000。註：86 的 2017 小改款定價（約 1,499,000）查無可靠來源、本次亦未能驗證，故本點刻意降低對 86 絕對百分比的依賴，改以本車自身曲線外推。純外推，故 low。

外推，非實測，理由同第 7 年。【本次 fact-check 修正，本記錄最大的一處錯誤】原研究者在第 7 年把 GR Yaris 調到 86 區間的『上緣』（57%，理由是 GR 稀有度加分），卻在第 10 年調到 86 區間的『下方』（45%，理由是渦輪四驅維修風險與絕對價位）—— 同樣兩個理由、沒有任何新證據，卻在相鄰兩個檢查點得到相反方向的結論，這是方法上的矛盾。且 45% 低於代用車 86 同齡實測：8891 Toyota 86 車系頁 2016 年式（10 年）【車商售價】NT$683,000 起、區間至 NT$880,000，對 2012 上市價 1,229,000-1,299,000 約 53-68%；86 是大量販售車，GR Yaris 是配額限量的 WRC 同源車，沒有理由跌得比 86 還兇。改採 50% 車商售價保值率：1,990,000 × 50% ≈ 車商售價 995,000，再 -14% 得自售 855,000，-15% 得車商收購 725,000。取 50%（低於 86 的 53-68%）已保留兩項下修因素：1.6 渦輪 + GR-FOUR 出保後的維修風險與零件成本高於自然進氣後驅的 86；且原始定價 1,990,000 使 10 年後的絕對價位仍偏高，在台灣二手市場屬買家池較小的價帶。曲線檢查：第 5→7 年每年約 -85,000、第 7→10 年每年約 -62,000，跌幅隨車齡趨緩，符合性能車價格觸底的一般型態。純外推，故 low。

maintenance.plan_notes:
間隔屬性（最關鍵的一點）：Toyota 台灣官方定保為「每半年或 1 萬公里，以先到者為準」（https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx，由 fact-check 端於 2026-08-12 獨立讀取確認，官網原文「建議您愛車每半年或 1 萬公里回廠進行定期保養」）。本買家 7,000 km/年，10 年全期都是【時間觸發】而非里程觸發 —— 一年固定進廠兩次、10 年約 20 次。這代表低里程並不會等比省下保養費，只會讓每次保養的更換項目較單純。

套餐內容（官方頁面已驗證）：T30 = 機油 + 機油濾清器 + 放油塞墊片 + 30 項以上檢查（每半年或 1 萬公里）；T50 = 加空氣濾芯、火星塞等定期更換件，50 項以上檢查（每 1 年或 4 萬公里）；T60 = 加冷氣濾網、煞車油、引擎冷卻液、燃油濾清器，60 項以上檢查（每 2 年或 4 萬公里）。注意：本買家在時間觸發下，每 1 年會落在 T50、每 2 年會落在 T60，但因里程極低（4 萬公里要 5.7 年才到），實務上多數里程驅動的更換件會被服務廠順延，故本表以「T30 級距為主、每 2 年一次較大級距」估算，屬保守簡化。

單次價位：Mobile01 車主回報一般 Toyota 原廠基本定保約 NT$1,500-2,900（自備機油可更低）。GR Yaris 的 G16E-GTS 是 1.6 渦輪三缸，機油量與工料成本較高、且需送具 GR 認證能力的服務據點，故本表 T30 級距抓 NT$4,000/次、較大級距抓 NT$10,000-12,000/次。此為推估值非實際單據，是保養各點只給 medium／low 的主因。

保固與出保：原廠保固 3 年／10 萬公里，7,000 km/年之下是「3 年時間先到」，第 3 年就出保，屆時里程僅 21,000 km。因此第 1、3 年的 period_cost 只有定保與耗材，第 5、7、10 年才開始編列出保後自費風險。

免費保養：查無 GR Yaris 有任何免費定期保養方案。Toyota 台灣沒有像 Volvo 那樣的免費保養專案，僅新車首次檢查免費，本表不做任何免費保養折抵（偏保守）。

低里程的耗材特性：在 7,000 km/年之下，輪胎是「橡膠老化到期」而非「磨到底」，約 5-6 年就必須換一套（第 5 年與第 10 年各一套），這是低里程車主常低估的一筆。

【本次 fact-check 修正】原記錄第 3、7、10 年的 major_items 金額加總與 period_cost 對不上（分別差 2,000 / 1,000 / 2,000）。已逐點調整為完全對帳。

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; all checkpoints use 7,000 km/yr (7000/21000/35000/49000/70000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/yr. That matters twice over. (1) Servicing is almost entirely TIME-driven: Toyota TW's official table triggers T30 either every 6 months by age OR, for SUPRA specifically, at 12,000 km then every 24,000 km. At 7,000 km/yr the 12,000 km mark arrives at ~1.7 yr, T50 (24,000 km) at ~3.4 yr, T60 (48,000 km) at ~6.9 yr, so the calendar clock fires far more often than the odometer. (2) Consumables age out rather than wear out: the staggered Michelin PS4S 255/35R19 front / 275/35R19 rear set is replaced on rubber hardening at ~5-6 years, not on tread depth. Toyota TW warranty is 3 years / 100,000 km, so this buyer is time-limited: cover expires at year 3 with only ~21,000 km on the car, and every year after carries full parts risk on the BMW-sourced B58 engine and ZF 8HP gearbox. Tax (牌照稅/燃料稅) and insurance are excluded from this record by design. A90 production ended March 2026 (verified), so this is a final-year car; that is a mild support for residuals but it is a forecast about the 2033-2036 market, not an observed fact, and this record deliberately gives it only modest weight in the year-10 figure.

purchase.source: Official list price independently re-verified on Toyota Taiwan's own showroom page (https://www.toyota.com.tw/showroom/SUPRA/), which lists three trims: 3.0T Premium MT NT$2,660,000, 3.0T Premium AT NT$2,690,000, 3.0T Track Edition NT$2,800,000. The NT$2,690,000 figure for 3.0T Premium AT is CONFIRMED — no correction needed (0% variance). Discount and on-road figures are realistic-transaction estimates, not published numbers.
purchase.notes: list_price NT$2,690,000 is 和泰/Toyota TW's 建議售價 for the 3.0T Premium AT, confirmed on the official showroom page by direct fetch. The showroom spec table is footnoted 「2025/3月起生產之SUPRA車輛規格配備」, which covers both 2025 and 2026 production; A90 production ended March 2026, so remaining new stock is the final model year and 2026 is the correct label. discounts NT$40,000: Toyota TW does commonly discount, but mainstream Toyota cash discounts (NT$100,000+ on a Corolla Cross or RAV4) do NOT apply to the GR Supra — it is a halo, low-volume, allocation-limited model in its final production year, so dealers have no incentive to cut price. Realistic give is a modest cash-equivalent of NT$30,000-60,000, usually delivered as 領牌禮/配件 rather than cash off the invoice; NT$40,000 used. onroad_fees NT$60,000 = 領牌+代辦 ~NT$13,000 plus 配件 ~NT$47,000 (paint protection film or coating, window film, dashcam, mats — the realistic delivery-day accessory spend on a NT$2.69M sports car). Fees scale with vehicle class, which is why this sits well above the NT$20,000-30,000 typical of a NT$800,000 hatchback. Tax and insurance are EXCLUDED by design. real_cost = 2,690,000 - 40,000 + 60,000 = NT$2,710,000.

items.name: 過戶費 (title transfer, incl. 代辦)
售前整備/美容 (pre-sale prep, paint correction, detailing)
刊登費 (8891 / SUM featured listing)

selling_costs.notes: Top of the NT$4,000-15,000 band because of vehicle class. On a NT$1.5-2M sports car sold privately, presentation directly moves the price — buyers at this level inspect paint and wheels closely, so a proper detail and paint correction (NT$10,500) pays for itself. 過戶費 is the regulatory transfer fee plus 代辦 handling. 刊登費 reflects a paid featured listing; the Taiwan Supra market is verified thin (8891 shows 6 cars nationwide, SUM shows 2), so a private seller needs visible placement to find the buyer at all.

value_checkpoints.source: Back-extrapolated one year from verified 8891 listings (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/gr-supra), re-read directly: a 2024 3.0T AT with 3,900 km asks NT$2,198,000 (2 years old, ~85% of its ~NT$2,580,000 original list), and the 2023 cluster sits at NT$2,040,000-2,060,000 (3 years old, ~81%). Stepping one year back gives a 1-year dealer RETAIL ask of ~NT$2,340,000 (87% of list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: that is 車商售價, not what an owner receives — cut 12% to reach 自售價 NT$2,060,000, then a further 13% to reach 車商收購價 NT$1,790,000. Upper end of the 8-15% dealer-retail-to-private band used because the Taiwan Supra market is extremely thin, so asks are unusually padded and cars sit for months. The 2024 comparator is a genuinely low-mileage AT car (3,900 km), matching this buyer's 7,000 km profile and the same transmission as this record.

Four genuine 3-year-old (2023 MY) cars on 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/toyota/gr-supra), mileages re-read directly from the page: 17,900 km / NT$2,060,000 (Hsinchu), 6,400 km / NT$2,040,000 (Taipei), 18,000 km / NT$2,058,000 (Tainan), and 2,686 km / NT$2,280,000 (Taipei). This buyer's car is at 21,000 km at year 3, so the correct comparators are the 17,900 km and 18,000 km cars, which cluster tightly at NT$2,058,000-2,060,000; the 2,686 km car at NT$2,280,000 is excluded as a much-lower-mileage outlier rather than as an aspirational one. Against the 2023 3.0T Premium MT list of NT$2,550,000 (verified) that is a dealer ask-to-list ratio of ~81% at 3 years. Applying 81% to this car's NT$2,690,000 list gives a dealer ask of ~NT$2,179,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: -12% to private sale NT$1,920,000, then -13% to dealer trade-in NT$1,670,000. Ratio normalisation rather than raw cash comparison, because the 3.0T Premium's Taiwan list has risen from NT$2,480,000 (2019) to NT$2,690,000 (2026). CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: all four comparators are MT cars while this record is the AT, and these are asking prices rather than transactions — hence medium, not high.

One verifiable 5-year-old (2021 MY) listing: NT$1,768,000 dealer ask in Taipei (明龍汽車) at https://auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-3952542.html, mileage not disclosed on the page. Against a 2021 3.0T Premium list of ~NT$2,480,000 that is a ~71% ask-to-list ratio. I adjusted up to 73% to credit this buyer's genuinely low 35,000 km, since the comparator's mileage is unknown and could be anything. 73% of NT$2,690,000 = dealer ask ~NT$1,964,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: -12% to private sale NT$1,728,000, then -13% to dealer trade-in NT$1,503,000. This is the first checkpoint fully outside Toyota TW's 3-year warranty, which weighs on buyer confidence for a BMW-engined car. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED to low: a second 2021 data point at NT$1,958,000 attributed to 小老婆車庫 could not be reproduced on any page I fetched, and that figure is identical to the unrelated 2020 Kaohsiung car's ask, so it is treated as unverifiable and excluded. This checkpoint rests on a single listing with undisclosed mileage.

The A90 launched in Taiwan in 2019 so 7-year-old cars of this generation exist, but the market is nearly empty and the only verifiable bracketing point is a 2020 3.0T AT with 94,377 km asking NT$1,958,000, confirmed on both SUM (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch.php?v=4&brand=TOYOTA&model=SUPRA) and 8891. A 6-year-old car with 94,377 km asking ~76% of its original list is a clear aspirational-ask signal on a thin market, not a transaction price. I therefore set a clean low-mileage 7-year ask-to-list at 67% — below the observed ask, stripping thin-market padding, while crediting that this buyer's car has 49,000 km rather than 94,000 km. 67% of NT$2,690,000 = dealer ask ~NT$1,802,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: -12% to private sale NT$1,586,000, then -13% to dealer trade-in NT$1,380,000. Confidence is low: this rests on one high-mileage aspirational ask. NOTE ON A REMOVED SOURCE: a 2019 3.0T AT listing asking NT$2,080,000 with 百萬改裝 was cited in the prior draft but does not appear on the 8891 Supra hub, which returns six listings none of which is a 2019 car; it is treated as unverifiable and plays no part in this figure.

EXTRAPOLATED — no genuine 10-year data can exist for the A90 (Taiwan launch 2019). The literal predecessor A80 Supra (1993-2002) is unusable: it is a 25-year-old appreciating collectible in Taiwan whose prices have risen, so its retention ratio would be nonsense. I used the BMW Z4 E89 instead — same two-seat premium sports segment, same era, and direct predecessor of the G29 Z4 that is this Supra's platform twin. Verified Taiwan data (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch.php?v=4&brand=BMW&model=Z4): a 2013 sDrive28i with 102,686 km asks NT$738,000 and a 2011 sDrive20i with 147,721 km asks NT$588,000; against an E89 sDrive28i original list of roughly NT$2,700,000 that is ~27% ask-to-list at 13 years. Interpolating back to 10 years gives ~35%. I adjusted UP to 45% for the one concrete, quantifiable reason: this car has 70,000 km against the comparators' 102,000-148,000 km, plus a modest allowance for the Supra's stronger enthusiast demand and Toyota reliability halo. I did NOT credit a last-of-the-generation collector premium — that is a forecast about the 2036 market, not evidence, and Taiwan buyers get materially more cautious past the 10-year 車齡 mark for financing and insurance reasons. 45% of NT$2,690,000 = dealer ask ~NT$1,211,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: -12% to private sale NT$1,065,000, then -13% to dealer trade-in NT$927,000. This is a reasoned extrapolation, not an observation.

maintenance.plan_notes: Toyota Taiwan publishes a T30/T50/T60 package schedule and, unusually, calls out SUPRA-specific mileage intervals in the footnotes. I re-fetched the page and confirmed the quoted text verbatim (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx): T30 「車齡：每半年實施 或 里程數：1萬、3萬、5萬等單數萬公里實施」 with the footnote 「(SIENNA車型為8千公里起每1.6萬公里實施/SUPRA車型為1.2萬公里起每2.4萬公里實施)」; T50 「SUPRA車型為2.4萬公里起每4.8萬公里實施」; T60 「SUPRA車型為4.8萬公里起每4.8萬公里實施」. The Supra's BMW-derived intervals are much longer than a normal Toyota's. WHICH TRIGGER APPLIES HERE: at 7,000 km/yr this is overwhelmingly TIME-driven. The book's 每半年 T30 fires twice a year from day one, while the odometer triggers are sparse — 12,000 km at ~1.7 yr, T50 at ~3.4 yr, T60 at ~6.9 yr, 60,000 km at ~8.6 yr. I modelled roughly annual-to-semiannual T30s (what low-mileage owners actually do while staying warranty-compliant) plus mileage-triggered T50/T60 where the arithmetic lands them, plus brake fluid on an independent 2-year clock since its mileage trigger essentially never arrives. NO FREE MAINTENANCE PROGRAMME: Toyota TW gives only the complimentary 1-month and 10,000 km new-car INSPECTIONS — these are checks, not oil-change packages, and there is no Volvo-style multi-year included-servicing plan, so every service below is paid. Warranty is 3 years / 100,000 km, so this buyer loses cover at year 3 on the time clock with the car barely run in at ~21,000 km; the year-7 and year-10 windows therefore carry explicit out-of-warranty risk provisions. Cost note: although the badge is Toyota, the mechanicals are BMW — B58 3.0 turbo six (~7L of premium synthetic, six spark plugs) and a ZF 8HP gearbox — so parts and labour sit far above mainstream Toyota rates. Toyota TW publishes NO Supra service prices (the page states 「如欲獲得保養套餐內容與價格費用之詳細資訊，請洽 TOYOTA 全台服務廠」), so every per-item cost below is an estimate anchored on the official schedule structure and known Toyota TW package pricing for larger models (a RAV4 Hybrid T30 runs ~NT$8,585). Treat the maintenance totals as a modelled range, not sourced prices.

major_items: Complimentary 1-month new-car inspection (free)
One paid T30: engine oil, oil filter, drain plug gasket, 30-point inspection (~NT$8,000 — B58 takes ~7L of premium synthetic)
Wipers and sundries (~NT$2,000)
checkpoints.source: Official Toyota TW schedule (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx) for interval structure, re-verified by direct fetch. Cost anchored on published Toyota TW T30 package pricing for larger models (RAV4 Hybrid T30 ~NT$8,585) and scaled for the Supra's 3.0 six-cylinder oil volume. At 7,000 km/yr the buyer never reaches the free 10,000 km inspection inside year 1, and never reaches the Supra's 12,000 km T30 mileage trigger, so this year is time-driven only. Fully in warranty, so no repair provision. Note this models one annual oil service rather than the book's strict 每半年, which is what low-mileage owners actually do; a strictly book-compliant owner would spend roughly NT$8,000 more.

major_items: Three paid T30 oil services across the 1-3y window (~NT$24,000)
Brake fluid change at year 2 on the time clock (~NT$4,000)
Free 10,000 km new-car inspection reached at ~1.4 yr (inspection only, no oil — NT$0)
Wipers, cabin filter, sundries (~NT$4,000)
checkpoints.source: Official Toyota TW T30 schedule and the SUPRA mileage footnote (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx). Time-driven period: the book calls for T30 每半年, and I modelled three paid services across the two-year window rather than four, which is what low-mileage owners realistically do while keeping warranty compliance. The 12,000 km SUPRA mileage trigger also lands here (~1.7 yr) and is covered by those services. Brake fluid is added on its own 2-year clock because the Supra's T60 mileage trigger (48,000 km) does not arrive until ~6.9 yr. The complimentary 10,000 km check falls in this window but is an inspection only, so it does not displace a paid oil service. Still inside the 3-year / 100,000 km warranty, so no repair provision. Costs are estimates — Toyota TW publishes no Supra price list.

major_items: T50 at 24,000 km / ~3.4 yr: six spark plugs, air filter, cabin filter, 50-point inspection (~NT$23,000)
Two to three T30 oil services (~NT$20,000)
Brake fluid at year 4 (~NT$4,000)
12V AGM battery, BMW-sourced and needs coding (~NT$10,000)
FIRST TYRE SET — Michelin PS4S 255/35R19 front + 275/35R19 rear, replaced on age not tread (~NT$40,000 fitted)
Alignment and sundries (~NT$5,000)
checkpoints.source: Interval structure from the official Toyota TW SUPRA footnote — the 24,000 km T50 lands at ~3.4 yr at 7,000 km/yr (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx). Tyre cost verified against Taiwan retail pricing for Michelin PS4S 255/35R19 at NT$7,600-8,800 per tyre with four-tyre bundles at NT$37,152-38,959 (https://biggo.com.tw/s/ps4s%20255-35-19); the wider 275/35R19 rears price higher, giving ~NT$35,000 for the staggered set plus ~NT$5,000 fitting, balancing and alignment. The tyres are replaced here because at 7,000 km/yr the compound hardens and ages out at 5-6 years long before the tread wears — a mileage-blind model would wrongly skip this. Warranty expires at year 3, so the back half of this window is at the owner's cost. Service prices are estimates, not a published list.

major_items: T60 at 48,000 km / ~6.9 yr: engine coolant, brake fluid, fuel filter, 60-point inspection (~NT$28,000)
Two to three T30 oil services (~NT$20,000)
Front brake pads and discs, replaced as a set at a GR dealer (~NT$40,000)
Out-of-warranty risk provision — B58 thermostat, coolant hoses, valve cover gasket or an ignition coil are the common 6-7 year items (~NT$25,000)
Sundries (~NT$5,000)
checkpoints.source: T60 timing from the official Toyota TW SUPRA footnote (48,000 km, reached at ~6.9 yr at 7,000 km/yr) — https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx. Fully out of warranty for this entire window (cover ended at year 3 on the time clock), which is why an explicit repair provision is included rather than assuming nothing breaks. Brake pads and discs are time-and-heat driven on a 250kW+ sports car even at low mileage, and Toyota TW GR dealers typically replace discs with pads rather than machining them. The risk provision is an estimate based on well-documented B58 wear items, not a Taiwan price list — no such list is published for the Supra.

major_items: Roughly five T30 oil services across three years, incl. the 60,000 km trigger at ~8.6 yr (~NT$40,000)
SECOND TYRE SET — staggered PS4S, again replaced on age at ~year 10 (~NT$40,000 fitted)
ZF 8HP transmission service: fluid, pan and filter (~NT$20,000) — BMW calls it lifetime fill, owners do not
Second 12V AGM battery with coding (~NT$10,000)
Rear brake pads and discs (~NT$30,000)
Out-of-warranty risk provision — water pump, thermostat, VANOS solenoids, oil filter housing gasket, suspension bushes, or one adaptive damper (~NT$60,000)
Cabin filters, wipers, sundries (~NT$8,000)
checkpoints.source: Extrapolated. The 60,000 km T30 trigger at ~8.6 yr comes from the official Toyota TW SUPRA footnote (https://www.toyota.com.tw/owner_maintenance.aspx); everything else is an estimated consumable-replacement and risk schedule for a 7-10 year old car entirely outside warranty. Second tyre set follows the same 5-6 year age-out logic as year 5, priced from verified Taiwan retail (https://biggo.com.tw/s/ps4s%20255-35-19). The ZF 8HP service is included because the A90 owner community widely does it around 80,000 km or 8-10 years despite BMW's lifetime-fill claim. The NT$60,000 risk provision reflects that this is a BMW powertrain in its second decade with no warranty and dealer-level parts pricing. Sanity check: 10-year maintenance totals ~NT$470,000 (~NT$47,000/yr) — high for a Toyota, normal for a BMW-engined sports car on staggered performance tyres. No owner receipts with NT$ figures could be found for the A90 in Taiwan, so this window is low confidence by construction.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses 7,000 km x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000), far below the TW average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. Two consequences are built into the numbers. (1) Resale: quoted against low-mileage comparables and against genuine PRIVATE listings, not against dealer asking prices. (2) Maintenance: Volvo TW's EX30 mileage-based service triggers are 30,000 and 60,000 km (verified live against the official 保養服務規劃 QueryMileage API, which returns exactly '30000@@60000'), so at 7,000 km/yr this owner reaches 30,000 km at ~year 4.3 and 60,000 km at ~year 8.6 and is on the TIME-driven schedule for essentially the whole 10 years. Consumables are therefore AGE-driven, not tread-driven: tires are replaced because rubber hardens (~every 5 years), not because they wear out. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: tax (牌照稅 is NT$0 for BEVs in TW under the current exemption anyway) and insurance. ALSO EXCLUDED: home AC charger hardware and installation, roughly NT$25,000-60,000 in TW depending on whether the building's electrical riser needs work and whether a dedicated meter (台電充電專用電表) is added. That is a real ownership cost but it is a one-off capital item, not maintenance, so it appears in neither purchase nor maintenance here — add it separately if the comparison needs it. Electricity cost is also excluded; for reference 8891 models the EX30 at 7.8 km/kWh.

purchase.source: List price re-verified independently by this audit against two live sources on 2026-08-12. (1) 8891 新車's embedded trim JSON returns three EX30 records with modelName/price pairs: 'Core Single Motor Extended Range' 139.9, 'Plus Single Motor Extended Range' 159.99, 'Ultra Twin Motor Performance' 174.99 (萬). (2) KingAutos' Volvo price list independently shows the EX30 Ultra at 174.99萬. NT$1,599,900 for the Plus is CONFIRMED — no change, well inside the 3% tolerance. Discount estimated from Volvo TW's official August 2026 購車方案 page plus market context (see notes); on-road fees are a standard TW build-up scaled to a ~1.6M premium car.
purchase.notes: Full official TW trim name is 'Single Extended Range Plus' (26 chars, over the 25-char display limit); shortened to 'Extended Range Plus' (19 chars), which keeps the official word order. Spec: 69 kWh NCM pack, 400V, RWD single motor, 272 hp, 595 km NEDC, 153 kW DC peak, PMA2 platform, 19-inch wheels (8891's official trim spec table lists 輪圈規格 18吋 for Core and 19吋 for Plus and Ultra — this matters for tire cost, see maintenance). The single-motor Core/Plus trims launched in Taiwan on 2025-08-04 (the Ultra came first, Feb 2025), so this car has been on sale here for almost exactly one year. DISCOUNTS (NT$70,000, ~4.4% of list — medium confidence, part judgement): Volvo TW's official monthly-offers page for August 2026 advertises the EX30 as '本月入主享 0 頭款及 超低月付 NT$15,000 起 優惠專案' — verified verbatim on 2026-08-12. That is a FINANCING subsidy, not a headline cash discount, so there is no published cash figure to cite. NT$70,000 is an estimate of the realistic negotiated cash-plus-accessory concession from a Volvo dealer, deliberately modest. Note what the same page shows for the combustion models: XC40/XC60/XC90/V60 all carry '再享政府貨物稅減徵及汰舊換新 最高 NT$100,000 補助' while the three BEVs (EX30/EC40/EX40) do NOT — because that rebate is a commodity-tax refund and BEVs pay no commodity tax. Volvo's own site confirms '建議售價已含電動車貨物稅減免' (verified verbatim on the extended-warranty page footer). So the BEV buyer cannot stack that NT$100,000; do not double-count it. Volvo TW is a genuinely discounting brand (unlike Tesla, which cuts list price instead), and the EX30 appears to be moving slowly here — one-year-old cars are already on the used market — which supports a real rather than token discount. ON-ROAD FEES (NT$45,000): 領牌+代辦 ~NT$15,000, plus ~NT$30,000 of typical delivery accessories (隔熱紙, 行車紀錄器, 踏墊, 鍍膜). No 貨物稅 and no 空污費 apply to a BEV. Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 1,599,900 - 70,000 + 45,000 = 1,574,900.
