selling_costs.notes: Costed for a PRIVATE sale, matching private_sale_price. The 監理站 transfer fee itself is trivial (行照工本費 ~200); the 1,800 covers 代辦 handling that most private sellers pay. The 8891 listing fee was verified by direct fetch on 2026-08-12: '個人刊登1筆需要400台幣，可持續曝光60天' (c.8891.com.tw/news/18339), so 1,200 covers roughly six months on market - realistic for a private EV sale. Pre-sale prep is the largest line: a premium EV needs interior detail plus paint polish/coating to hold a private-sale price, and 6,500 is a mid-range TW quote. Two Tesla-specific items to watch that are NOT in this total: a missing key card costs 5,000-8,000 to re-cut and is deducted at appraisal, and a battery State-of-Health report (via the Tesla app) is effectively mandatory paperwork for a private BEV sale - free to produce but non-optional. If sold to a dealer instead, selling costs fall to roughly zero because the dealer absorbs transfer and prep, but the price drops to dealer_tradein_price.

value_checkpoints.source: 8891 中古車 live listings (https://auto.8891.com.tw/tesla/model-3), re-harvested and re-parsed independently on 2026-08-12: 141 cars on site, 129 unique rows extracted across nine sort orders, 126 with a numeric price. REVISED DOWN from the prior draft (was 1,364,000). No 1-year-old example of THIS trim exists - it launched 2026-01, so the oldest is ~7 months - and the entire year-1 anchor is one predecessor-trim car: a 2025 後輪驅動 with 13,000 km asking 1,538,000 against its 1,699,900 list. A 2024 RWD with only 8,052 km asks 1,528,000, i.e. near-new RWD dealer asks cluster flat at 1,528,000-1,538,000 regardless of 2024 vs 2025 - evidence that the ask is set by the segment, not by age. I set the 1-year dealer ask at 1,489,000 (85.1% of list) rather than the prior 1,550,000, because a 1-year-old car competes head-on with a new one at 1,749,900 AND with the confirmed zero-tariff repricing path that electrify.tw computes at ~1,532,900 for this same trim. ADJUSTMENT MADE: 8891 numbers are 車商售價 (dealer retail asks); private_sale = dealer ask x 0.88 (12% below dealer retail) and dealer_tradein = private x 0.86 (a further 14% down), so trade-in is ~0.76 x dealer ask, consistent with the TW norm of 車商收購 at 75-80% of 車商售價. Lands at 73.5% of real_cost, just under a TW Tesla dealer's own published residual table (piopro.com.tw: 75% at 1 year of list). Confidence LOWERED to low: a single predecessor-trim listing is not a cluster.

REVISED DOWN materially from the prior draft (was 1,206,000 - the single largest correction in this record). Real low-mileage clusters re-verified on 8891 on 2026-08-12: 2024 後輪驅動 at 2 years asking 1,528,000-1,530,000 with 8,052-37,600 km against a 1,699,900 list (~90%); 2022 後輪驅動 at 4 years asking 1,288,000 with 32,000 km, 1,208,000 with 33,000 km against a 1,754,900 list (~69-73%). The prior draft interpolated these as PERCENTAGES OF LIST and landed at 78% (dealer ask 1,370,000), which produced a private figure retaining 67.7% of real_cost - higher than the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid record in this same table (61.9%) and level with a gasoline Camry (67.0%). A Tesla out-retaining a Toyota hybrid in Taiwan is not credible, and the percentage-of-list method is itself biased upward here: the 8891 data shows used Model 3 asks CONVERGING TO AN ABSOLUTE BAND at a given age irrespective of original price - at 4 years the 2022 RWD (1,754,900 list) and the 2022 Long Range AWD (2,234,000 list) both ask ~1,288,000, i.e. 73% and 58% of their respective lists. Applying a percentage to a HIGHER list therefore overstates a more expensive car. I set the 3-year dealer ask at 1,240,000 (70.9% of list), just under today's observed 4-year absolute band, because the documented repricing risk lands inside this window: 能源署 filings show a Model 3 Standard projected at 1,350,000-1,530,000, and zero tariff could cut this trim's own list to ~1,532,900. A 3-year-old car cannot retail near a brand-new cheaper Tesla. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale = dealer ask x 0.88, dealer_tradein = private x 0.86. Lands at 61.2% of real_cost (62.3% of list), matching the piopro.com.tw dealer residual table (61% at 3 years). Low-mileage throughout: at 21,000 km this car is well under the 60,000-90,000 km typical of a 3-year-old TW Model 3.

REVISED DOWN from the prior draft (was 924,000). 8891 2021 Model 3 listings at exactly 5 years old, low-mileage subset, re-verified 2026-08-12: Standard Range Plus asking 958,000 @ 50,000 km, 900,000 @ 50,000 km, 908,000 @ 96,000 km against a 1,654,900 list (~54-58%); Long Range asking 1,258,000 @ 34,000 km and 1,208,000 @ 43,000 km against a 1,972,900 list (61-64%). Our car is the ENTRY trim on the RWD/entry track, so the SR+ track is the right comparator, and the prior draft's 60% of list sat above what that track actually shows. I used a dealer ask of 960,000 (54.9% of list). ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale = dealer ask x 0.88, dealer_tradein = private x 0.86. Lands at 47.4% of real_cost (48.3% of list), essentially on the piopro.com.tw dealer table (49% at 5 years), below the RAV4 Hybrid record (54.8%) as a BEV should be, and in line with the sibling Tesla Model Y (46.8%) and Toyota bZ4X (47.3%) records. Note the 2021 sample is genuinely noisy (same year and trim spans 758,000 to 1,258,000) because 2021 Q3 is the TW TPC-to-CCS2 charge-connector split, worth 50,000-100,000 at appraisal, and because FSD (+100,000-150,000) / EAP (+50,000-80,000) ride with some cars. Our car will not carry the connector penalty, but an equivalent obsolescence step (HW4 compute, future connector or FSD-tier gating) is the most likely cause of it landing below this figure.

EXTRAPOLATED from the PREDECESSOR GENERATION and revised down from the prior draft (was 748,000). The current Highland Model 3 launched in TW only in January 2024, so no 7-year-old example of this generation exists. Used the pre-facelift 2019 Model 3, genuinely 7 years old in TW (deliveries began September 2019). 8891 listings re-verified 2026-08-12: Long Range 820,000 @ 40,000 km (against a 1,869,900 list = 44%), 858,000 @ 116,000 km, 888,000 @ 135,000 km, 788,000 @ 163,000-164,000 km; Standard Range Plus 918,000 @ 47,000 km (against a 1,559,900 list = 59%), 880,000 @ 75,000 km, 750,000 @ 129,000 km; Performance 968,000 @ 141,000 km. The striking and reproducible pattern is that 7-year-old Model 3 asks converge into an absolute 750,000-968,000 band almost regardless of original trim price or mileage - a battery-age floor effect, not proportional decay. I used a dealer ask of 780,000, inside that band and toward its lower half because the entry trim sits there. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale = dealer ask x 0.88, dealer_tradein = private x 0.86. Lands at 38.5% of real_cost, in line with the sibling Model Y record (38.6%) and above the bZ4X (34.9%), which Model 3 liquidity justifies. Value here is still supported by the battery and drive-unit warranty (8 years; at 49,000 km the 192,000 km cap is nowhere near binding), which transfers to the buyer - that support disappears one year later.

EXTRAPOLATED and revised down from the prior draft (was 510,000). No 10-year-old Model 3 exists anywhere (first global deliveries 2017, TW September 2019), so per instruction this leans on the oldest BEVs actually trading in Taiwan rather than a combustion analogue. Best available: Tesla Model S on 8891 - a 2018 75D with 66,000 km asking 998,000 against its 3,336,000 list = 29.9% at 8 years, and a 2017 75D with 236,000 km asking 958,000 against its 3,309,000 list = 29.0% at 9 years. The prior draft applied a dealer ask of 33% of list at TEN years, which is ABOVE the 29-30% those comps show at EIGHT and NINE years - a 10-year-old car cannot out-retain a 9-year-old one, so that was corrected. I used a dealer ask of 480,000 (27.4% of list), continuing the observed decay one step past the Model S comps while staying above a pure floor because a mainstream Model 3 is far more liquid than a large Model S and 70,000 km at 10 years is exceptionally low. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale = dealer ask x 0.88, dealer_tradein = private x 0.86. Lands at 23.7% of real_cost, between the Toyota bZ4X (20.9%) and sibling Model Y (25.5%) records. The decisive factor is that from year 8 the battery and drive-unit warranty has EXPIRED (the 192,000 km cap never binds at this mileage), so the buyer carries full pack risk - a Model 3 pack replacement in TW runs into the hundreds of thousands, which is why old TW BEVs trade on an absolute floor rather than a retention percentage. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

maintenance.plan_notes: Tesla Taiwan has NO free scheduled-maintenance programme and no fixed service interval - it publishes a self-pay price list instead, and warranty is not voided by skipping visits. At 7,000 km/yr the schedule is TIME-DRIVEN, not mileage-driven, with one exception. INTERVALS CORRECTED against the primary source on 2026-08-12 (the prior draft misstated two of them): the owner's manual table reproduced at wuangus.cc reads 車廂空氣濾清器 每 3 年 (cabin air filter every THREE years, not two) and A/C 乾燥劑袋 6 年 (desiccant bag every SIX years, not four) - so only ONE desiccant replacement falls inside 10 years, not two. Brake fluid is 每 2 年 (check/replace). Wiper blades 每年或視需要. The one genuinely km-driven item is tire rotation/balance (每 10,000 公里, i.e. roughly every 1.4 years). The manual's mileage grid never binds: 懸吊系統扭力檢查 sits at 40,000 km steps, reached only at ~5.7 years, and the car finishes 10 years at 70,000 km. ALSO CORRECTED: the prior draft budgeted 6,000 for a battery-coolant change at year 10, but the same source states 電池冷卻液 - 在大多數情況下，在車輛使用壽命期間都無需更換 (no replacement needed during the vehicle's life), so that line was removed. Official Tesla TW self-pay prices used throughout, Model 3 (2023+) column, effective 2024-11-06, each figure re-verified in the source HTML: 冷氣系統測試 290, 底盤扭力確認(前+後) 2,029, 冷氣濾網更換 1,397, 冷氣乾燥包更換 3,711 (refrigerant extra), 煞車油 2,764, 雨刷一對 1,796, 16V 電瓶更換 9,417. Cross-checked against a real TW owner receipt: a full periodic visit (tires/pressure, chassis torque, A/C test, cabin filter, brake fluid) invoiced 6,673. WHY THIS IS A BEV, NOT A COMBUSTION CAR: no engine oil, no oil filter, no spark plugs, no timing belt/chain, no fuel system service, no emissions check - the bulk of a combustion car's bill is simply absent. Regenerative braking means pads and discs are barely worn at 70,000 km; the real brake risk on a low-mileage TW car is disc corrosion from humidity, not wear, so one front pad-and-disc job is budgeted late rather than repeatedly. BUT the BEV-specific costs are real and included: tires wear FASTER on a Model 3 (kerb weight and instant torque), so two full sets are budgeted (~year 5 and ~year 10, driven by rubber ageing as much as tread at this mileage) at 23,000-24,000 each for four 235/45R18 tires with fitting, balancing and alignment; brake fluid still needs changing; and the low-voltage battery still dies - this generation uses a 16V lithium unit at 9,417, budgeted once in the 5-7 window. WARRANTY SHAPE drives the back end: basic vehicle warranty is 4 years / 80,000 km, so years 0-4 are nearly free of unscheduled cost, years 5-7 carry out-of-warranty risk on everything except the pack, and from year 8 the battery and drive-unit warranty (8 years / 192,000 km for Long Range - the cap never binds at 70,000 km) expires too, which is why the 7-10 period is by far the largest. TAIL RISK NOT IN THESE NUMBERS: a post-warranty pack or drive-unit failure is a several-hundred-thousand event; the 7-10 figure carries a probability-weighted allowance, not a full pack replacement. Ten-year total is 184,000 (~18,400/yr) - roughly half to two-thirds of a comparable combustion sedan over the same period at the same mileage, but emphatically not zero.

The prior draft billed a 冷氣乾燥包 3,711 plus refrigerant ~1,300 and a 冷氣濾網 1,397 in this window on the basis of a '4-year desiccant / 2-year cabin filter' schedule; the cited source actually says A/C 乾燥劑袋 6 年 and 車廂空氣濾清器 每 3 年, so neither falls due here — the desiccant moves to the 5-7 window and the filter to years 3, 6 and 9. checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN from the prior draft (was 100,000). Two schedule corrections: the prior draft billed a second 冷氣乾燥包 here on a 4-year interval (the real interval is 6 years, so only one falls in 10 years) and a 6,000 battery-coolant change justified by an unreachable 160,000 km trigger — but the same source states 電池冷卻液 在大多數情況下，在車輛使用壽命期間都無需更換, so that line was removed outright. Scheduled items priced from the Tesla TW self-pay list, Model 3 (2023+) column (wuangus.cc/tesla-model-3-service); tire set from the TW retail/specialist range cited at the 5-year checkpoint. The dominant line — the 35,000 out-of-warranty allowance — is an explicit estimate, not a quote: from year 8 the battery and drive-unit warranty has expired and nothing on the car is covered. It is probability-weighted for the realistic failures of an 8-10 year old TW Tesla (A/C compressor, suspension, door handles, MCU/screen, 16V system, HV contactor), and deliberately does NOT price a full pack replacement, which would be a several-hundred-thousand event. Treat this period as the least certain number in the record.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr, roughly half the TW average of 12,000-15,000. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years. At this mileage the Model Y is entirely TIME-driven, not km-driven: Tesla has no fixed scheduled-service interval, and the items that do exist (cabin/HEPA filter every 2-3 yr, brake fluid every 2 yr, A/C desiccant bag every 6 yr) are all calendar-based. Tires are replaced on rubber age (~5-6 yr), not tread depth - 35,000 km at year 5 would not wear out a set, so the first set is budgeted at year 6 and the second at year 10. The battery and drive-unit warranty (8 years / 160,000 km for the RWD; the Long Range carries 192,000 km, visible in TW used listings advertising 電池保固19.2萬公里) is bounded by the TIME limit at this mileage, never the km limit, so it expires at year 8 and year 10 is fully out of warranty. HOME CHARGER IS EXCLUDED from every number here: a TW home installation (Tesla Wall Connector plus a dedicated 220V circuit, meter work, and building-management approval) runs about NT$30,000-80,000 depending on the parking space, and it is a one-off ownership cost, not maintenance. Also excluded by design: all tax (貨物稅, 牌照稅, 燃料費) and all insurance. Electricity/charging cost is not modelled here either. Spec basis re-verified against the U-CAR spec table on 2026-08-12: 60 kWh total / 57.5 kWh usable pack, 1,928 kg kerb weight, 279 hp, 0-100 km/h 5.9 s, WLTP 517 km, 255/45 R19 tires front AND rear - the tire size drives the replacement cost below.

It moves the LIST price instead, repeatedly - verified from the U-CAR event log: 2022-09-23 launch (LR 229.99萬 / Performance 259.99萬); 2023 cuts and a small raise leaving LR at 212.79萬; 2023-11-01 RWD added at 179.99萬; 2024-04-26 cut RWD by 6.5萬 to 173.49萬 and LR/Performance by 2萬 each; 2025-03 facelift RAISED the RWD to 189.99萬 (+165,000, +9.5%). So a buyer today gets zero discount but carries full exposure to the next list-price move, and the RWD list has swung 179.99 -> 173.49 -> 189.99萬 in under three years. selling_costs.notes: Priced for a private sale (自售), which is what private_sale_price assumes. The statutory 過戶 registration fee itself is only a few hundred NT$; NT$2,500 reflects the usual 代辦 (agent) service most private sellers use. Detailing is set at the higher end of normal because a Tesla's light interior and large glass roof are what buyers inspect first, and because a low-mileage car only realises its low-mileage premium if it also PRESENTS as low-mileage. NT$12,000 sits mid-band for a ~NT$1.9M mid-size SUV and matches the figure used for the Model Y Long Range AWD record in the same dataset. If the owner trades in to a dealer instead (dealer_tradein_price), most of this cost disappears - the dealer absorbs transfer and prep - which is part of why the trade-in figure is lower.

value_checkpoints.source: No 1-year-old facelift RWD exists yet (TW facelift on sale 2025-03), so this is interpolated between new (NT$1,899,900) and the youngest real listings. Independently re-pulled 好車網 (https://www.hotcar.com.tw/UsedCarSell/CarFilter) on 2026-08-12 via its listing API: 115 live Tesla listings, of which 47 Model Y. The MY2024 Model Y RWD low-km cluster asks NT$1,498,000-1,638,000 at 9,750-27,655 km (median ~NT$1,558,000) against that car's NT$1,734,900 list - i.e. ~90% dealer ASKING at ~2.3 years. That asking level is not disciplined: the same dataset contains a MY2024 RWD at 42,628 km asking NT$1,830,000, which is 105% of its own original list, and the spread at comparable mileage runs 22%. I therefore use the observed data for curve SHAPE and set the LEVEL from the mature, liquid 5-7 year Tesla market (see the year-5 and year-7 checkpoints), landing at ~83% dealer asking for a 1-year-old low-km facelift RWD = ~NT$1,584,000, which already includes a low-mileage uplift for 7,000 km vs a typical ~13,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale set 11% BELOW that dealer asking price (mid of the 8-15% band) = NT$1,410,000; dealer trade-in a further 13% below the private figure = NT$1,225,000.

Real same-model, same-trim listings exist but are read down deliberately. 好車網 2026-08-12: MY2023 Model Y RWD asking NT$1,538,000 (37,283 km), NT$1,498,000 (39,847 km), NT$1,558,000 (42,556 km); MY2024 Model Y RWD asking NT$1,498,000-1,638,000 across 9,750-59,322 km. SUM汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch?brand=TESLA&keyword=Model%20Y), independently re-parsed the same day, confirms the band: 2024 Model Y at NT$1,498,000 (38,022 km), NT$1,528,000 (38,000 km), NT$1,588,000 (47,138 km), NT$1,538,000 (11,617 km) - SUM does not print the trim on those cards, so trim attribution is inferred, not stated. Taken at face value those cars sit at 85-90% of their own original list. THREE REASONS THAT NUMBER IS NOT CARRIED FORWARD. (1) It is dealer ASKING on demonstrably undisciplined stock (one MY2024 RWD asks 105% of its own original list). (2) The anchors are only ~2.2-2.5 years old, not 3.0 - MY2023 RWD deliveries started after the 2023-11-01 TW launch - so reading them as 3-year data overstates by roughly half a year of depreciation. (3) Those cars enjoy a tailwind this buyer will not get: the 2025-03 facelift RAISED the RWD list from NT$1,734,900 to NT$1,899,900, lifting the entire used stock, and Tesla's TW history is of CUTS (2024-04 took the RWD down 6.5萬). I therefore set the level by interpolating the year-1 and year-5 points on the slope observed in the mature 5-7 year Tesla market: ~70% dealer asking = ~NT$1,326,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = asking - 11% = NT$1,180,000; trade-in = private - 13% = NT$1,025,000. This is roughly NT$130,000 below the researcher's figure and is the single largest correction in this record.

Base is the oldest Tesla trading in volume here, the MY2021 Model 3 (age ~5.1 yr), from the 47 live Model 3 listings pulled from 好車網 on 2026-08-12. Against U-CAR's verified original TW list prices (SR+ NT$1,609,900 after the 2020-03 raise; LR NT$1,957,900 after the 2021-06 raise): SR+ asks NT$938,000 at 84,746 km (58.3%), NT$958,000 at 89,086 km (59.5%), NT$908,000 at 96,187 km (56.4%); LR asks NT$1,138,000 at 64,773 km (58.1%), NT$998,000 at 105,131 km (51.0%), NT$838,000 at 122,038 km (42.8%). The directly relevant low-mileage analogue - a MY2021 Model 3 LR at 35,000 km, exactly this checkpoint's mileage - asks NT$1,258,000 = 64.3%. I set the Model Y RWD at ~57.4% dealer asking = ~NT$1,090,000: between the high-mileage median (~57%) and the low-mileage example (~64%), then haircut ~4 points because this car's NT$1,899,900 base is an elevated post-facelift list and because the Model Y Standard (see sources) threatens the RWD specifically. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = asking - 11% = NT$970,000; trade-in = private - 13% = NT$844,000. Low confidence because the base is a different model.

EXTRAPOLATED - stated explicitly, not invented. There is no 7-year-old Model Y anywhere in Taiwan (TW launch 2022-09). The oldest BEV with a real TW market at this age is the MY2019 Model 3, launched TW 2019-08-12 at SR+ NT$1,559,900 / LR NT$1,869,900 / Performance NT$2,149,900 (verified from https://newcar.u-car.com.tw/tesla/model%203/7036/event on 2026-08-12). 好車網 MY2019 Model 3 listings (age ~7.1 yr): LR NT$938,000 at 79,299 km (50.2% of its own list), LR NT$858,000 at 116,212 km (45.9%), LR NT$888,000 at 135,044 km (47.5%), Performance NT$968,000 at 141,188 km (45.0%) - median ~47%, and note EVERY one is high mileage (79k-141k km, i.e. 11,000-20,000 km/yr). A low-mileage uplift for 49,000 km vs a typical ~110,000 km argues for roughly +8 points relative, which I then give back for this car's elevated post-facelift list base, landing at ~47% dealer asking = ~NT$893,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = asking - 11% = NT$795,000; trade-in = private - 13% = NT$691,000. Symmetry check: today's 7-year-old Model 3s are still inside their own 8-year battery warranty, exactly as this car will be at year 7, so the warranty tailwind is comparable on both sides and the drop from year 5 is orderly rather than a cliff.

EXTRAPOLATED WITH NO DIRECT DATA - there is no 10-year-old Tesla market in Taiwan at all. The oldest TW Teslas trading are MY2019 Model 3s at 7 years (好車網, 47 Model 3 listings pulled 2026-08-12, none older than MY2019), so the 7-to-10 segment is projected, not observed. Extending the Model 3-derived dealer-asking curve (~57% at 5 yr, ~47% at 7 yr as a share of that car's own original list) another three years, with the warranty cliff applied, gives ~31% dealer asking = ~NT$585,000, already inclusive of a low-mileage allowance for 70,000 km vs a typical ~130,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = asking - 11% = NT$520,000; trade-in = private - 13% = NT$452,000. Two BEV-specific forces pull in OPPOSITE directions here and roughly offset: (a) the 8-year battery and drive-unit warranty has expired, and TW buyers discount an out-of-warranty EV hard because an out-of-pocket pack replacement is NT$400,000-700,000; (b) this trim uses the ~60 kWh BYD LFP pack, whose cycle life is far better than NMC, and at only 70,000 km it will have seen very few cycles, so a car that can show a good state-of-health readout will clear the top of this band. Confidence is low and should be read as such.

maintenance.plan_notes: Tesla Taiwan has NO fixed scheduled-maintenance programme and NO free-service package - there is no annual service you are required to buy, which is the single biggest structural difference from a combustion rival. What remains is a short list of calendar-driven items, and at 7,000 km/yr EVERY interval below is TIME-driven, never km-driven. Recurring items: cabin/HEPA air filter every 2-3 years (~NT$3,500 at a TW service centre); brake fluid every 2 years (~NT$4,000 - Taiwan's humidity makes this a real replacement, not just a test); A/C desiccant bag at ~6 years (~NT$6,500); tire rotation every 10,000 km, which at this mileage is roughly every 18 months (~NT$1,200); wiper blades every 1-2 years. WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT vs a combustion car: no engine oil, no oil filter, no spark plugs, no timing belt/chain, no transmission fluid, no exhaust or catalytic converter, and no scheduled coolant change (Tesla specifies none for Model 3/Y - a coolant service is still budgeted in the 5-7 and 7-10 windows as prudence at age). WHAT IS WORSE THAN A COMBUSTION CAR: tires. At 1,928 kg with instant torque the Model Y works 255/45 R19 rubber hard, and at 7,000 km/yr the binding constraint is rubber AGE, not tread, so sets get replaced on the calendar regardless of wear - budgeted at year 6 and year 10. TIRE PRICING CORRECTED: a fitted set of four quality EV-rated 255/45 R19 tires in Taiwan is NT$30,000-42,000 (roughly NT$6,500-10,000 per tire plus fitting), not the NT$52,000-56,000 the researcher assumed - that is 21-inch money, and it inflated the ten-year plan by roughly NT$25,000 on its own. Tires are still the largest single line item here at ~NT$78,000 over ten years. Brakes go the other way: regenerative braking means the pads may never wear out inside 70,000 km, but low-mileage cars in a humid climate suffer ROTOR CORROSION instead, so caliper cleaning is budgeted at year 5 and a pad-and-rotor job around year 8-9. The low-voltage battery still dies (the facelift uses a lithium-ion LV battery, longer-lived than lead-acid but not immortal) and is budgeted at ~year 6-7 at ~NT$12,000. Warranty shape drives the back end: the basic vehicle warranty (4 years / 80,000 km) expires on TIME at year 4; the battery and drive-unit warranty (8 years / 160,000 km for the RWD) expires on TIME at year 8, since the km cap is unreachable at this mileage. So the 5-7 window carries a modest out-of-warranty allowance and the 7-10 window a larger one (A/C compressor, suspension bushings, half-shafts, MCU/screen, coolant pump, a second LV battery). IMPORTANT EXCLUSION: the 7-10 allowance does NOT budget a high-voltage pack replacement. At 70,000 km on an LFP pack that is unlikely, but if it happens it is NT$400,000-700,000 and would dwarf every number in this table. Home-charger installation is excluded here by design and noted in assumptions.notes instead. Ten-year total across all five periods: ~NT$224,500 - materially below a comparable combustion or hybrid SUV (a Toyota RAV4 Hybrid runs ~NT$244,000 over the same 70,000 km in this dataset) but emphatically NOT near zero.

Out-of-warranty risk is a probability-weighted allowance rather than an observed cost - no 7-year-old Model Y exists in Taiwan - informed by the fault pattern of MY2019-2020 Model 3s now at this age in the TW market. major_items: SECOND TIRE SET at ~year 10 (~NT$40,000) - again age-driven, not wear-driven
Out-of-warranty repair allowance (~NT$32,000): ALL warranties expired at year 8 - A/C compressor, suspension, half-shafts, MCU/screen, coolant pump, second LV battery
Brake pads and rotors at ~year 8-9 (~NT$18,000) - corrosion-driven at this mileage, not friction-driven; regen means the pads themselves are barely worn
Cabin/HEPA air filter x2, years 8 and 10 (~NT$7,000)
Brake fluid x2, years 8 and 10 (~NT$8,000)
Coolant service (~NT$6,000)
Tire rotations x2, wiper blades x2, alignment (~NT$7,000)
EXCLUDED: high-voltage pack replacement. Unlikely on an LFP pack at 70,000 km, but it is NT$400,000-700,000 if it happens
checkpoints.source: Cost SINCE year 7 (7-10 yr window). Pure extrapolation - Taiwan has no 10-year-old Tesla market of any kind; the oldest TW Teslas trading are MY2019 Model 3s at 7 years. The out-of-warranty allowance is a probability-weighted estimate, not an observed figure. Modelled, not a quoted invoice.

assumptions.notes: 年行駛 6,000-8,000 km，遠低於台灣平均 12,000-15,000 km；各檢查點一律用中位數 7,000 km/年（7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km）。保養觸發方式（已對照官方週期表逐項確認，非一概而論）：「每 20,000 km／每 1 年」「每 40,000 km／每 2 年（大保養）」「每 8 年／160,000 km（電池冷卻液）」三組都寫明先到者為準，在 7,000 km/年下一律由時間先到；但「每 10,000 km」那一組（輪胎換位、車內空氣濾網、雨刷水）官方沒有給時間替代條件，所以它是純里程觸發，約每 1.43 年到期一次。換言之並非「所有項目都由時間觸發」。家用充電樁「不」計入 maintenance，也未計入 real_cost：Tesla 壁掛式連接器約 NT$13,500，台灣公寓大樓拉專線＋獨立電表＋管委會施工，實務落在 NT$40,000-80,000，屬另計的持有成本。稅金與保險依設計排除（電動車現行免徵貨物稅、免牌照稅與燃料費，但本表一律不列）。電費亦不在本表範圍。

purchase.source: 建議售價 NT$3,249,900，由兩個獨立來源當場擷取交叉確認（2026-08-12）：U-CAR 車款頁列 Model S 車系 324.99-339.99 萬，Yahoo 汽車「2026 Tesla Model S」共 2 筆，全輪驅動 324.99、Plaid 339.99。與原研究者數字一致，未修改。折扣 0 元的依據是 Tesla 台灣的定價史本身：U-CAR 事件簿逐日記錄 2023/03 重新開賣 304.99 萬 → 2023/05 調漲 8 萬（312.99）→ 2023/09 降價 18 萬（294.99、降幅 5.7%）→ 2025/06 小改款調漲 30 萬（324.99），全部是「原廠改牌價」而非經銷折讓。Tesla 直營、無經銷體系、無議價空間，故 discounts 為 0。
purchase.notes: 本車即 Model S 雙馬達全輪驅動 Long Range 版（非三馬達 Plaid），670 hp、WLTP 650 km、19 吋輪圈；2025/06 小改款導入前視鏡頭、全光譜氣氛燈、新交錯式輪圈與冰霜藍／曜石黑新色（選配價分別為 9.7 萬與 4.9 萬，未計入）。onroad_fees 由原研究者的 85,000 下修為 60,000：Tesla 台灣是直營交車，沒有燃油車經銷體系那種業代加裝包，把 34,000 的鍍膜與車內配件當成必付項目並不成立；同資料集內另一筆 Tesla 記錄（Model Y，車價 2,299,900）用的是 30,000。本次拆解為新車領牌＋監理規費＋代辦約 6,000（電動車免牌照稅與燃料費）、全車頂級隔熱紙約 40,000（Model S 為全景玻璃車頂，貼膜面積與單價都明顯高於一般車）、腳踏墊與交車配件約 14,000，合計 60,000，約佔車價 1.8%。real_cost = 3,249,900 − 0 + 60,000 = 3,309,900。稅金與保險依規定排除。

售前整備／美容鍍膜
刊登費（8891／ONLYEV 加值刊登）
電池健康檢測報告

selling_costs.notes: 取 4,000-15,000 級距的上緣（即上限），理由有三：一是 300 萬級旗艦車自售前整備（拋光、鍍膜、內裝深度清潔）行情本來就高於一般國產車；二是電動車自售多一項燃油車沒有的成本——買方會要求電池健康度報告，第三方檢測約 NT$2,000，不附的車在議價時會被砍更多；三是流通量極稀，ONLYEV 全台 Model S 在售僅 21 台、SUM 汽車網全站 Model S 掛零（兩者皆 2026-08-12 實際擷取），刊登期會拉長，加值刊登費因此列滿。已確認 15,000 是級距天花板而非可再往上加的數字。

value_checkpoints.source: 外推，無真實樣本。2025/06 小改款車 2025 下半年才交車，ONLYEV 2026-08-12 全台 21 台 Model S 在售車源中沒有任何一台 1 年內的小改款車。可用的最近錨點是同世代車商開價：三台 2024/03 Model S LR（8,000-8,300 km、2.4 年）開 259.8/259.8/259.9 萬，以及 2024/10 Model S Plaid（14,000 km、1.8 年）開 268 萬＝其 339.99 萬列表價的 78.8%。由此推估 1 年期小改款 LR 車商開價約 275 萬。private_sale_price 2,430,000 為車商開價減 11.6%（車商開價→自售的正常價差），dealer_tradein_price 2,100,000 再減 13.6%。原研究者的 2,480,000 略微下修，理由是折舊必須前重後輕，原表 1→3 年僅跌 7.7% 而 3→5 年跌 21%，形狀不合理。須明講的風險：本段之所以看起來平緩，是因為 2025/06 列表價一次漲 30 萬把整批中古開價一起墊高，這是本表最大的單一下檔風險。

本世代真實車商開價，但已扣除同儕比較後的樂觀成分。ONLYEV 2026-08-12 擷取的同齡本世代 Model S LR 車商開價：2023/05 開 258 萬（37,000 km、3.25 年）、2023/08 開 252 萬（40,000 km、3.0 年）、2023/11 開 239.8 萬（30,000 km、2.75 年），中位約 250 萬。注意這批開價彼此矛盾：里程最低（30,000 km）的 2023/11 反而開價最低，2023/12 Plaid 開 288 萬卻高於更新的 2024/10 Plaid 268 萬——21 台的市場沒有價格發現，開價是掛牌願望值而非成交值。同平台較厚的 Model Y LR 市場（78 台）同齡開價僅為其列表價的 65-69%，而 Model S 這批達 77.5-80%，差距明顯來自流動性不足與 2025/06 漲價墊高。故車商開價取 248 萬（低於 252-258 萬群集、高於 239.8 萬），本檢查點 21,000 km 低於同齡真實車（30,000-40,000 km）的加分已含在內。private_sale_price 2,180,000 為車商開價減 12.1%，dealer_tradein_price 1,880,000 再減 13.8%。

內插，本世代在台灣尚無滿 5 年的車（2023/03 才重新開賣，最老的本世代車 3.4 年）。上錨點是本檢查表 3 年期；下錨點是前代 Raven（2019-2021 Long Range，2019/03/22 起列表價 266.3 萬，已於 U-CAR 45803 原文確認）的真實低里程車商開價：ONLYEV 2020/09 出廠 33,000 km 開 169.8 萬（5.9 年）、2020/06 出廠 33,000 km 開 163.8 萬（6.2 年）；同齡高里程明顯較低（92,000 km 為 158-160 萬、140,000 km 為 148.8 萬），本檢查點 35,000 km 屬低里程帶，取低里程曲線。兩種換算刻意並陳：用 Raven 對「自身列表價」的保值率（5.9 年 63.8%）外推到本車 324.99 萬得約 224 萬，用 Raven 開價對「今日列表價」的比值（169.8/324.99＝52.2%）得約 185 萬；前者會重複計入 2025 漲價效果，後者偏保守，取中央值 199 萬為車商開價。方法間 ±20% 的落差就是本點的不確定度。private_sale_price 1,750,000 為車商開價減 12.1%，dealer_tradein_price 1,500,000 再減 14.3%。

前代外推，非本世代實價，confidence low。7 年期唯一的真實低里程樣本是更前一代 Model S 75D：ONLYEV 2019/02 出廠、39,000 km 車商開價 138 萬（7.5 年）；同代 2019/03、110,000 km 為 136.8 萬。此處刻意改用「對今日列表價的比值」而非原研究者推導的舊車原價：138/324.99＝42.5%。原研究者用的分母 NT$3,492,900 無法佐證——U-CAR 45555 原文只列降價「後」的 80D 2,834,000／100D 2,982,000／P100D 3,444,000 與 658,900-2,971,900 的降幅區間，全文未出現 75D 也未出現 3,492,900，且 U-CAR 45803 顯示 3/1 之後 Model S 入門其實是標準里程 245 萬，該推導不成立，已移除。本檢查點為 7.0 年、49,000 km（略新、里程略高於 138 萬那台），取車商開價 143 萬＝今日列表價的 44.0%。private_sale_price 1,250,000 為減 12.6%，dealer_tradein_price 1,065,000 再減 14.8%。此區間已反映 Tesla 反覆降價把整批中古庫存一次重新定價的風險。

外推，台灣不存在 10 年份的 Tesla 中古市場，這點已查證而非假設：U-CAR 事件簿載明 Model S「預計 2017 年第一季陸續交車」，全台最老的 Model S 約 9.5 年；ONLYEV 2026-08-12 全部 348 台 Tesla 在售車中最老為 Model S 75D 2018/11（7.8 年）；SUM 汽車網全站 Tesla 車源中 Model S 為零（已實際擷取確認）。因此依規定改用實際仍在交易的最老 BEV 外推，而非燃油車類比：Model S 75D 2018/11、108,000 km 車商開價 99.8 萬＝今日列表價的 30.7%（7.8 年）。本車 10 年時里程僅 70,000 km（遠低於該車的 108,000 km），但多 2.2 年車齡，且 BEV 在此階段主導價格的是電池日曆老化、原廠保固（基本 4 年、電池與驅動單元 8 年／24 萬公里）全數到期、以及 MCU 觸控螢幕等已知故障件——低里程的加分遠不如燃油車。兩者大致抵銷後略往下，取 26.2% 得車商開價約 85 萬。private_sale_price 730,000 為減 14.1%，dealer_tradein_price 620,000 再減 15.1%（車齡越高車商收購價差越大）。

maintenance.plan_notes: Tesla 台灣沒有免費定期保養方案，也不強制回廠，但官方公開了保養週期與價目表。價格全數採用 ONLYEV 整理的台灣原廠保養價目表（2026/03/26 更新，含工資、零件與 5% 營業稅）之 Model S「MS 2023+」欄位，即本車所屬世代，並已於 2026-08-12 逐項回原頁面核對無誤：底盤巡視＆扭力檢查 3,140、冷氣濾網 815、冷氣乾燥包 4,165、煞車油 2,619、HEPA 濾網 4,287、雨刷片一對 2,125、馬達油＋油芯 6,268；技師工資 2,415/hr，冷媒 R1234YF 9.45/g 另計。低壓電池在 MS 2023+ 欄位確實掛「—」（該世代改用 16V 鋰電池），以同表 Model 3/Y 的 16V 鋰電池 9,055 與舊款 Model S 12V 鉛酸 8,345 推估約 10,000。觸發方式已逐組確認，不是一概而論：「每 20,000 km／每 1 年」（輪胎對調平衡、煞車卡鉗清潔、雨刷片）、「每 40,000 km／每 2 年」（大保養：冷氣乾燥包、電池冷卻液檢查、前後懸吊扭力、冷氣系統、四輪定位、冷媒、煞車油）、「每 8 年／160,000 km」（電池冷卻液更換）三組官方都寫先到者為準，在 7,000 km/年下都是時間先到；但「每 10,000 km」那一組（輪胎換位、車內空氣濾網、雨刷水）官方沒有時間替代條件，屬純里程觸發，約 1.43 年一次。另有「每 3 年」HEPA 濾網（Model S/X/Y 適用）與「每 4 年」煞車油兩個純時間項。電動車省下的項目是實的：無機油、無火星塞、無正時系統、無變速箱油、無排氣檢測，且動能回收讓煞車來令片幾乎不磨耗。但輪胎反而更耗（車重逾 2 噸＋670 hp，且 7,000 km/年下是老化到期而非磨耗到期，5-6 年仍須換一套）、煞車油與冷卻液照換、低壓電池照壞——這三項是本表後段成本主軸，再加上保固到期後的空氣懸吊與 MCU 風險。真實帳單校準：Model 3/Y 車主實付大保養 NT$6,673（約 3 小時）與 NT$7,360（含冷媒乾燥包），Model S 零件單價較高，故本表大保養抓約 NT$11,000。10 年合計約 NT$315,000、年均 NT$31,500——明顯低於同價帶燃油旗艦房車，但絕非零。相對原研究者版本，本表把 16V 低壓電池首次更換由 3-5 年段移到 5-7 年段（4 年車齡的鋰電池極少陣亡，5-7 年才是實際首次故障帶），連帶修正原表 5 年期 69,000 高於 7 年期 62,000 的非單調問題。

major_items: 雨刷片一對 NT$2,125（原廠價目表 MS 2023+）
輪胎對調與平衡約 NT$1,500（每 20,000 km／每 1 年，時間先到）
全車在 4 年／8 萬公里新車保固內，無自費維修
7,000 km 未達 10,000 km 門檻，車內空氣濾網與輪胎換位尚未到期（該組為純里程觸發）
checkpoints.source: ONLYEV 台灣 Tesla 原廠保養價目表（2026/03/26 更新）Model S MS 2023+ 欄位，配合同頁官方保養週期表，兩者均於 2026-08-12 實際擷取核對。第 1 年只有「每 1 年」的時間項到期，且 Tesla 台灣不強制回廠，實務上多數車主第一年僅換雨刷片與做輪胎對調。

major_items: 第 2 年大保養：底盤巡視＆扭力 3,140＋冷氣乾燥包 4,165＋煞車油 2,619＋冷氣濾網 815 ≈ 10,739
第 3 年 HEPA 高效濾網 4,287（每 3 年純時間項，Model S 適用）
兩次雨刷片 4,250、兩次輪胎對調平衡 3,000
整段仍在 4 年基本保固內，無保固外修理支出

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the TW average of ~12,000-15,000. Midpoint 7,000 km/yr used at every checkpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). CONSEQUENCE: nothing on this car is mileage-driven at this rate. Tesla TW warranty is 4yr/80,000km basic and 8yr/240,000km battery+drive unit; at 7,000 km/yr the km caps NEVER bind, so only the year caps matter — basic cover ends year 4, all cover ends year 8. Tires age out on rubber hardening (5-6 years) long before tread wear. Brake pads may never wear out (regen), so the brake cost here is disc corrosion from disuse in Taiwan's humidity, not pad wear. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: 使用牌照稅, 燃料費 and insurance are excluded per the model spec (BEVs also currently enjoy TW road-tax exemption, not credited here). ALSO EXCLUDED: home charger. A Tesla Wall Connector plus installation in Taiwan runs roughly NT$35,000-80,000 — cheap in a 透天厝, expensive in a 社區大樓 needing a 台電 sub-meter application and riser wiring. Real one-off ownership cost, but NOT maintenance, so deliberately out of maintenance.checkpoints. Electricity/charging cost likewise out of scope. FACT-CHECK NOTE: the value curve in this record was revised DOWN from the researcher's draft at every checkpoint — see value_checkpoints[].source and sources[] for why.

purchase.source: Independently re-verified against U-CAR's Model X model page (fetched 2026-08-12 by direct HTTP, WebFetch was 403'd): the page's trim table lists Model X 5人座 at 349.99萬 = NT$3,499,900 (other trims: 7人座 361.29萬, Plaid 6人座 364.99萬, 6人座 370.99萬). The researcher's list_price is CORRECT and unchanged. onroad_fees WAS reduced from 85,000 to 60,000 — see notes.
purchase.notes: 2025/06 facelift Model X Long Range (dual-motor AWD), 5-seat, 670hp, WLTP 597 km, 20-inch Perihelix wheels — the entry point of the TW Model X range. discounts = 0 is correct and deliberate: Tesla Taiwan sells at a fixed published price with no dealer haggling; instead of discounting individual cars it moves the list price for everyone. U-CAR documents exactly that four times: 348.99萬 at the 2023/03 relaunch, +8萬 to 356.99萬 in 2023/05, −32萬 (−8.9%) to 324.99萬 in 2023/09, then +25萬 to today's 349.99萬 with the 2025/06 facelift. That −32萬 overnight cut is the single most important fact in this record — it repriced every used Model X in Taiwan instantly and is why the value curve here is deliberately weak. ONROAD_FEES CORRECTION: the researcher used 85,000 (領牌+代辦 15,000, window film 45,000, mats/liner/coating 25,000). That is out of line with the same-brand sibling record in this dataset (Tesla Model Y: 30,000 on a 2,299,900 car, 1.3%); price-scaled to 3,499,900 that would be ~45,600. Model X's panoramic wraparound windscreen genuinely does cost more to film than a normal SUV, so a premium over the scaled figure is justified, but not a doubling. Set to 60,000 = 領牌規費+代辦 ~15,000, film ~25,000, mats/boot liner/coating ~20,000. Tax and insurance excluded by design and NOT in this number.

售前整備 / 美容 (large luxury SUV)
刊登費 (8891 / SUM 自售刊登)

selling_costs.notes: Priced for a private sale (自售), which is what value_checkpoints assume. Reviewed and left unchanged — 14,500 is at the top of the brief's 4,000-15,000 band, which is right for a 5,057mm luxury SUV with falcon-wing doors and a large glass area; prep is not a NT$3,000 quick polish. Comparable to the sibling Tesla Model Y record's 12,000 for a smaller car. If the owner trades in to a dealer instead, most of this disappears (the dealer handles 過戶 and its own prep) but so does 13-17% of the price — that trade-off is what dealer_tradein_price captures.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED — no 1-year-old Model X exists in any reachable Taiwan used listing. SUM's entire national Tesla inventory is 50 cars and contains exactly 3 Model X, none newer than 2023; 8891 (the largest TW inventory) was unreachable, every used-car URL path returned 404. REVISED DOWN from the researcher's 2,870,000. Their figure was 80.1% of real_cost / 82.0% of list at year 1, which fails three cross-checks: (a) it out-retains the sibling Tesla Model Y record in this same dataset (75.5% at year 1) even though Model X is a 350萬 niche car with 3 national comparables versus Model Y's liquid 21-listing market, and illiquid luxury cars depreciate FASTER in percentage terms, not slower; (b) it out-retains the Lexus RX350h hybrid (77.1%), violating the rule that a BEV should almost never out-retain a comparable hybrid in Taiwan; (c) it implies a dealer would ask ~3,250,000 (93% of new list) for a 1-year-old car when the buyer can order new at 3,499,900 with full warranty and free config — that market does not exist, especially for a brand that cut this exact model's list price 32萬 overnight in 2023/09. Set to 72.8% of real_cost. dealer_tradein_price is 13.5% below private, the normal 收購 spread. No dealer asking price was copied into private_sale_price.

Anchored on the ONE exact-trim real listing on SUM, which I independently re-fetched and confirmed on 2026-08-12: 2023 TESLA MODEL X, 65,860 km, 5人座 4WD, 冠立汽車 (金鑽車商, 臺南市), asking NT$2,798,000. That listing is REAL — the researcher transcribed it correctly. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: 2,798,000 is 車商售價 (dealer retail ask), not what an owner receives. The researcher applied −15% then a +10% low-mileage uplift then a manual hold-down, netting out at dealer ask −12.4%. I applied a wider −23% haircut instead, because that single ask does not survive scrutiny: the car it describes originally listed at either 324.99萬 (post Sept-2023 cut) or 356.99萬, so a 279.8萬 ask is 78-86% of ITS OWN original list after 3 years and 65,860 km. Nothing in Tesla's TW market supports that — SUM's age-4 (2022) Model 3 cohort asks 110.8-145.8萬 against a ~165-175萬 original, i.e. mostly ~70% at ASK level, and asks on a 3-car national market with no published 行情 table are aspirational rather than transactional. −23% gives ~2,155,000 private for the 66,000 km car. Our buyer's car has 21,000 km, about a third the mileage, which argues for an uplift; SUM's own age-5 Model 3 data shows that effect is real and large (35,000-35,343 km asking 125.8-129.8萬 versus 95.8萬 at 122,551 km, ~+31%). I did NOT stack that uplift on top, because it would double-count against the price-cut risk already embedded in the wider haircut, and because a low-mileage premium is much thinner on a car with three national comparables than on a Model 3 with twenty-six. Landed at 2,150,000 = 60.4% of real_cost, below the sibling Model Y (62.9%) and below every hybrid in the dataset. Single dealer ask on an illiquid market, hence LOW not medium (the researcher marked this medium). dealer_tradein_price is 14.0% below private.

INTERPOLATED between the two real Model X anchors I re-verified on SUM (2026-08-12): the age-3 2023 car at 2,798,000 ask and the two age-8 2018 cars at 1,280,000 / 1,488,000 ask. All converted from dealer ask to private before use. Year 5 is the first checkpoint fully outside Tesla's 4-year basic warranty, which weighs on price. A low-mileage premium is warranted (35,000 km at age 5 versus 66,000-121,000 km on the anchors) and SUM's age-5 Model 3 spread confirms low mileage is worth a lot on a TW Tesla, but the premium is applied more conservatively than the researcher did, for the illiquidity reason given at year 3. REVISED DOWN from 2,020,000 (56.3% of real_cost) to 1,640,000 (46.1%). The researcher's figure sat essentially level with the Lexus RX350h hybrid flagship (57.1%) and nearly 10 points above the sibling Model Y (46.8%) — a Tesla luxury SUV retaining like a Lexus hybrid is the exact failure mode this market's evidence rules out. NEGATIVE FINDING, independently confirmed: SUM's own 中古車行情查詢 (price-02.php) returns no 行情 table for TESLA MODEL X at any year 2016-2026 — I queried it directly and got a page with no price rows. There is therefore no published Taiwan price guide to corroborate this curve, which is why this checkpoint is low. dealer_tradein_price is 14.6% below private.

GENUINE same-model data at nearly the right age — Model X is not a new nameplate in Taiwan, deliveries began ~2017, so age-8 cars really do trade. Two real SUM listings, both independently re-fetched and confirmed 2026-08-12: 2018 MODEL X 75D, 109,470 km, 5人座 4WD, 和悅汽車 (高雄市), asking NT$1,280,000; and 2018 MODEL X 100D, 120,820 km, 6人座 4WD, 源豐汽車 (彰化縣), asking NT$1,488,000. The 75D 5-seat is the closest analogue to this AWD 5-seat trim. Sanity check on the level chosen: my 1,270,000 private for a 49,000 km age-7 facelift car implies a dealer ask of ~1,477,000, which is a ~15% premium over the actual 1,280,000 ask on a car one year older with 2.2x the mileage — a sensible, non-heroic adjustment. The researcher's 1,550,000 required a ~+42% jump off the same anchor and implied a dealer ask above the age-8 100D. Cross-check against the 75D's own original TW list (the pre-facelift 75D launched around NT$3.4-3.6M): its 1,280,000 ask is only ~35-38% of original, ~31-33% after conversion to private, which is the real shape of Model X depreciation in Taiwan and does not support a 43% figure at age 7. Year 7 also sits right on the edge of the 8-year battery-and-drive-unit warranty expiry, and TW buyers discount hard for a BEV about to lose that cover. dealer_tradein_price is 15.4% below private — the spread widens with age because dealers carry more battery risk.

EXTRAPOLATED — there is no genuine 10-year Model X market in Taiwan to sample. The oldest Model X listed on SUM as of 2026-08-12 are 2018 cars (age 8); nothing from 2016-2017 was offered. Per the brief I leaned on the oldest BEVs that DO trade here rather than a combustion analogue: SUM's age-6 Model 3 cohort (2020, 75,000-139,000 km) asks 73.8-99.8萬, and the age-5 2021 cars at 35,000 km ask 125.8-129.8萬, showing TW BEV values fall away steeply while low mileage still commands a large premium late in life. Method: took the year-7 figure above and applied ~−14%/yr for three more years (1,270,000 x 0.86^3 = ~808,000). The accelerating rather than decelerating decline is deliberate and BEV-specific — this window crosses the 8-year battery + drive unit warranty cliff, after which residual value is dominated by unverifiable battery state-of-health and by Model X's own expensive failure points (air suspension, falcon-wing doors). Low mileage of 70,000 km is the main thing holding the number up. REVISED DOWN from 990,000 (27.6% of real_cost) to 800,000 (22.5%), keeping it below the sibling Model Y (25.5%) and consistent with the revised curve above it. dealer_tradein_price is 16.9% below private — the widest spread of any checkpoint, because a 10-year out-of-warranty BEV is the hardest thing on a TW lot to underwrite.

maintenance.plan_notes: Tesla Taiwan mandates NO scheduled maintenance — there is no service-interval table to follow and no free scheduled-maintenance programme (unlike Volvo TW, which has run such schemes). Servicing is condition- and time-based. At 7,000 km/yr EVERY interval that matters here is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven. SOURCING CAVEAT, independently confirmed: tesla.com/zh_TW returns HTTP 403 to automated access — I retested the model page, the maintenance-schedule page and the warranty page and all three 403'd — so these are engineering estimates built on (a) the physical spec verified on U-CAR's official spec sheet, (b) Tesla's published TW warranty terms, and (c) normal Taiwan parts-and-labour rates. They are NOT transcribed from a fetched Tesla price list. Treat the levels as informed estimates and the SHAPE as the reliable part. Verified spec facts driving the numbers (all re-checked on U-CAR's spec page 2026-08-12): staggered tires 265/45 R20 front and 275/45 R20 rear, curb weight 2,373 kg, 智慧型空氣懸吊 (adaptive air suspension) standard front AND rear, 鋰離子電池, 5,057mm length, 四輪碟煞. WHY THIS IS NOT A COMBUSTION CAR: no oil, no filters, no spark plugs, no timing belt, no transmission service — years 1-3 are close to free. WHY IT IS NOT ZERO EITHER: staggered fitment means the tires cannot be cross-rotated and must be replaced as a full set, and 2,373 kg plus instant torque chews them faster than a combustion SUV; brake fluid and coolant still need changing; the low-voltage battery still dies; and from year 8 the car is out of ALL warranty with two known Model X money pits — air-suspension struts (roughly NT$50,000-80,000 per corner at Tesla) and falcon-wing door actuators/sensors. Those two are why the 7- and 10-year windows step up sharply. CORRECTION vs the researcher's draft: they placed the cabin HEPA filter on a 2-year interval (years 2/4/6/8/10). Tesla's published interval for Model S/X HEPA-equipped cars is every 3 YEARS, not 2 (the 2-year figure is the Model 3/Y cabin filter). Re-cadenced to years 3/6/9, which moves one filter out of the 3-5y window and trims that period. 10-year total ~NT$501,000 (avg ~NT$50,100/yr) — well under an equivalent large luxury combustion SUV over the same period, but nowhere near zero, and ~2.7x the sibling Tesla Model Y record, which is right for a heavier, air-sprung, falcon-winged car on staggered 20-inch rubber.

major_items: Covered by 4yr/80,000km basic warranty — no chargeable service
Tire rotation / wheel alignment check (~2,000)
Wiper blades (~1,500)
No oil, no filters, no spark plugs, no transmission service — BEV
checkpoints.source: Structural, not sampled: Tesla TW has no mandatory 1-year service and the car is inside its 4-year basic warranty. At 7,000 km nothing is due. The only real outlays are a rotation and wipers. This near-zero result is robust regardless of Tesla price-list access. Unchanged from the researcher's draft.

major_items: Cabin HEPA filter at year 3 (~8,000 — Model S/X interval is 3 years, filter is larger and dearer than a normal car's)
Brake fluid moisture test at year 2 (~1,500, test only, replacement rarely needed yet)
Tire rotations x2 (~4,000)
Wipers (~1,500)
Still inside 4yr/80,000km basic warranty — defects chargeable to Tesla
checkpoints.source: Time-driven items only; the 21,000 km cumulative figure triggers nothing mileage-based. Still fully inside basic warranty, so no repair risk is priced in. Total unchanged at 15,000, but the cabin HEPA filter was moved from year 2 to year 3 to match Tesla's actual Model S/X 3-year interval. Levels are Taiwan market estimates, not a fetched Tesla price list (tesla.com/zh_TW 403s).

major_items: FIRST TIRE SET — 4 tires aged out at ~5 years, not worn out (~50,000)
Staggered 265/45R20 + 275/45R20 means no cross-rotation and full-set replacement
Wheel alignment after fitting (~3,000)
Brake fluid replacement at year 4 (~4,000)
Tire rotations (~4,000), wipers (~1,500)
Basic warranty EXPIRES at year 4 — first out-of-pocket repair exposure (~9,000 provision)
checkpoints.source: Dominated by the first tire set. Tire sizes (265/45 R20 front, 275/45 R20 rear) and 2,373 kg curb weight independently re-verified on U-CAR's official Model X spec sheet 2026-08-12; premium 20-inch rubber in Taiwan runs roughly NT$11,000-13,000 per corner fitted, so ~50,000 a set. At 7,000 km/yr these tires are replaced on AGE (rubber hardening, ~5-6 years), never on tread depth — a mileage-based model would wrongly skip this cost entirely. Year 4 is when the basic warranty lapses, hence the first small repair provision. Reduced from the researcher's 78,000: their year-4 cabin HEPA filter does not belong here, because the Model S/X filter interval is 3 years (years 3/6/9), not 2.

major_items: Brake service — pads plus disc corrosion from LOW use in TW humidity, not from wear (~30,000)
Out-of-warranty risk provision: air-suspension strut / falcon-wing door actuator (~50,000)
Cabin HEPA filter at year 6 (~8,000)
A/C desiccant bag at year 6 (~6,000)
Coolant service (~8,000)
Rotations / alignment (~6,000), wipers (~2,000)
Battery + drive unit warranty still live until year 8
checkpoints.source: The brake line item is the counter-intuitive BEV point and is deliberate: regenerative braking means the pads on a 7,000 km/yr car are nowhere near worn, but the discs corrode from disuse in Taiwan's humidity and get replaced for rust, not wear. The 50,000 risk provision covers the two Model X-specific out-of-warranty failures — 智慧型空氣懸吊 confirmed standard front AND rear on U-CAR's spec sheet (struts roughly NT$50,000-80,000 per corner at Tesla), and falcon-wing door actuators/sensors. Probability-weighted provision, not a certainty. Fully outside basic warranty; battery/drive cover has not yet lapsed. Trimmed from 112,000 after re-cadencing the brake fluid to Tesla's 4-year interval (year 4 falls in the previous window, year 8 in the next).

major_items: ALL warranty gone from year 8 — battery + drive unit cover expires on the 8-year clock
SECOND TIRE SET, aged out again ~year 10 (~52,000) + alignment (~3,000)
Air-suspension strut replacement, 1-2 corners typical at this age (~90,000)
Falcon-wing door actuator / sensor repair — known Model X item (~55,000)
Brake pads + discs replacement (~35,000)
Low-voltage Li-ion battery replacement ~year 9 (~15,000)
Cabin HEPA filter at year 9 (~8,000), brake fluid at year 8 (~4,000), coolant (~8,000)
Misc: control arms, bushings, A/C compressor risk, MCU (~30,000)
checkpoints.source: The expensive window, and the reason a BEV's 10-year maintenance must not be modelled as flat. Two things collide: the 8-year battery/drive warranty lapses (at 7,000 km/yr the 240,000 km cap is irrelevant — only the year cap bites), and Model X's two structural weak points come due. Air suspension is confirmed standard front and rear on U-CAR's official spec sheet, so it is not a hypothetical option. The second tire set is again an AGE replacement at only ~70,000 km cumulative. Note what is still absent versus a combustion car: no oil, no plugs, no timing components, no gearbox rebuild. Trimmed from 312,000 to 300,000 on the HEPA re-cadence (years 3/6/9 gives one filter in this window, not two). 10-year total ~NT$501,000. Estimated levels, not a fetched Tesla price list — hence low confidence on magnitude, though the shape is solid.
